operations.name: join
operations.description:
Registers a new member user account with credentials. This operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_citizen table using provided email and password fields. The operation generates a new authentication session and issues initial access and refresh tokens. This endpoint supports the registration of members, allowing them to create persistent accounts with full platform privileges.

The operation requires the email and password fields which must be defined in the request body according to the discussion_board_citizen schema. The password field is expected to follow platform password policies. The email field must be unique within the discussion_board_citizen table.

The authentication system enforces secure password storage through hashing before persisting to the database. Upon successful registration, the system creates a new record in discussion_board_citizen_sessions to establish the initial session state.

This registration operation is available to any unauthenticated user and is the first step for members to gain full platform access with posting, commenting, and uploading privileges.

requestBody.description: Registration information for creating a new member account.

responseBody.description: Successfully registered member credentials with issued JWT tokens.

operations.name: login
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing member user with provided credentials and returns valid JWT tokens. This operation validates the user's email and password against the discussion_board_citizen table records.

The login process checks for the existence of a member with matching email and verifies the hashed password against the stored value in the discussion_board_citizen table. Upon successful validation, it creates a new authentication session entry in discussion_board_citizen_sessions and issues fresh access and refresh tokens.

User authentication is session-based and follows standard JWT patterns. The operation uses the email field from the request body to look up the member record and password field to verify authentication. No additional system checks are required beyond database validation.

This operation returns user-specific tokens upon successful authentication and is available to any unauthenticated user attempting to establish a session with the platform.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for member authentication.

responseBody.description: Authenticated member session with issued JWT tokens.

operations.name: refresh
operations.description:
Renews an expired access token by validating the refresh token and issuing new tokens. This operation verifies the provided refresh token against active sessions stored in the discussion_board_citizen_sessions table.

The refresh operation checks the validity of the refresh token, its expiration timestamp, and associated member record existence. It validates that the session remains active and has not been revoked. Upon successful verification, it creates a new access token, refresh token, and renews the session duration in discussion_board_citizen_sessions.

The refresh mechanism enhances security by allowing token rotation without requiring users to re-enter credentials. This operation is specifically designed for authenticated member users who possess a current refresh token.

The system enforces rate-limiting on refresh attempts to prevent abuse and maintains strict expiration policies to minimize token exposure risk.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for renewing access credentials.

responseBody.description: New access and refresh tokens generated from valid refresh token.

operations.name: status
operations.description:
Retrieves the current authentication status of the member user. This operation checks if the member has an active session and verifies the validity of their access token without requiring re-authentication.

The status endpoint queries the discussion_board_citizen_sessions table to validate the member's current session token. It returns the active status, token expiration time, and associated account information without exposing sensitive credentials.

This operation is essential for client-side applications to determine authentication state and manage UI state (e.g., showing logged-in vs logged-out interfaces). It allows for seamless user experience by avoiding unnecessary redirects or re-login prompts during active sessions.

The operation requires no request body and is designed to be called frequently by client applications to maintain session awareness. It operates under the member authorization actor to ensure only authenticated members can check their own status.

responseBody.description: Current authentication status and session metadata for the member.

operations.description:
Registers a new admin account in the discussion board system. This operation creates a new admin entity in the discussion_board_moderator table with initial authentication credentials.

The operation requires a valid email address to be provided in the request body, which will be verified against the discussion_board_users table to ensure uniqueness. The password field will be hashed using bcrypt before storage in the discussion_board_moderator table. The admin's account will be initialized with default permissions for content moderation and user reporting.

This operation is distinct from user registration (join for citizen actors) and is specifically designed for system administrators who require elevated privileges to manage content, review reports, and suspend users. The admin account creation process includes additional background verification steps that are not available to regular citizens.

All admin accounts created through this endpoint will have immediate access to moderation tools within the system. The registration process enforces strong password policies and requires email verification before the account can be fully activated.

requestBody.description: Request body containing admin registration information. Defines the required fields for creating a new admin account, including email address and password. The email field references the discussion_board_users table for unique verification, and the password field must meet the system's strength requirements.

responseBody.description: Response body containing the issued JWT access and refresh tokens for the newly created admin account. Includes the admin's unique identifier, email address, and token expiration information. This structure follows the IAuthorized pattern for authentication responses and enables immediate API access upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates an admin user by validating their credentials against the discussion_board_moderator table. This operation verifies the provided email address and password against stored values in the admin account database record.

The system validates the password by comparing the hashed value stored in discussion_board_moderator.password against the provided plaintext password using bcrypt comparison. Upon successful authentication, a JWT access token and refresh token are generated. The access token has a short expiration time (typically 15 minutes) to enhance security, while the refresh token has a longer lifespan (typically 7 days) and is stored in an encrypted form in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table linked to the admin's account.

This operation is only available to admins whose accounts are in active status (discussion_board_moderator.status = 'active'). Accounts marked as suspended, banned, or deleted cannot authenticate through this endpoint. The system also enforces rate limiting on authentication attempts to prevent brute force attacks, leveraging the discussion_board_authentication_logs table to track and block suspicious activity.

Successful login responses include the admin's unique identifier and role, enabling the API to properly authorize subsequent requests based on admin privileges. This operation does not require prior authentication and is publicly accessible for the purpose of user authentication.

requestBody.description: Request body containing admin authentication credentials. Includes the email address and password required to authenticate an admin user. The email address is matched against the discussion_board_users table to identify the corresponding admin record, and the password is validated against the hashed value in the discussion_board_moderator table.

responseBody.description: Response body containing the issued JWT access and refresh tokens for the authenticated admin. Includes the admin's unique identifier, email address, and token expiration information. This structure follows the IAuthorized pattern for authentication responses and enables immediate API access upon successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Renews the access token for an authenticated admin using a valid refresh token. This operation verifies the provided refresh token against the encrypted tokens stored in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table and issues a new access token with an extended expiration period.

The refresh token must be currently valid and not expired. The system checks the refresh token's integrity and confirms it corresponds to an active admin account in discussion_board_moderator table. The refresh operation reuses the same admin account to maintain the authentication context without requiring re-entry of credentials.

This operation enhances security by allowing frequent refresh of short-lived access tokens while requiring infrequent re-authentication with credentials. The refresh token cannot be used to generate additional refresh tokens, and each refresh operation invalidates the previous refresh token in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table to prevent replay attacks.

The response includes a new access token and a new refresh token, ensuring session continuity while maintaining security through token rotation. This operation is only available to admins who have previously completed a successful login operation and whose access token has expired or is nearing expiration.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the refresh token used to renew the admin's access token. The refresh token must be one that was previously issued during a successful login operation and is still valid in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table.

responseBody.description: Response body containing the newly issued JWT access and refresh tokens for the admin account. Includes the admin's unique identifier, email address, and token expiration information after the refresh operation. This structure follows the IAuthorized pattern and ensures continuous authenticated access to protected API endpoints.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Allows an authenticated admin to modify the status of an article in the discussion_board_articles table. Admins can set articles to 'published', 'hidden' or 'deleted' status, bypassing regular publication workflows. The operation reads the article's current status from discussion_board_article_status_logs and updates it within the discussion_board_articles table using the admin's authorized identity. All actions are logged in discussion_board_moderation_actions for audit purposes.

This admin privilege is essential for content moderation - allowing quick removal of inappropriate content or immediate publication of time-sensitive material. The request includes the article UUID and target state, ensuring precise control. The operation is only available to users authenticated as admin.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: UUID identifier of the article to modify status for as referenced in discussion_board_articles table.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the target status value for the article. Must be one of: 'published', 'hidden', or 'deleted' per discussion_board_article_statuses enumeration.

responseBody.description: Response body confirmed the successful status update including the new article status and timestamp of modification as stored in discussion_board_article_status_logs.

operations.name: updateArticleStatus

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific system configuration setting from the discussion board's configuration system. This operation fetches the current value of a named configuration parameter based on its unique key identifier.

The configuration values are stored in the discussion_board_configurations database table and represent system-wide settings that may be modified without code deployment. Each configuration key acts as a unique identifier for a specific setting, enabling dynamic configuration management across the platform.

This API operation serves as the primary interface for retrieving configuration values used by various components of the system, including content moderation rules, user experience preferences, and platform behavior controls. The configuration system allows administrators to adjust platform parameters through administrative interfaces without requiring code deployments or system restarts.

The retrieved configuration value is returned in a format compatible with its expected usage context, which may include boolean flags, numeric thresholds, string values, or JSON-encoded configuration objects. Requesting a configuration key that does not exist will return a 404 Not Found response.

Changes to configuration values are direct and immediate updates to the record in the database. There is no soft delete behavior or historical versioning. The current value is always the latest value stored in the database.

This operation is often used in conjunction with PATCH /configurations/{configKey} for configuration updates and in support of system components that need to dynamically adapt their behavior based on current platform settings. Related operations: Update configuration (PATCH /configurations/{configKey}).

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique system identifier for the configuration setting to retrieve. This corresponds to the 'key' field in the discussion_board_configurations database table and is used to look up the specific configuration value. The configuration key is a case-sensitive string that uniquely identifies the setting within the system.

responseBody.description: The configuration value corresponding to the requested key. This represents the current value assigned to the configuration setting in the discussion_board_configurations table. The value may be a string, number, boolean, or JSON object depending on the configuration type.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieve system configuration parameters for the discussion board platform. This operation operates on the discussion_board_configurations table from the database schema and provides access to critical system settings that govern platform behavior, content moderation policies, user experience parameters, and operational constraints.

The configuration includes all platform-wide settings that determine how the discussion board functions, including content visibility rules, attachment limits, posting frequency restrictions, moderation thresholds, and operational performance parameters. This endpoint is essential for clients that need to customize their interface behavior according to platform rules or for administrators who need to verify current system configurations.

Security considerations involve ensuring only authorized actors can access sensitive configuration data. While basic configuration parameters may be publicly accessible for frontend compatibility, sensitive settings related to moderation thresholds, authentication limits, and internal system parameters are restricted to administrative access. The response includes configuration values that may change dynamically based on platform updates or administrative modifications.

This operation does not modify any configuration values - it is strictly read-only. Modifications to configuration must be handled through administrative interfaces with appropriate authorization levels. The configuration data is cached for performance optimization but may be refreshed automatically when administrative changes are made. Related operations: None - this read-only configuration endpoint is not linked to any update operations as configuration changes follow a separate administrative workflow.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and filtering parameters for configuration retrieval

responseBody.description: Current system configuration values with all applicable parameters

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Update a specific configuration setting for the discussion board system. This operation modifies the system configuration identified by the configKey parameter, which represents a unique configuration key in the discussion_board_configurations table. The update applies to live system settings affecting platform behavior, user experience, or operational parameters.

The configuration system stores key-value pairs that control platform functionality, including moderation rules, content display preferences, system limits, and feature toggles. This endpoint allows authorized administrators to modify these runtime settings without requiring a system restart.

Security note: Modifying system configurations can significantly impact platform behavior. This operation requires admin privileges as the configuration changes affect all users and system operations. Only users with 'admin' role can modify configuration values, as these changes can potentially disrupt service, alter user experience, or create security vulnerabilities.

Operational considerations: The configuration update must be validated before application to ensure the new value is syntactically and semantically correct for the particular configuration key. Configuration values may include JSON strings, boolean flags, numeric limits, or string-based settings depending on the configuration type. The system must maintain atomicity of the update operation to prevent partial configuration changes.

Configuration management best practices: Changes to configuration settings should be documented, reviewed, and tested before deployment to production. This operation provides an API interface for configuration management but should be used judiciously in production environments.

Related operations: To retrieve the current configuration, use GET /configurations/{configKey}. To list all available configurations in the system, use GET /configurations.
operations.name: update

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the configuration setting to be updated. This key corresponds directly to the 'key' field in the discussion_board_configurations table and must match exactly with an existing configuration record in the system. The configuration key is a string value that uniquely identifies each configuration setting, such as 'max_comments_per_post', 'enable_signups', or 'content_moderation_level'. This must be provided in the URL path as a path parameter.

requestBody.description: The new configuration value and metadata to be applied to the target configuration setting. This request body contains the updated configuration data with the value field representing the actual configuration value to be stored. The new value is stored directly in the value field of the discussion_board_configurations table. The configuration key is provided as a path parameter, so it should not be included in the request body.

responseBody.description: The updated configuration object with its new value and metadata after successful update. The response includes the complete configuration record with all fields after the update operation has been successfully completed, including the updated value field, last_modified timestamp, and metadata fields.

prerequisites.description: Configuration must be created before it can be updated

operations.description:
Create a new discussion board configuration record in the system. This operation allows administrators to define platform-specific settings, including moderation policies, content filtering rules, and system behavior parameters. The configuration record is stored in the discussion_board_configurations table and applies globally across the entire platform.

The operation validates that all configuration values comply with established constraints and business rules, including maximum values for posting limits and minimum thresholds for trust scores. Each configuration setting is validated against schema-defined constraints to ensure system stability and prevent malicious or erroneous configurations.

Security: This operation is restricted to administrators only due to the sensitive nature of system-wide configuration changes. No other user roles can modify these settings.

The configuration record includes fields like postPerDayLimit, attachmentFileSizeLimit, and trustScoreThreshold, all of which are tightly controlled to maintain platform quality and prevent abuse while preserving user experience.

The created configuration becomes active immediately upon creation and governs platform behavior for all users until modified by another admin. Related operations: View configuration (GET /configurations), Update configuration (PUT /configurations).
operations.name: create

requestBody.description: Configuration data for setting platform-wide behavior parameters

responseBody.description: The created configuration record with all defined fields

operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific configuration setting from the discussion board system. This operation directly targets the discussion_board_configurations table in the database and removes the record identified by the configKey parameter. This is a hard delete operation that immediately and permanently eliminates the configuration entry from the system storage, with no possibility of recovery.

The configKey parameter must exactly match an existing configuration key in the database. If the key does not exist, the operation will return a 404 error. This operation does not soft-delete records; it performs a complete deletion as specified by the system architecture.

This action is irreversible and should only be used when a configuration is confirmed to be obsolete, corrupt, or otherwise invalid. After deletion, any service or component dependent on this configuration will revert to its default behavior.

Security: This operation is restricted to administrative users only, as misconfiguration can impact system behavior. No user-facing actors can perform this deletion, ensuring system stability and preventing accidental removal of critical settings.
operations.name: erase

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique identifier key of the configuration setting to be removed (global scope)

prerequisites.description: Configuration must be created before it can be deleted. The DELETE operation requires an existing configuration key to remove, and the only way to create a configuration is through POST /discussionBoard/configurations.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific discussion board channel by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches detailed information about a single channel from the discussion_board_channels table, including its name, description, creation timestamp, and moderation status. The channel identifier is provided in the path parameter as channelId.

The channel data returned includes essential metadata for displaying the channel to users and for selecting appropriate content filters. Community channels with a published status can be accessed by registered citizens. Pending or hidden channels are not visible to regular users.

Security: Only authenticated citizens can retrieve channel details. The system checks the user's authentication token against the channel's access control policy. Rate limiting is applied to prevent automated enumeration of channel identifiers.

This operation is used by the frontend application to load channel information when navigating to a specific channel page. The operation is paired with POST /channels for creating new channels and DELETE /channels/{channelId} for removing channels.

Related operations: POST /channels (create new channel), PATCH /channels (list/search channels), DELETE /channels/{channelId} (delete channel).
operations.name: at

parameters.name: channelId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target channel (system-generated UUID)

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the requested channel including name, description, and status

prerequisites.description: Channel must be created by a moderator before it can be retrieved by a citizen

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of discussion board channels. This operation operates on the discussion_board_channels table from the database schema and provides advanced search capabilities for finding channels based on multiple criteria including name, description, category, and active status.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Channels can be sorted by name, creation date, or member count in ascending or descending order. Search filters allow matching partial names, descriptions, and category identifiers.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of private channels based on user authentication. Public channels are accessible to all users, while private channels require appropriate permissions.

This operation integrates with the discussion_board_channels table as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available channel fields and relationships. The response includes channel summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional details based on authorization level.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for channel filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of channel summary information matching search criteria

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Channel must be created by an administrator before it can be queried via the search API

operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board channel with new configuration settings, name, description, or visibility status. This operation modifies the discussion_board_channels table directly, which stores the core metadata of each channel including its public visibility, moderation policies, title, and description. Changes are restricted to users with moderator privileges.

The operation validates that the target channel exists and is active. All fields provided in the request body are merged with existing channel data; omitted fields retain their current values. The channel's createdByUserId, createdAt, and channelCode fields cannot be modified. Modifying the channel's visibility status or moderation policy triggers automatic cache invalidation and updates to channel listing views across the platform.

Security and privilege checks are enforced: Only actors with moderator role can invoke this operation. The system correlates the authenticated user's ID with the moderator list to verify authorization. No other actors can perform this update, even if they created the channel.

Related operations:
- GET /channels/{channelId}: Retrieve current channel details before modification.
- PATCH /channels: Search or list channels with filters for an overview.
- DELETE /channels/{channelId}: Permanently remove a channel (requires elevated permissions).

Error handling: If the channel does not exist or has been soft-deleted, a 404 Not Found error is returned. If the request contains invalid data (e.g., empty title or malformed description), a 400 Bad Request error is returned with a detailed validation message.

parameters.name: channelId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target channel (channelCode) in snake_case format as defined in the database schema. This is a string-based system-assigned code guaranteed to be unique across the entire platform (global scope).

requestBody.description: Properties to update on the target channel. Only provided fields are modified; omitted fields retain their current value. Do not include readOnly fields like id, createdByUserId, createdAt, or channelCode.

responseBody.description: The updated channel entity with all its current properties after the modification has been applied. Includes system-managed fields such as updatedAt and version which reflect the modification.

operations.name: update

operations.description:
Create a new discussion channel for organizing content and conversations on the board.

This operation allows moderators and administrators to establish new discussion channels that serve as containers for related articles and user interactions. Each channel represents a thematic or organizational grouping within the discussion platform, enabling users to navigate and contribute to specific topics of interest.

The creation process requires the channel name, description, and visibility settings. Channels are automatically assigned unique identifiers and are immediately available for users to access. This operation is governed by access controls established in the discussion_board_channels model, ensuring that only authorized actors can create new channels.

Security: Only users with moderator or admin privileges can create new channels. The operation validates that the channel name is unique and meets minimum length requirements. Channel creation triggers a system event logged in the discussion_board_audit_events table for audit trail purposes.

Related operations: List channels (GET /channels), Get channel details (GET /channels/{channelId}), Update channel (PUT /channels/{channelId}), Erase channel (DELETE /channels/{channelId}).

requestBody.description: Configuration details and metadata for creating a new discussion channel

responseBody.description: The newly created discussion channel with system-assigned identifiers and metadata

operations.name: create

operations.description:
Permanently remove a discussion board channel and all its associated content. This operation permanently deletes the channel entity from the discussion_board_channels table and is irreversible. All related content including articles, comments, and attachments within this channel are also permanently deleted.

This is a hard delete operation that removes data from the database entirely, not a soft delete. The channel cannot be recovered after deletion. This operation does not preserve any historical records or archived copies of the channel data.

Due to the irreversible nature of this operation, it requires administrative privileges. Only users with moderator or admin roles can execute this deletion. The system does not maintain any soft-delete backup or recovery mechanism for deleted channels. This design ensures data integrity and prevents accidental retention of obsolete content.

Related operations: Get channel details (GET /channels/{channelId}), List channels (GET /channels), Update channel (PUT /channels/{channelId}).
operations.name: erase

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target channel to be permanently deleted.
parameters.name: channelId

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific attachment by its unique identifier from the discussion board system. This operation operates on the discussion_board_attachments table and returns detailed metadata about the requested attachment, including its file name, size, MIME type, upload timestamp, and associated content reference.

The attachmentId parameter must match the unique identifier of an existing attachment record in the database. This endpoint is designed for file retrieval and serves as a gateway to the stored attachment content. The file data itself is not returned directly in the response body but is accessible via a secure, time-limited URI as specified in the response schema.

Security: This endpoint implements an authorship validation check where the requesting user's authentication token is matched against the attachment's original uploader. Only authenticated users who have permission to view the associated content can access the attachment. Public attachments may be made available for anonymous access based on the content's publication status and visibility rules.

Error handling: Returns 404 Not Found if the attachmentId does not exist, 403 Forbidden if the user lacks permissions to access the attachment, or 500 Internal Server Error if there is a system issue retrieving the file. The attachment remains accessible through this endpoint for its lifetime or until explicitly removed by moderation unless it's part of archived or deleted content.
operations.name: at

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target attachment (global scope)
parameters.name: attachmentId

responseBody.description: Detailed metadata about the requested attachment with secure access URI for content retrieval

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of attachment records from the discussion board system. This operation operates on the discussion_board_attachments table and provides advanced search capabilities for finding attachments based on file type, size range, upload date intervals, associated content ID, and ownership context (article, comment, or user).

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Attachments can be sorted by creation date, file size, or filename in ascending or descending order. The search functionality enables filtering by exact file extension (e.g., .jpg, .pdf), size range (min/max bytes), and date ranges (created_after, created_before). Additionally, users can filter by the parent content type (article, comment, post) and specific parent IDs to retrieve attachments linked to particular content.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive attachment information based on the requesting user's authorization level. Only users with appropriate permissions can access detailed attachment information or retrieve attachments for private content. The operation respects content visibility rules - attachments linked to published content are accessible to users with appropriate view permissions, while attachments linked to unpublished or hidden content are restricted accordingly.

This operation integrates with the discussion_board_attachments table as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available fields and relationships to discussion_board_attachment_images and discussion_board_attachment_files. The response includes attachment summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional metadata based on authorization level.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for attachment filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of attachment summary information matching search criteria

operations.description:
Update an existing attachment in the discussion board system. This operation modifies the metadata and content reference for an attachment identified by its unique ID. The operation operates on the discussion_board_attachments table and is accessible to both citizens (regular users who created the attachment) and moderators (who can manage any attachment).

The attachment entity supports file uploads and image uploads through attachments. When an attachment is updated, system must validate that the user has permission to modify the attachment (ownership check for citizens, elevated permissions for moderators). The object_id field in the attachment must reference a valid entity in the system, such as an article or comment, and the attachment_type must be one of the permitted types specified in the schema.

Users can update attachment metadata to correct errors, change descriptions, or adjust permissions, but cannot change the underlying file content itself - file uploads require new attachment creation. This protects file integrity and prevents content manipulation. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time. Related operations: GET /attachments/{attachmentId} to retrieve attachment details, DELETE /attachments/{attachmentId} to remove the attachment from the system.

This operation is critical for user experience as it allows users to maintain the accuracy of their content submissions and allows moderators to correct unauthorized or inaccurate metadata. The system ensures that updates do not disrupt existing references to the attachment by maintaining the attachment's unique ID across updates.
operations.name: update

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target attachment

requestBody.description: Update parameters for the attachment including description and object_id

responseBody.description: Updated attachment object with new metadata and timestamps

Update an existing attachment in the discussion board system. This operation modifies the attachment metadata including file location (file_url), file type (content_type), file size (file_size), and description. The operation operates on the discussion_board_attachments table and is accessible to both citizens (regular users who created the attachment) and moderators (who can manage any attachment).

The attachment entity supports file uploads and image uploads through attachments. When an attachment is updated, the system validates that the user has permission to modify the attachment (ownership check for citizens, elevated permissions for moderators). The object_id field in the attachment must reference a valid entity in the system, such as an article or comment. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time. Related operations: GET /attachments/{attachmentId} to retrieve attachment details, DELETE /attachments/{attachmentId} to remove the attachment from the system.

This operation is critical for user experience as it allows users to maintain the accuracy of their content submissions and allows moderators to correct unauthorized or inaccurate metadata. The system ensures that updates do not disrupt existing references to the attachment by maintaining the attachment's unique ID across updates.

operations.description:
Create a new attachment for discussion board content. This operation allows authenticated citizens to upload files and images associated with posts, articles, or comments. The system supports attachment of various file types including images, documents, and other media as permitted by platform policies.

The operation interacts with the discussion_board_attachments database table and requires a valid citizen authentication token to be presented. The attachment is associated with a specific content item or post ID provided in the request body, enabling proper content-linking and retrieval. The system validates file size, type, and integrity before storage, and generates secure URLs for subsequent access.

Policies and restrictions enforced include maximum file size limits (20MB), allowed file extensions (jpg, jpeg, png, gif, pdf, doc, docx, zip), and content moderation scanning upon upload. The attachment record includes metadata such as original filename, MIME type, file size, upload timestamp, and storage location.

Related operations: GET /attachments/{attachmentId} to retrieve attachment details, DELETE /attachments/{attachmentId} to remove an attachment, and PATCH /attachments to list attachments associated with a specific content item.

Storage is managed through a cloud-based object storage service with automatic thumbnail generation for images and content delivery network (CDN) serving for optimal performance.
operations.name: create

requestBody.description: Upload data and metadata for a new attachment including the file content and associated content reference.

responseBody.description: Created attachment record with database-generated identifiers and secure access URLs.

prerequisites.description: Article must be created before an attachment can be associated with it, as the content_id field references an existing article record.

operations.description:
Permanently removes an attachment from the system by its unique identifier. This operation deletes the attachment record from the discussion_board_attachment_images or discussion_board_attachment_files table, depending on the attachment type. The operation is irreversible and all associated file metadata is permanently destroyed. This endpoint is designed to handle file cleanup after content deletion or user request for data removal.

Security: Only authenticated users with appropriate permissions can delete attachments. The system verifies ownership by cross-referencing the attachment's creator ID with the authenticated user's ID. If the attachment was created by a citizen, only that citizen or a moderator can delete it. Moderator deletion requires no ownership verification.

System behavior: This operation performs a hard delete, completely removing the record from the database and marking the referenced file storage for cleanup by the system's garbage collection process. The operation does not maintain any trace of the deleted file in the system, except for audit logs that record the deletion event.

Related operations: This operation is typically called after DELETE /posts/{postId} or DELETE /comments/{commentId} to clean up attached media files. It's also used when users request the removal of their own content under privacy regulations.

Implementation: The implementation first validates the attachment ID exists, then checks ownership permissions, then deletes from the appropriate attachment table (discussion_board_attachment_images or discussion_board_attachment_files), and finally logs the deletion in the discussion_board_audit_events table.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target attachment. This is a UUID that references either discussion_board_attachment_images or discussion_board_attachment_files table.

operations.name: erase

operations.description:
Permanently removes an attachment from the system by its unique identifier. This operation deletes the attachment record from the discussion_board_attachment_images or discussion_board_attachment_files table, depending on the attachment type. The operation is irreversible and all associated file metadata is permanently destroyed. This endpoint is designed to handle file cleanup after content deletion or user request for data removal.

Security: Only authenticated users with appropriate permissions can delete attachments. The system verifies ownership by cross-referencing the attachment's creator ID with the authenticated user's ID. If the attachment was created by a citizen, only that citizen or a moderator can delete it. Moderator deletion requires no ownership verification.

System behavior: This operation performs a hard delete, completely removing the record from the database and marking the referenced file storage for cleanup by the system's garbage collection process. The operation does not maintain any trace of the deleted file in the system, except for audit logs that record the deletion event.

Related operations: This operation is typically called after DELETE /posts/{postId} or DELETE /comments/{commentId} to clean up attached media files. It's also used when users request the removal of their own content under privacy regulations.

Implementation: The implementation first validates the attachment ID exists, then checks ownership permissions, then deletes from the appropriate attachment table (discussion_board_attachment_images or discussion_board_attachment_files), and finally logs the deletion in the discussion_board_audit_events table.

This is used exclusively by moderator actors for auditing purposes and maintaining accountability in moderation workflows.

Security: Access is restricted to moderator actors only, as these logs contain sensitive information about user actions and moderation decisions. The operation ensures confidentiality and integrity of moderation records by preventing unauthorized access. Log entries are immutable and cannot be modified after creation through this API.

Implementation: The operation performs a direct lookup on the discussion_board_moderation_logs table using the provided logId as the primary key. The response includes all fields stored in the database table for this log entry. This endpoint is read-only and does not support any modifications to the data. Related operations: GET /moderation-logs with pagination for auditing multiple entries.

Discriminator Note: The system retains these logs as non-soft-deleted records to ensure regulatory compliance and auditability. There is no deletion capability for these records, even for system administrators, to maintain a complete and unalterable audit trail.

Each log entry includes the acting moderator, the action taken, the affected content or user, timestamps, and the reason for the action.

Security: This endpoint is restricted to moderator role actors only, as it provides sensitive audit information about platform governance and content moderation decisions. Standard citizens cannot access this data to prevent potential abuse of moderation system information. The operation integrates with the discussion_board_moderator_actions table, which records all moderation events, and the discussion_board_moderation_audit_trails table, which preserves complete original content metadata for compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

It does not map to a single entity but synthesizes information from various moderation systems for comprehensive oversight. Update operations are restricted to modify only certain fields like additional_notes, status, or resolution_details, while critical audit fields like action_type, target_id, actor_id, and timestamp remain immutable to maintain integrity of the audit trail.

This operation fetches an individual authentication log record from the discussion_board_authentication_logs table in the database. Each log entry records a user authentication event including timestamps, IP addresses, user agent information, and authentication outcomes. This provides critical security auditing capability for suspicious login attempts or unauthorized access patterns.

Authentication logs are system-generated audit records that are automatically created whenever a user attempts to authenticate, regardless of success or failure. These records are essential for security monitoring, compliance reporting, and forensic analysis following suspected security incidents. The data includes details such as authentication method (email/password, session token), client device information, geographical location based on IP address, and the result of the authentication attempt.

Access to these logs is strictly controlled and restricted to administrative users only. The operation implements a zero-trust model where even authenticated users cannot access log data unless explicitly granted administrative permissions. This ensures the confidentiality and integrity of security audit information.

This operation is read-only and does not modify any system state. It complements other security operations such as user management and account suspension by providing the audit trail context needed to make informed decisions about user access and platform security.

Related operations: List authentication logs (PATCH /authentication-logs), Manage moderator actions (POST /moderation-actions).

All registration attempts are logged for audit purposes in the discussion_board_authentication_logs table, ensuring compliance with security and regulatory standards. This enables tracking of registration attempts, IP addresses, and timestamps for security monitoring and abuse prevention.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent automated registration abuse and mandatory validation of email format. Only one account per unique email address is permitted, preventing duplicate registrations. New users begin with a default trust score of zero, which increases as they contribute positive content and interactions that are approved by the moderation system.

Subsequent operations rely on a successful registration, as authentication tokens generated during this operation are required for accessing protected resources such as posting articles, commenting, and uploading files. This makes user registration the foundational operation for all citizen activity on the platform.

The operation returns the complete archived article including all metadata, publication history, and associated audit trail information.

Related Objects: The response references the original discussion_board_articles table record via the article_id foreign key, which links to the archived version. The author information is retrieved from the discussion_board_citizen table to maintain author attribution.

Archived content is designated as read-only; no update or deletion operations are allowed on archived articles. This operation is part of the platform's legal compliance system to maintain immutable records of user-generated content for regulatory and dispute resolution purposes.

operations.description:
Retrieve archived discussion board articles and their associated content metadata filtered by search criteria and pagination parameters.

This operation operates on the discussion_board_archives table which stores permanently preserved copies of articles and related data following moderation actions or user-initiated archival. Unlike the main discussion_board_articles table, archived records are immutable and retain the exact state of the content at the time of archiving, including title, content, authorship, attachment references, and moderation metadata.

This endpoint enables users and moderators to search archived content using keyword queries against the article title, article content, and attached filenames. The search functionality supports substring matching and returns results sorted by archival timestamp in descending order, with full pagination controls including page size and offset. Archived content is returned in summary form without full content to optimize performance, since archived records are primarily intended for audit, compliance, and historical review rather than active discussion.

Security and authorization: This operation is restricted to moderator actors only, as archived content contains sensitive historical records that may include moderation decisions and redacted content. The archived records serve as an immutable audit trail and may contain sensitive personal information or policy-violating material that is not intended for public access. Citizen actors cannot access archived content under any circumstances, as the primary purpose of archiving is to preserve a secure record of content removed from public visibility.

Related operations: This search functionality complements the active article search on /articles, with the critical distinction that archived results include content that has been permanently removed from active feeds. The response format follows the IPageIDiscussionBoardArchive.ISummary structure to provide only essential metadata without bloating the response with full content text or attachment files, adhering to the performance and security requirements of historical record retrieval.

requestBody.description: Search parameters and pagination controls for querying archived article records

responseBody.description: Paginated list of summary metadata for archived articles matching search criteria

operations.description:
Update an archived discussion board article that has been moved to the archive. This operation permits moderators to modify the content or metadata of archived articles while maintaining their archived status. The operation is performed on the discussion_board_archives table which stores historical copies of previously published articles.

Archived articles are immutable copies of articles that have been removed from public view, typically due to moderation actions, policy violations, or content updates. This endpoint allows authorized moderators to update the archive record itself - for example, to add a moderation note explaining why the article was archived, update the reason code, change the archive timestamp, or correct metadata. Importantly, this is not a restoration operation - the article remains archived and the original article record is not modified.

Security is enforced through the moderator actor, ensuring only users with elevated privileges can alter archive records. Archive records contain sensitive information about moderation decisions, making strict access control critical. The archive ID is required and must match an existing archived article.

The update operation preserves all original archival metadata to maintain audit integrity while allowing necessary corrections. This operation does not restore the article to the public forum. To restore content, the operation must proceed through the appropriate restoration workflow.

This operation interfaces with related components: discussion_board_article_status_logs to confirm the original status change, discussion_board_moderation_actions to verify the moderator's authority, and discussion_board_archive_logs to maintain a complete audit trail of all modifications to the archive entry.

operations.description:
Create a new archived item in the discussion board system. This operation is designed for the discussion_board_archives table and allows moderators and administrators to permanently store content that has been removed from public view for compliance, legal, or archival purposes.

When content is removed through moderation actions (such as deletion or hiding), this operation creates a permanent archive entry that preserves the original content, metadata, and moderation context. The archived item cannot be retrieved by regular users, but it remains accessible to authorized personnel for audit, legal discovery, or compliance reporting.

The operation requires explicit authorization for moderators or administrators, as it involves handling potentially sensitive content. Archived data includes the original post/comment content, author information, removal reason, moderator ID, and timestamp of the archival action. This ensures full traceability for regulatory compliance.

Security: Only users with moderator or admin privileges can create archives. The operation validates that the target content exists in the moderation system and was properly flagged for removal. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of the archival system.

This operation is part of the content moderation pipeline and complements the discussion_board_moderation_actions, discussion_board_moderation_audit_trails, and discussion_board_compliance_records tables.

Archived items are not subject to normal data retention policies and may be preserved indefinitely for legal requirements.

Related operations: POST /moderate (initiates the moderation process), PATCH /moderation/actions (retrieves moderation history), and GET /compliance/records (retrieves legal compliance audit trails).

requestBody.description: Data required to create an archival record for removed content

responseBody.description: Confirmation of the successfully created archival record

operations.description:
Permanently delete a discussion board archive entry from the system. This operation targets the discussion_board_archives table in the database and performs a hard delete, removing the archive record entirely with no possibility of recovery. This is a privileged operation available only to moderators.

The archive entry to be deleted is identified by its unique archiveId parameter, which corresponds to the primary key field in the database table. Prior to deletion, the system validates that the requesting user has moderator privileges. Once confirmed, the archive record is immediately and permanently removed from the database.

This operation has no request body and returns no response body, consistent with standard HTTP DELETE practices. The deletion is irreversible, meaning all associated archive data (including metadata and historical references) is permanently eliminated from the system. This operation does not use a soft delete pattern as the discussion_board_archives table has no soft_delete_column field in the schema.

Due to the permanent nature of this action, it is restricted to moderator actors only. Regular users cannot initiate archive deletions. This aligns with the business requirement that only authorized personnel should be able to remove archival content from the system.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific activity log entry from the discussion board system. This operation accesses the discussion_board_activity_logs table and returns comprehensive details about a single logged event, including the actor, action performed, target resource, timestamp, and contextual metadata.

This endpoint is designed to support both citizen users and moderators who require visibility into platform activities for auditing, troubleshooting, or user support purposes. The activity log contains records of all user-initiated actions and system events that impact content or user behavior on the platform. Each log entry is uniquely identified by a logId and contains immutable historical data.

The activity log includes comprehensive metadata such as the IP address from which the action originated, the user agent string for device identification, and the specific target resource identifier (e.g., article ID, comment ID, user ID) that was affected by the action. This granular detail enables precise forensic analysis of platform events.

Security considerations include token-based authentication validation prior to access and auditing of all retrieval attempts. The data returned by this endpoint is essential for maintaining platform integrity, investigating suspicious activity, and ensuring compliance with content moderation policies. This operation returns complete and unaltered historical records - activity logs serve as the definitive source for tracking user actions.

Related operations: The PATCH /activity-logs endpoint can be used to search a range of activity logs using filtering and pagination criteria. This GET /activity-logs/{logId} operation is the direct accessor for retrieving individual log entries identified by their unique identifier.

Retrieve paginated activity logs from the discussion board system. This operation reads from the discussion_board_activity_logs table and returns a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of system events including user actions, moderation decisions, and system status changes.

The operation supports comprehensive filtering by actor type (user, moderator, system), activity type (login, post, remove, warn, ban), date range, and target content. Results can be sorted by timestamp, actor name, or activity type in ascending or descending order. Pagination is fully supported with configurable page sizes and cursor-based navigation.

The system logs all activities for audit and compliance purposes, and this operation provides the interface for reviewing these records.

This operation is the primary interface for system administrators and moderators to monitor platform activity, investigate potential policy violations, and conduct compliance audits. It does not create, update, or delete logs - these are automatically generated by system processes.

Security and authorization: Only users with the "moderator" role can modify activity logs. The operation validates the user's authentication token against the moderator actor definition in the system. This prevents regular citizens from tampering with audit trails.

This operation does not delete or alter any existing system-generated data; it only allows moderated correction of the log record. Record history is preserved for audit purposes, as log entries are immutable records of system activity.

The operation maps directly to the discussion_board_activity_logs table, which is defined with a primary key of "id" and contains fields for action type, timestamp, actor, context, and metadata. The request body includes optional fields for the caption, object, details, and comment that populate the corresponding columns in the database.

The response returns the updated activity log entry with all fields, including the original ID and creation timestamp. This ensures the client receives the final state of the modified log entry, which may include updated metadata or a status flag indicating moderation review.

Direct API dependency: If an activity log is being corrected to reflect new data from a related activity (e.g., a user's report being resolved), this operation must be preceded by a retrieval of that related entity. For example, the report's status change should be known before updating the associated activity log.

operations.description:
Create a new activity log entry in the discussion board system. This operation captures user actions, system events, and moderation activities that contribute to the platform's audit trail and security monitoring. Each log entry records the action performed, the actor responsible, the affected resource, and the timestamp when the action occurred.

The system automatically generates activity logs for all user-initiated actions including content creation, comment posting, file uploads, moderation actions, and system events. These logs are essential for compliance, security auditing, and forensic analysis. When a user performs an action such as creating an article, posting a comment, uploading a file, or reporting content, the system automatically creates an associated activity log entry.

This operation is specifically designed for system-level operations and administrative tools that need to record manual interventions or system-generated events that aren't triggered by standard user interface actions. It is not used for normal user actions, which are automatically captured by the system.

Activity logs are immutable records that persist indefinitely for compliance purposes. They cannot be deleted or modified after creation. The system maintains a comprehensive historical record of all platform activities, including user actions, moderator decisions, security events, and system operations.

The activity log includes critical information components:
- actor_id: The user performing the action (citizen, moderator, or system)
- action_type: The type of activity performed (e.g., comment_created, article_published, report_submitted)
- target_type: The type of resource affected (article, comment, user, etc.)
- target_id: The ID of the affected resource
- description: A plain text description of the event
- metadata: JSON data containing additional context specific to the action type
- ip_address: The IP address from which the action originated
- user_agent: The browser or client information

For administrative use only, this endpoint allows authorized system administrators or automated processes to record custom audit events, compliance actions, or system maintenance activities that require documentation in the audit log. The system will automatically record the current timestamp and populate the IP address and user agent fields based on the request context.

requestBody.description: Creation data for a new activity log entry

responseBody.description: The successfully created activity log entry with system-generated fields

operations.description:
Permanently delete a specific activity log entry from the system. This operation removes the complete audit record associated with the given log ID from the discussion_board_activity_logs table in the database. This action is irreversible and removes all historical information about the tracked activity, including timestamp, actor, action type, target identifier, and context metadata.

This operation is intended for administrative cleanup of erroneous or sensitive log entries that must be completely removed from the audit trail. It is not used for routine log retention policies, which should be managed through automated archival and purging processes.

Security: Only users with the "moderator" actor role can execute this deletion. The system does not perform soft deletion on activity logs; this is a hard delete operation that removes records permanently from the database. This design choice ensures that administrators have complete control over the audit trail integrity, and no archived or hidden versions of deleted activity logs remain accessible.

Related operations: GET /activity_logs (to view log entries before deletion), GET /activity_logs/{logId} (to retrieve specific log details).

**No soft delete**: This operation performs a permanent deletion without marking records as deleted or moving them to an archive. The record is completely removed from the database.

The operation enforces fine-grained access controls based on user roles and permissions within the system. For security and privacy compliance, access to detailed status logs is restricted to system administrators and privileged audit personnel.

The log record includes critical audit information that supports platform reliability assurance and operational transparency. Status logs are immutable records that capture system behavior for forensic analysis and accountability purposes.

Retrieve a specific thumbnail image by its unique identifier from the discussion_board_thumbnails table. This operation allows users to access image assets associated with articles, comments, or other content on the discussion board platform. The thumbnail is referenced by its system-generated unique identifier and returned as a binary image resource with the appropriate content type.

The thumbnail entity is stored in the discussion_board_thumbnails table, which contains metadata about image assets including file path, size, MIME type, and upload timestamp. The thumbnailId parameter must correspond to the unique identifier of a thumbnail record.

Security and access control: This endpoint does not require authentication as thumbnails are typically public assets associated with published content. However, the system automatically validates that the requested thumbnail exists and is associated with visible content. Attempts to access non-existent or orphaned thumbnails return a 404 error.

Response format: The response returns the raw binary image data with content-type headers corresponding to the image format (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp). No JSON response body is returned; the response contains the actual image bytes directly.

Related operations: This endpoint typically follows POST operations that upload new thumbnails and is used in conjunction with GET operations that retrieve parent content objects containing thumbnail references.

operations.description:
Provides read-only access to automatically generated thumbnail metadata derived from image attachments associated with articles, enabling efficient display and navigation in the client interface.

Access is restricted to authenticated users who have permission to view the associated articles. Thumbnails of hidden or deleted articles are not returned. This operation does not support creation, modification, or deletion of thumbnails — they are generated automatically by the system upon successful upload of image files to articles.

The system generates thumbnails as optimized PNG representations of uploaded JPG, PNG, or GIF images, with dimensions scaled to 150px width. Metadata including MIME type, file size, original width/height, and upload timestamp are stored for querying and caching efficiency.

This endpoint supports advanced pagination with configurable page size and sorting by upload timestamp (default descending), file size, or original dimensions. Query parameters filter results by associated article IDs, content type, or file size threshold.

IMPORTANT: This is a read-only interface to system-generated derived content. Users cannot upload, modify, or delete thumbnails directly. All thumbnail data is tied to its parent article's visibility and permissions. 

Related operations: 
- `GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}` must be pre-executed to obtain possible article IDs for thumbnail lookup.
- `GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/image` retrieves the original uploaded image, while this endpoint returns only the generated thumbnail metadata and URL.

operations.description:
Update the profile and settings of a specific citizen account in the discussion board platform.

This operation allows an authenticated citizen to modify their own account information, including display name, bio, notification preferences, and privacy settings. The citizen's identity is automatically authenticated through the JWT token, ensuring that citizens can only update their own account. This is a fully validated PUT operation that requires the citizen to provide complete, up-to-date information.

Security considerations include strict ownership verification, where the system validates that the JWT token's subject ID exactly matches the citizenId path parameter. Suspended or banned citizens are prohibited from making updates, and the system enforces rate limiting on profile modification operations to prevent abuse or spam. The operation logs all updates to the citizen's account activity log for audit purposes.

This endpoint is only accessible if the provided citizenId matches the authenticated user's ID. Any attempt to update another citizen's profile through this endpoint will be rejected. Related operations include fetching citizen profile details (GET /citizens/{citizenId}) and listing citizens (PATCH /citizens)

When a citizen account is deleted, all associated data is also removed, including their articles, comments, and attachments. This ensures complete data removal in compliance with privacy regulations.

This is a hard delete operation - no soft delete flag is used, and no audit trail remains in the database for the deleted record. The citizen's email address and authentication credentials are permanently erased from the system.

The moderator role is managed as a permission layer atop citizen accounts, ensuring separation of concerns between identity (stored in discussion_board_citizen) and authorization (stored in discussion_board_moderator). When a moderator's privileges are updated, the change is applied immediately and does not affect the underlying user account data.

Security: This operation is restricted to users with the "moderator" actor role who are acting in an administrative capacity. Changes to moderator status should be audited to prevent privilege escalation attacks.

This operation does not delete or deactivate the underlying citizen account in any way. It only updates the moderator role assignment. There is no soft delete mechanism for moderator roles; removal of moderator status is permanent and complete.

Results are returned in paginated format with configurable page size, sorting by creation date, update date, or relevance score, and complete pagination metadata.

The operation leverages full-text search capabilities on the article's title and content fields to provide accurate keyword matching. Users can filter articles by their current status (draft, pending, published, hidden) and specify date ranges for creation or modification. Category filtering allows users to retrieve articles belonging to specific discussion channels.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and filtering of sensitive article data based on the requesting user's authorization level. Only published articles are accessible to non-administrative users, while administrators can view articles in all supported states (draft, pending, published, hidden). The operation does not expose private metadata such as internal IDs or audit logs.

This operation integrates with the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_article_statuses, discussion_board_channels, and discussion_board_citizen models as defined in the database schema. The response format is optimized for frontend consumption, returning only essential summary information for article listings.

operations.description:
Create a new article in the discussion board system. This operation allows authenticated citizens to create new articles with title, content, and optional attachments. The article is initially saved in 'draft' status and requires a publication step before becoming publicly visible. This operation directly interacts with the discussion_board_articles database table, which stores the primary article metadata including author, title, content, status, and timestamps.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated citizens (regular users) can create articles. The system automatically populates the author_id field from the JWT authentication token. No other actors (like moderators) are permitted to create articles through this endpoint.

Validation rules: The article title must be non-empty and under 500 characters. The content field must not be empty. The status field is automatically set to 'draft' and cannot be overridden by the client. The created_at and updated_at fields are managed by the system and populated automatically. The published_at field remains null until the article is published.

Relationships: This operation creates a record in discussion_board_articles, which can later be associated with comments (discussion_board_article_comments), tags (discussion_board_article_categories), and files (discussion_board_article_files, discussion_board_article_images) through separate operations. This article creation operation does not create or associate any attachments - those require separate POST operations on the appropriate attachments endpoints.

Important: This operation does not publish the article immediately. As per system requirements, articles must be published via a separate operation to maintain editorial control. This follows the business workflow where articles are reviewed before public display. Related operations: PATCH /articles (list/search articles), PUT /articles/{articleId} (update article), DELETE /articles/{articleId} (erase article), POST /articles/{articleId}/publish (publish article).

The article entity is linked to the discussion_board_articles database table, which stores all article metadata including the author ID, publication timestamp, and current status (draft, pending, published, etc.). Only the author of the article (citizen actor) or a moderator with appropriate privileges can perform this update. The operation validates that the article exists and is in a state that permits editing: only articles with status 'draft' or 'published' can be updated. Articles with status 'pending', 'hidden', or 'deleted' cannot be updated and will return a 403 error.

The system automatically logs all article updates to the discussion_board_article_status_logs table for compliance and audit purposes. This audit mechanism ensures accountability and enables moderation review if the updated content violates community guidelines. The update operation does not affect the article's creation date or original author information, preserving the article's provenance.

This operation is part of the article lifecycle managed by the discussion_board_articles table and its related metadata tables. It is paired with the GET /articles/{articleId} operation for retrieving article details and DELETE /articles/{articleId} for removing articles entirely. The update operation respects the article's current status: articles in 'draft' status can be freely edited, while articles in 'published' status remain accessible to the public while being modifiable only by their owner or administrators.

Note: This operation does not handle media attachments directly; those are managed through separate PUT operations on the related media tables (discussion_board_article_images, discussion_board_article_files, etc.).

This operation is restricted to moderators and administrators only. Regular citizens cannot delete articles they created, as articles are preserved for community review and moderation accountability. The article's status records (discussion_board_article_status_logs) and publication log (discussion_board_article_publication_log) are also permanently removed.

Each uploaded image must be a valid image file (PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG) with a maximum size of 5MB as specified in the system configuration. The operation returns the complete image record with auto-generated fields including upload timestamp, file metadata, and the generated thumbnail URI.

Security: Only authenticated citizens can upload images to articles they have permission to modify. Rate limiting enforces a maximum of 10 images per request and 50 images per article. The upload endpoint is protected against malicious file injection by validating file content type against the actual image binary signature, not just the file extension.

Related operations: GET /articles/{articleId}/images (list article images), DELETE /articles/{articleId}/images/{imageId} (remove an image).

The system validates that the article_id parameter corresponds to an existing article with appropriate visibility settings. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of file upload functionality. File uploads trigger audit events recorded in discussion_board_audit_events for security monitoring.

Implementation: This operation handles multipart file uploads through URI string references in the request body. The system automatically extracts file metadata including MIME type, size, and original filename. Uploaded files are stored securely and referenced by a generated file URI. The update operation modifies the updatedAt and updatedBy fields to reflect the modifier, while the original createdBy and createdAt fields remain unchanged to preserve attribution of original upload. The publication log does not include the article's content, metadata, or comments - only the state transitions concerning its publication status. For performance and clarity, this endpoint supports pagination and filtering of log entries by status type or date range. Security: Only authenticated users (citizen or moderator) with access to the article can view its publication log. This prevents unauthorized actors from tracking unpublished content history. The system ensures that logs for hidden or deleted articles are only accessible to moderators with appropriate permissions. Related operations: GET /articles/{articleId} (retrieve article details), PATCH /articles (search articles by status).
