operations.description:
Perform a bulk update of notification preferences for a set of users.

This operation updates notification preference settings for multiple users by providing an array of user identifiers and a new set of preference values. The operation is designed specifically for administrators to synchronize notification settings across multiple users in bulk, typically during onboarding or policy changes.

The request body expects an array of user IDs and a single update object containing the notification preferences to be applied. Each user referenced must have an existing account in the system and have a notification preference record associated with their user_id in the discussion_board_users table. System will update or create these records as needed.

Security: Only users with admin role can execute this operation. All changes are logged in the audit trail with the admin's identifier. The operation validates that each user ID provided corresponds to an existing user in the system before applying changes.

Implementation: This operation does not directly modify the discussion_board_notification_preferences table. Instead, it updates the notification preferences through the discussion_board_users table relationship, which has a one-to-one relationship with notification preferences. This architectural design maintains data integrity and prevents direct access to subsidiary table. For each user in the request, the system looks up their user record and updates or creates their associated notification preference record, then returns a summary of changes.

Related operations: GET /discussion_board/users (to retrieve user list for bulk update selection), PATCH /discussion_board/users/{userId}/notifications/preferences (for individual preference updates).
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Contains the list of user identifiers and the new notification preference settings to be applied in bulk.

responseBody.description: Summary of the bulk notification preference update operation, including total processed users, successfully updated users, failed users with reasons, and meta information about the update timestamp and executor.

prerequisites.description: User account must be created before notification preferences can be updated for that user.

operations.description:
Retrieve compliance audit reports generated by the system for regulatory and compliance tracking. This operation queries the discussion_board_compliance_records table to fetch all compliance-related events and records generated by system activities and user actions on the discussion board platform. Compliance records are created automatically by the system whenever users violate moderation policies, submit reports, or when moderators take actions on content or user accounts.

The operation returns a comprehensive dataset of compliance events including user reports, moderation actions, content violations, and system-generated audit events. This ensures full transparency and traceability for regulatory requirements and internal audits. Examples include when a user reports an article, when a moderator removes content, when a citizen's trust score changes, or when an appeal is filed against a moderation decision.

This is a read-only operation designed for compliance officers, internal auditors, and system administrators who need a complete historical record of platform governance activities. No authentication is required because compliance reports contain only system-generated audit data that should be accessible for transparency purposes. The operation is designed to support external regulatory compliance audits and internal quality assurance reviews. The response includes full metadata about each event including timestamps, actor information, affected content references, and action descriptions.

This operation does not have any prerequisites and can be called independently. It complements other moderation-related operations but serves as the authoritative source for official compliance records. The compliance reports are immutable and permanently stored, ensuring they serve as a reliable audit trail that cannot be altered by subsequent system operations.

Related operations include: POST /reports (to submit new reports), PATCH /moderation/actions (to retrieve moderator actions), and GET /citizen/violations (to view user violation histories). For legal compliance purposes, this operation should be called before any data deletion or account closure operations to generate a final compliance snapshot.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Collection of compliance audit records with event details, timestamps, and affected entities

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of security audit log entries from the system's comprehensive logging subsystem.

This operation allows authorized moderators to access recorded security events for compliance reviews, forensic analysis, and system monitoring. The endpoint provides read-only access to security-related records including authentication attempts, permission changes, configuration modifications, and access violations.

Access is restricted to users with the 'moderator' role. Regular citizens are not permitted to view security logs. All access attempts to this endpoint are themselves logged in the system for additional accountability.

The response includes metadata for each log entry: event type, timestamp, source IP address (when available), affected user ID, and a brief description of the event. Results are paginated to manage large result sets.

This endpoint integrates with the discussion_board_security_logs table and does not modify any data in the system. It is designed to meet regulatory compliance requirements including GDPR and CCPA by providing access to immutable audit records.

Related operations: GET /audit/moderation/actions (retrieves moderation actions), GET /users/{userId}/security/history (retrieves security history for a specific user).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of security audit log entries with event metadata

operations.name: get

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of operational audit logs from the discussion board platform. This operation queries the discussion_board_operational_logs database table, which tracks all system-level operational events including authentication attempts, security violations, system state changes, and maintenance activities. The logs are structured as immutable records that capture the exact state of system events for compliance, auditing, and forensic analysis.

The operation returns a comprehensive dataset including the event timestamp, actor identity (if authenticated), event type classification, source IP address, associated resource ID (when applicable), and detailed event metadata. This information enables platform administrators to monitor system health, detect anomalous patterns, and respond to potential security incidents. The log entries are designed to be append-only and are never modified or deleted to preserve audit trail integrity.

This endpoint is critical for system governance and regulatory compliance, providing verifiable evidence of system behavior during audit reviews or security investigations. The operation supports pagination to efficiently handle the potentially large volume of operational logs generated by the platform.

Related operations: GET /audit/security/logs (for security-specific events) and GET /audit/moderation/logs (for content moderation actions).

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of operational log entries containing full event details for system auditing and compliance.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve audit events from the discussion_board_audit_events table to monitor system activities and security events. This operation provides a comprehensive log of all significant system events including user authentication attempts, moderator actions, and system configuration changes. The audit trail is essential for security compliance, forensic analysis, and operational monitoring.

The operation supports advanced filtering and pagination to handle high-volume audit data. Filters include event type, actor, timestamp range, and severity level. Results are sorted by timestamp in descending order to show most recent events first.

Security considerations include restricted access to this endpoint - only administrators can retrieve audit logs to prevent tampering and unauthorized access. The operation does not return any personally identifiable information (PII) that isn't already part of the system's audit record.

The audit events schema includes fields for event type, actor identifier, target resource, timestamp, IP address, and additional metadata. This operation exposes this data through a paginated endpoint with search capabilities.

Related operations: GET /members (to identify actor names), GET /moderators (to identify moderator actions).
operations.name: get

responseBody.description: Paginated list of audit events with comprehensive event details including type, actor, timestamp, and metadata

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive administrative dashboard overview with aggregated system metrics and key performance indicators.

This operation compiles critical system statistics from multiple sources to provide administrators with a holistic view of platform health and activity. Unlike direct database table queries, this endpoint performs complex aggregations across multiple tables including articles, comments, users, reports, and moderator actions to deliver summarized insights.

The dashboard displays real-time metrics including total active users, recent activity volume, pending moderation tasks, system performance indicators, and compliance statistics. This aggregated view enables administrators to quickly assess platform status, identify emerging issues, and prioritize resource allocation without needing to navigate individual data tables.

Security protocols restrict access to administrative actors only, ensuring sensitive system metrics remain confidential. Rate limiting is applied to prevent excessive querying of high-compute aggregation endpoints. The data is calculated on-demand and reflects the current state of the system as of the request time.

The operation integrates data from multiple sources: discussion_board_articles for content volume metrics, discussion_board_comments for engagement levels, discussion_board_citizen for user statistics, discussion_board_reports and discussion_board_article_reports for moderation workload, and discussion_board_moderator_actions for active moderation metrics. No single database table represents this aggregated view—it is computed dynamically through combined queries.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive summary of administrative dashboard metrics including user activity, content volume, moderation workload, and system health indicators.

operations.description:
Retrieve all unresolved reports from the discussion board system for moderator review. This operation aggregates data from the discussion_board_reports and discussion_board_article_reports tables to provide a comprehensive view of unaddressed user reports.

The endpoint returns reports that have not been processed by moderators, including both standalone reports on user behavior and reports on specific article content. Each report contains metadata about the reporter, the reported entity, the reason for the report, and timestamp of submission.

Security: Only moderators can access this endpoint. The operation filters reports that have no associated moderation action record in the discussion_board_moderation_actions table. Reports are returned in chronological order with the oldest first to prioritize timely review.

System Design Note: This operation does not require pagination as the volume of unresolved reports in a healthy system should remain manageable (typically under 100 at any time). For systems experiencing high report volumes, automated moderation queues or automated classification systems are recommended.

Related Operations: GET /dashboards/reports/resolved to view processed reports and POST /moderation/actions to take action on reported content.

responseBody.description: List of unresolved reports containing reporter information, reported entity details, report reason, and timestamp

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve a high-level moderation summary for administrators, aggregating key metrics across the discussion board platform.

This operation provides an aggregated view of moderation activity by combining data from multiple system tables including moderation_actions, citizen_violations, report_aggregations, moderation_logs, and bans. It serves as a real-time operational dashboard for moderators to understand platform health and resource allocation needs.

The metrics include: total reported content items, pending moderation actions, active citizen suspensions, recent moderation actions within the last 24 hours, and the count of content items flagged for review. These metrics are computed dynamically from the underlying database tables and represent the current state of platform moderation activity.

All data is computed on-demand from the actual moderation records and does not correspond to any single database table. The operation ensures administrators have real-time visibility into the moderation workload and system health. This summary is updated dynamically as new reports, moderation decisions, and suspensions occur across the platform. Response includes aggregated counts, trends, and status indicators for immediate assessment.

Security: Only moderator and admin actors can access this summary. The operation does not expose individual user or content data, focusing instead on aggregate statistics to maintain privacy while providing actionable insights. This enables moderators to identify emerging patterns, workload imbalances, or potential system issues without compromising user privacy. The implementation uses database aggregation queries with efficient filtering to ensure fast response times even with large-scale data.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive summary of moderation activity across the discussion board platform, including key aggregated metrics for monitoring system health and moderator workload.

operations.description:
Retrieve real-time activity monitoring data for the discussion board platform.

This endpoint provides administrative insights into system activity by aggregating critical operational metrics from the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_activity_logs, and discussion_board_moderation_logs entities. The data enables system administrators to monitor platform usage patterns, detect anomalies, and ensure system integrity.

The operation calculates the total count of published articles, active comments, recent system events, and moderation actions over the past 24 hours. It provides essential visibility into platform health and user engagement without exposing sensitive user data.

Implementation notes: This operation does not map to a single database table but instead aggregates data from multiple system tables. The implementation executes five separate statistical queries:

1. COUNT of discussion_board_articles with status='published' AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
2. COUNT of discussion_board_comments with created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
3. COUNT of discussion_board_activity_logs with action_type IN ('login', 'post_create', 'comment_post') AND timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
4. COUNT of discussion_board_moderation_logs with action_type IN ('hide', 'delete', 'warn') AND timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
5. COUNT of discussion_board_article_reports with status='pending' AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'

The composite result provides a comprehensive operational dashboard for system monitoring, helping administrators identify emerging issues such as spikes in moderation actions or unusual activity patterns that may indicate abuse or technical problems.

This endpoint is exclusively accessible to administrators to maintain system security and data privacy.

responseBody.description: Aggregate metrics for platform activity monitoring

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Perform a unified global search across all public content types on the discussion board, including articles, comments, posts, and file attachments. This operation aggregates results from multiple database entities into a single search response, enabling users to find relevant content regardless of where it was originally posted.

The implementation executes composite SQL queries that UNION results from the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_posts, discussion_board_attachment_images, and discussion_board_attachment_files tables. Each result is tagged with its content type and includes only publicly accessible data (published status confirmed) with minimal metadata for quick display.

Security: Only returns content that has been published and is not subject to moderation restrictions. Private or draft content is excluded from results. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of this high-resource operation.

Implementation note: This does NOT map to a single database table - instead it executes:

SELECT 
  'article' as type,
  id,
  title as display_text,
  content as preview,
  created_at,
  author_id
FROM discussion_board_articles
WHERE status = 'published'

UNION ALL

SELECT 
  'comment' as type,
  id,
  content as display_text,
  content as preview,
  created_at,
  author_id
FROM discussion_board_comments
WHERE status = 'published'

UNION ALL

SELECT 
  'post' as type,
  id,
  title as display_text,
  content as preview,
  created_at,
  author_id
FROM discussion_board_posts
WHERE status = 'published'

UNION ALL

SELECT 
  'image' as type,
  id,
  file_name as display_text,
  description as preview,
  uploaded_at as created_at,
  uploaded_by as author_id
FROM discussion_board_attachment_images
WHERE status = 'published'

UNION ALL

SELECT 
  'file' as type,
  id,
  file_name as display_text,
  description as preview,
  uploaded_at as created_at,
  uploaded_by as author_id
FROM discussion_board_attachment_files
WHERE status = 'published'

ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 50;

This unified search serves the business requirement for users to find relevant content across all content types within a single interface. Related operations: GET /articles (search within articles only), PATCH /comments (search within comments only).
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search query parameters for global search including keywords, filters, and pagination controls.

responseBody.description: Paginated results of unified search across all content types with content type tagging and minimal data for display.

status.description:
Current status of the moderation action. This is updated based on the moderator's review outcome, such as 'resolved', 'pending', or 'appealed'. This field is required because it tracks the state transition of the moderation case within the workflow, and must be explicitly provided in any update operation to ensure the system maintains a consistent and auditable state progression.

The moderation system requires explicit status updates to trigger notifications, update moderation workflows, and maintain accurate status aggregations for reporting purposes. Status values are constrained by platform policy: 'approved', 'rejected', 'pending', 'appealed', 'resolved'.

Failure to include this field in an update request would prevent proper status progression and could cause blocking of moderation actions.

additional_notes.description:
Moderator-provided notes detailing the reasoning behind the status update, additional context about the moderation action, or comments regarding user behavior. This field is required because it provides human-readable context that is critical for audit trails, appeal reviews, and compliance verification.

The platform's legal and compliance framework mandates that every moderation action must be accompanied by a documented rationale. These notes serve as the primary source of context when reviewing moderation decisions during appeals or compliance audits.

This field is intended to capture explicit reasoning that supplements automated reason codes and creates a comprehensive human-readable record of the moderator's decision-making process.

Null values are not permitted because a moderation action without documented reasoning violates platform policy and regulatory requirements.

resolution_details.description:
Detailed explanation of the resolution applied, including findings from investigation, user communication outcomes, or actions taken beyond the initial moderation. This field is required because it documents the final resolution state and any follow-up actions taken in the moderation case.

This field captures the complete resolution narrative that explains how the moderation issue was fully addressed, including any disposition of reported content, user notifications issued, additional sanctions applied, or system changes implemented as a result of the case.

Resolution details are mandatory for all completed moderation cases to satisfy regulatory compliance requirements and to enable downstream reporting on the effectiveness of moderation actions.

This field is distinct from 'additional_notes' which captures the reasoning for action, while 'resolution_details' captures the final outcome and execution context.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying non-immutable metadata of a moderation log entry. This schema is used when a moderator needs to update the status, add notes, or provide resolution details for an existing moderation action.

All components of this update are mandatory to ensure regulatory compliance, auditability, and workflow integrity. The moderation system maintains an immutable audit trail where critical metadata (action_type, actor_id, target_id, created_at) cannot be modified, but required update fields that affect status, documentation, and resolution must be explicitly supplied.

This design ensures that every moderation action update is fully traceable, contextually documented, and legally defensible. Omission of any of these required fields would result in incomplete audit records that violate compliance standards and prevent proper workflow progression.

Immutable audit fields such as action_type, actor_id, target_id, and created_at are protected from modification and remain unchanged regardless of updates to this structure.

value.description: The new configuration value to be applied. This string value will be stored in the 'value' field of the discussion_board_configurations table and can represent any configuration type including JSON strings, boolean flags, numeric limits, or string-based settings depending on the configuration key. The value must be validated for syntactic and semantic correctness specific to the configuration key being updated.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating a specific configuration setting in the discussion board system. This schema defines the structure of the request body for PUT /discussionBoard/moderator/configurations/{configKey}. The configuration key is provided as a path parameter and should not be included in this request body. Only the 'value' field is required, representing the new configuration value to be applied. This DTO must exclude any immutable fields like 'key', 'created_at', 'last_modified', or 'metadata' as they are managed by the system and not modifiable by the client.

description.description: The description or caption of the attachment, which can be updated to provide additional context or correct errors. This field is optional and can be left null to retain the existing description.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for the Discussion Board Attachment entity. This schema defines the fields that can be modified when updating an existing attachment. All fields are optional, following the partial update pattern. The update operation modifies metadata (description, file_url, content_type, file_size, display_order) without altering the actual file content, which is immutable after upload. The system ensures authorization by verifying ownership (citizen) or elevated privileges (moderator) for the update request. This schema is used in PUT operations on /discussionBoard/citizen/attachments/{attachmentId} and /discussionBoard/moderator/attachments/{attachmentId}.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token used to renew the admin's access token. This token must be previously issued during a successful login operation and still valid in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. It must be a valid JWT token string with proper cryptographic signature.

IAdmin.IRefresh.description: Request body for the admin refresh token operation. Contains the refresh token necessary to obtain a new access token while maintaining authentication context without requiring credential re-entry. This schema follows security best practices by including only the refresh token and no other credentials or user identifiers.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. This field is required to ensure consistent pagination behavior across all client applications. Without a defined page, the API response could return an unpredictable number of records, leading to inconsistent user experiences in list views.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Default is 20 if not specified. This setting controls record volume per API response, optimizing network performance and client-side rendering. Values beyond 100 are prohibited to prevent excessive memory consumption and slow response times on bulky datasets.

oneOf.description: Field to sort by. Must be one of: "created_at", "file_size", or "filename". Defaults to "created_at" if not specified. This parameter allows clients to control the ordering of uploaded attachments in the response list. Sorting by 'created_at' provides chronological order, 'file_size' orders by file volume (useful for identifying large uploads), and 'filename' provides alphabetical sorting based on the user-provided original filename.

After the field for sorting is selected, order controls presentation priority - typically 'desc' is preferred to show most recent uploads first.

file_extension.description: Exact file extension to filter by (e.g., "jpg", "pdf"). Case-insensitive matching. Matches the file extension part after the last dot. This parameter allows users to search for attachments of specific file types from the discussion_board_attachments table. Filters are applied against the 'extension' column which stores normalized, lowercase file extensions. Useful for finding all images (jpg, png, gif) or documents (pdf, docx) without retrieving unrelated file types.

min_file_size.description: Minimum file size in bytes. Filters attachments to include only those with size greater than or equal to this value. This search criterion allows filtering out small or potentially invalid files (like empty uploads) by setting a minimum threshold. Must be a non-negative integer. For example, setting this to 1048576 ensures only files larger than 1MB are returned. This helps users find meaningful content and reduces noise from placeholder or corrupted files.

max_file_size.description: Maximum file size in bytes. Filters attachments to include only those with size less than or equal to this value. This search criterion allows limiting results to files that meet storage or bandwidth constraints. Must be a non-negative integer. For example, setting this to 20971520 ensures only files up to 20MB (system maximum) are returned. Used by moderators to find large files that may require additional review.

created_after.description: ISO 8601 datetime string. Filters attachments created after this timestamp. This parameter enables searching for attachments uploaded following a specific point in time, useful for auditing recent uploads or investigating content posted after an event. Must follow ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ. When used with created_before, it creates a time window filter for time-series analysis.

created_before.description: ISO 8601 datetime string. Filters attachments created before this timestamp. This parameter enables searching for attachments uploaded up to a specific point in time, useful for reviewing content posted before an event or policy change. Must follow ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ. When used with created_after, it creates a time window filter for time-series analysis.

oneOf.description: Type of content the attachment is linked to. Must be one of: "article", "comment", or "post". This field allows filtering attachments by the type of content they are associated with in the discussion board system. It corresponds to the 'attachment_type' field in the discussion_board_attachments database table. This categorization is critical for organizers to retrieve all attachments for articles, comments, or general posts in one query without retrieving irrelevant content.

content_id.description: UUID of the specific content item (article, comment, or post) to filter attachments by. Attachment must be linked to this exact content ID. This parameter allows precise retrieval of all attachments associated with a single content item. Uses the 'object_id' field from the discussion_board_attachments table. For example, querying with a specific article ID returns only attachments linked to that article, enabling modular content display in UIs. Must be a valid UUIDv4 format.

author_id.description: UUID of the citizen who uploaded the attachment. Only applicable when authorizationActor is "citizen"; moderators may use this to filter by any author. This field filters attachments by the uploading user, retrieved from the 'upload_citizen_id' column in the database. Citizens can only filter for their own uploads (matching their JWT identity). Moderators can filter to find uploads by any citizen for moderation purposes, such as investigating pattern abuse or reviewing a specific user's content history.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and pagination of attachment records. This schema defines the search criteria for retrieving attachments from the discussion_board_attachments table based on file metadata, creation dates, associated content, and ownership context. All fields are optional to support flexible search querying, but pagination parameters (page, limit) are treated as required to ensure consistent pagination behavior across all client applications.

The system is designed to handle complex filtering combinations. For example, users can combine file_extension with created_after to find all .jpg images uploaded after a specific date, or use min_file_size with parent_type to find large files attached to articles.

Security Note: The API enforces access control based on user role and attachment visibility. Even if a response includes a record in the search, clients may receive a permission error if they attempt to access the attachment's actual content (file_url) without authorization.

Common Use Cases:
- Citizens: Find all images they uploaded to their articles
- Moderators: Retrieve all attachments for an article flagged by reports
- Administrators: Audit all attachments uploaded in the last 24 hours
- Analytics: Generate reports on attachment content types over time

This schema must be used with the PATCH method (not GET) because it contains complex filtering logic that exceeds URL length limits and requires structured data that cannot be efficiently expressed in query parameters.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and filtering parameters for configuration retrieval. This schema defines the filter criteria used to query system configuration parameters for the discussion board platform. Configuration parameters control platform-wide behaviors including content visibility rules, attachment limits, posting frequency restrictions, moderation thresholds, and operational performance parameters. Since this is a request schema for a read-only operation, it contains only filtering and search parameters, not configuration values themselves.

The request object allows clients to specify criteria for retrieving specific configuration settings. It supports both exact value matching and range queries for numerical configuration parameters. Since configuration management is handled by administrative interfaces, this request schema is intentionally minimal and focused on query parameters only.

Note: This schema defines request parameters, not configuration values. Configuration values are returned in the IDiscussionBoardConfiguration response schema.

section.description: Section or category of configuration settings to retrieve. Used to filter configuration settings by functional area. Valid values include 'content', 'moderation', 'performance', 'security', and 'user_interface'. When not specified, all configuration settings are returned.

key.description: Exact configuration key to retrieve. Used for fetching a specific configuration parameter by its unique key name. Supports wildcard matching with '*' character at the end (e.g., 'attachment_*' to match all attachment-related settings).

minValue.description:
Minimum value filter for numerical configuration parameters. Used to filter configuration settings where the value is greater than or equal to this threshold. Applies only to numeric configuration parameters.

Example: Setting minValue: 5 would return configuration settings where the value is 5 or higher.

maxValue.description:
Maximum value filter for numerical configuration parameters. Used to filter configuration settings where the value is less than or equal to this threshold. Applies only to numeric configuration parameters.

Example: Setting maxValue: 100 would return configuration settings where the value is 100 or lower.

type.description: Type of configuration parameter to filter by. Used to restrict results to configuration parameters of a specific data type. Valid values include 'string', 'number', 'boolean', and 'json'. When not specified, all types are returned.

isActive.description: Filter for active configuration parameters only. When set to true, returns only configuration settings that are currently active and in effect. When set to false, returns only inactive configuration settings. When not specified (null), both active and inactive configurations are returned.

name.description:
The name of the discussion channel. Must be unique and contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, hyphens, and underscores. This is the primary identifier users see when browsing channels.

Channel names should be concise, descriptive, and reflect the topic or theme of the content to be discussed. They cannot be altered after creation to maintain consistency in links and references.

description.description:
A detailed description of the channel's purpose, rules, and expected content. This provides context for users before they participate in discussions within this channel.

Descriptions should be comprehensive enough to guide user behavior, set expectations for content quality, and clarify any specific moderation policies that apply to this channel. This field is optional but strongly recommended for effective community management.

isArchived.description:
Indicates whether the channel has been archived and is no longer accepting new content.

Archived channels remain accessible for viewing historical content but prevent new articles, comments, or attachments. This is used for seasonal topics, completed projects, or outdated discussion themes that should no longer be actively moderated.

oneOf.description:
Visibility and moderation status of the channel. Determines whether this channel appears in public listings:

- `draft`: Channel is being configured but not yet published
- `pending`: Channel has been submitted for review but not yet approved
- `published`: Channel is active and visible to all users
- `hidden`: Channel has been temporarily hidden by moderators

Channels with status 'draft' or 'pending' are not visible to regular citizens. Only moderators can change visibility.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new discussion board channel. This schema defines the fields required to establish a new container for organizing articles and community interactions.

The channel creation process is restricted to users with moderator or administrator privileges. The schema enforces required fields to ensure all newly created channels have a proper name, visibility setting, and configuration. This complements the 'IDiscussionBoardChannel' response type, which adds system-generated fields like 'id' and 'created_at' upon successful creation.

All user submissions are validated for length and format constraints before database insertion, and violations trigger appropriate error responses. Security is enforced at the application level through authorization checks against the 'moderator' actor context within the discussion_board_channels model.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for channel filtering. Used in the patch /discussionBoard/channels operation to filter and paginate discussion board channels based on name, description, category, active status, and other search criteria. Supports comprehensive sorting and pagination functionality for efficient channel discovery.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Default value is 1 when not specified.

limit.description: Number of channels per page in the result set. Must be between 1 and 100. Default value is 20 when not specified. Higher values increase response size but reduce total page count.

oneOf.description: Field to sort channels by. Valid values are 'name' for alphabetical order by channel name, 'created_at' for chronological order by creation timestamp, and 'member_count' for ranking by number of members in the channel.

search.description: Free-text search term to match against channel name and description fields. Performs partial string matching to find channels containing the specified term. Case-insensitive matching is applied.

is_active.description: Filter channels by active status. When true, returns only active channels. When false, returns only inactive channels. When not provided, returns all channels regardless of active status.

category.description: Filter channels by specific category reference. Only channels assigned to this category will be included in results. Use this to narrow results to a specific content category.

IAdmin.ILogin.description:
Request DTO for admin authentication login. Contains email and password credentials used to authenticate a moderator account against the discussion_board_moderator table.

The email field is matched against the discussion_board_users table to identify the corresponding admin record.
The password field is validated using bcrypt comparison against the hashed password stored in the discussion_board_moderator table.

The system only allows login for moderators with active status (discussion_board_moderator.status = 'active'). Suspended, banned, or deleted accounts cannot authenticate.

This operation is publicly accessible and does not require prior authentication.

The system enforces rate limiting on authentication attempts to prevent brute force attacks, tracking failed attempts in the discussion_board_authentication_logs table.

Passwords are always transmitted in plain text to this endpoint and are hashed server-side before storage comparison.

email.description: The registered email address of the moderator account. This is matched against the discussion_board_users table to identify the corresponding admin record. Must be a valid email format as defined in RFC 5322.

password.description: The plaintext password credential for the moderator account. This is validated against the hashed password stored in the discussion_board_moderator table using bcrypt comparison. Never transmit pre-hashed passwords; always send the original plaintext password. This is the only field that accepts plain password input; all other representations (password_hashed, hashed_password, password_hash) are strictly forbidden.

authentication_type.description: Type of authentication event being logged. Indicates the nature of the authentication attempt, such as login, logout, or failed authentication. Maps directly to the authentication_type column in the discussion_board_authentication_logs table which tracks the classification of each authentication event for security analysis and audit purposes.

ip_address.description: The IP address from which the authentication event originated. Captures the network location of the authentication attempt for security monitoring and geo-location analysis. This corresponds to the ip_address column in the database which stores the client's IP address during the authentication event.

user_agent.description: The user agent string provided by the client's device or browser during authentication. Contains detailed information about the operating system, browser, and device used for the authentication attempt. This maps to the user_agent column in the database which stores full user agent strings for forensic analysis and security monitoring.

IDiscussionBoardAuthenticationLog.ICreat.description: Request data structure for creating a new authentication log entry in the discussion board platform. This schema defines the mandatory fields required to record authentication events such as logins, logouts, and failed attempts. Each log entry captures critical security information including the type of authentication event, originating IP address, and client device information. This data is stored in the discussion_board_authentication_logs table as part of the platform's comprehensive security monitoring and compliance requirements. All fields are required to ensure complete audit trails for forensic analysis, breach detection, and regulatory compliance.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorAction.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and pagination of moderator actions log retrieval. This schema defines the query parameters used to filter moderation actions by time range, actor, action type, and content type, with pagination controls for handling large result sets. The fields correspond directly to the filtering capabilities described in the API operation for /discussionBoard/moderator/moderation-logs.

This schema is used by the moderator role actors to retrieve historical moderation events. It enables administrators to audit governance and compliance activities across the platform.

All filter fields are optional except for page and limit, which are required for pagination safety. Without these parameters, queries could return unbounded result sets that negatively impact system performance.

Note: The field names in this schema use camelCase (e.g., moderatorId) for consistency with JavaScript/TypeScript conventions, while the underlying database tables use snake_case (e.g., moderator_id). The service layer automatically maps these field names during query translation.

afterTime.description:
Filter actions that occurred after this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ) to specify the lower boundary of the time range.

This parameter is useful for incremental data retrieval, such as syncing with external systems or implementing real-time monitoring dashboards. When used with beforeTime, it creates a time window for analysis.

Example: "2026-01-09T17:39:02Z"

Must be earlier than beforeTime if both are provided. If unspecified, the system will include actions from the earliest available record.

beforeTime.description:
Filter actions that occurred before this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ) to specify the upper boundary of the time range.

This parameter defines the end of the analysis window and is typically used in conjunction with afterTime. When specified without afterTime, retrieves all actions up to this point.

Example: "2026-01-09T17:39:02Z"

Must be later than afterTime if both are provided. If unspecified, the system will include actions up to the most recent record.

moderatorId.description:
Filter actions performed by a specific moderator. Uses UUID format (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8") to reference the unique identifier of a moderator in the discussion_board_moderator table.

When specified, only moderation actions taken by this specific moderator will be included in the results. This is useful for auditing individual moderator activity or assessing workloads.

This field maps to the moderator_id column in the discussion_board_moderator_actions table. The application converts camelCase "moderatorId" to snake_case "moderator_id" during query construction.

actionType.description:
Filter actions by type. Specifies the specific moderation intervention performed.

Valid values include: "remove_content", "suspend_user", "warn_user", "appeal_resolve", "ban_user", "unban_user", "modify_status", "restore_content".

Must match the action_type field in the discussion_board_moderator_actions table. This field enables targeted analysis of specific moderation behaviors.

Example: "remove_content" for reviewing content removal decisions.

This field maps to the action_type column in the database (camelCase to snake_case conversion handled by service layer).

targetType.description:
Filter actions by the type of target entity affected. Specifies the category of content or user that was subject to moderation.

Valid values include: "article", "comment", "citizen", "attachment", "channel", "report".

This field enables analysis of moderation patterns across different content types. For example, tracking whether certain content types are disproportionately targeted.

Example: "comment" to investigate comment moderation trends.

This field maps to the target_type column in the discussion_board_moderator_actions table (camelCase to snake_case conversion handled by service layer).

page.description:
Pagination page number. Must be a positive integer starting at 1.

Specifies which page of results to return. Each page contains a fixed number of items defined by the limit parameter.

This parameter is required because without pagination, a single request could return millions of records, overwhelming system resources.

Example: page: 3 returns the results from the third page (records 41-60 if limit=20).

limit.description:
Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.

Controls the batch size of results returned per request, balancing performance and response size. Default is 20 items per page, which is sufficient for most UI display needs.

Maximum limit of 100 is enforced to prevent performance degradation from excessively large result sets.

Example: limit: 25 returns 25 records per page.

This parameter is required to ensure controlled data retrieval and prevent unbounded queries.

oneOf.description: Sort results chronologically by the timestamp of the moderation action.
Sort results by the identifier of the moderator who performed the action.
Sort results by the type of moderation action performed (e.g., "ban_user", "remove_content").
Sort results by the identifier of the content or user affected by the moderation.

sortField.description:
Field to sort results by. Must be one of the following: "createdAt", "moderatorId", "actionType", or "targetId".

Determines the primary sort order for moderation actions. When unspecified, results are sorted by createdAt (most recent first) by default.

The corresponding database fields are: created_at, moderator_id, action_type, and target_id (converted from camelCase to snake_case in service layer).

oneOf.description: Sort results in ascending order (oldest to newest).
Sort results in descending order (newest to oldest).

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction. Must be either "asc" (ascending) or "desc" (descending).

Defines the order of results based on the sortField. Default sort direction is "desc", which shows the most recent actions first.

Example: sortDirection: "desc" creates reverse chronological order of moderation events, showing the most recent actions at the top.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating a discussion board channel. Only provided fields are modified; omitted fields retain their current value. Do not include readOnly fields like id, createdByUserId, createdAt, or channelCode.

name.description: The display name of the channel. Used in UI for channel listing and selection. Must be between 1 and 100 characters and cannot be empty when provided.

description.description: Detailed description of the channel's purpose and guidelines. Used for community posting guidance and can be displayed in channel header. Can be null or empty to clear existing description.

oneOf.description:
Visibility and moderation status of the channel. Determines whether this channel appears in public listings:

- `draft`: Channel is being configured but not yet published
- `pending`: Channel has been submitted for review but not yet approved
- `published`: Channel is active and visible to all users
- `hidden`: Channel has been temporarily hidden by moderators

Channels with status 'draft' or 'pending' are not visible to regular citizens. Only moderators can change visibility.

isArchived.description: Indicates whether the channel has been archived. Archived channels are preserved for historical purposes but hidden from active listings.

name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded attachment as provided by the client. This preserves the original file naming for user reference and debugging.

This field corresponds to the `original_filename` column in the discussion_board_attachments database table and must be populated with the actual filename from the client upload. Validation rules require a non-empty string with a maximum length of 255 characters to prevent database overflow.

extension.description:
File extension without the leading dot (e.g., "jpg", "pdf", "zip"). This field standardizes file extension representation for system processing and content type determination.

The extension must be extracted from the original filename and validated against the platform's allowed file types (jpg, jpeg, png, gif, pdf, doc, docx, zip). The 10-character maximum ensures compatibility with filesystem and database constraints while accommodating modern long extensions.

size.description:
File size in bytes representing the exact size of the uploaded attachment. This value is calculated by the system during upload and used for storage accounting and quota enforcement.

The size corresponds to the `file_size_bytes` column in the database and must be a positive integer between 1 byte and 20,971,520 bytes (20MB), which is the maximum allowed file size per policy. This field ensures compliance with storage limits and helps prevent abuse.

mimetype.description:
Standard MIME type (content type) of the file as determined by content inspection and file signature analysis. This field provides accurate content classification independent of the file extension.

This maps to the `content_type` column in the database and should follow IANA standards (e.g., "image/jpeg", "application/pdf"). The system performs content verification to ensure the declared MIME type matches the actual file content, enhancing security against malicious uploads. Value length is limited to 100 characters to accommodate complex custom MIME types.

content_id.description:
Identifier of the discussion board content (article, comment, etc.) to which this attachment is associated. This creates the relationship between the attachment and its parent content item.

This field corresponds to the `content_id` column in the discussion_board_attachments table. The value must be a valid UUID that references an existing content record in the system. This allows efficient retrieval of all attachments for a specific content item and establishes the ownership relationship required by the application's data model.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new attachment for discussion board content. This schema defines all required information for uploading files and images associated with posts, articles, or comments. The attachment creation operation requires authentication as a citizen and enforces strict validation rules for file size, type, and integrity.

The request body must include the original filename, file extension, file size in bytes, accurate MIME type, and content ID to which the attachment is linked. This design follows the two-phase upload pattern where files are first uploaded to object storage, then referenced by URL in this DTO.

All fields are required because the system must have complete information to properly process, validate, and store the attachment. This ensures data consistency and prevents incomplete or broken links in the system. The maximum file size is capped at 20MB (20,971,520 bytes) to maintain performance and system reliability.

oneOf.description:
The target publication status for the article, determining its visibility state in the discussion_board_articles table.

- 'published': The article becomes publicly visible to all users
- 'hidden': The article is removed from public view but retained in the system for audit purposes
- 'deleted': The article is permanently removed from public view and marked for archival

This status value triggers a corresponding entry in discussion_board_article_status_logs and is recorded in discussion_board_moderation_actions with the administering moderator's identity. This privileged operation bypasses normal publication workflows and requires admin authentication via JWT token.
