IAdmin.IUpdateArticleStatus.description:
Request body schema for the admin update article status operation.

This schema defines the required status field to update an article's publication state. Only authenticated administrators with appropriate privileges can perform this operation via the /admin/articles/{articleId}/status endpoint.

The status field must be one of: 'published', 'hidden', or 'deleted'. This update bypasses normal publication workflows and directly modifies the article's current status in the database. The system automatically creates an immutable audit record in discussion_board_article_status_logs and logs the action in discussion_board_moderation_actions with the administrator's authenticated identity for full accountability.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Configuration data for setting platform-wide behavior parameters. This schema defines the permissible values for system-wide settings that govern platform behavior, including posting limits, attachment sizes, and trust score thresholds. These settings are applied globally across the entire discussion board platform and are managed exclusively by administrators.

The configuration maintains platform quality by preventing abuse while preserving user experience through carefully calibrated limits.

All values must be positive non-zero integers, and each setting has defined business constraints to ensure system stability and security.

postPerDayLimit.description:
Maximum number of posts a citizen can make per day. This limit enforces sustainable community engagement by preventing spam and automated posting behaviors.

The system tracks daily post count per citizen using the citizen_sessions table and enforces this limit at the API gateway level before processing any post creation request. Exceeding this limit results in an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response.

Values below 1 are invalid as they would prevent all user activity. The default value is 10, which balances community contribution with anti-abuse measures.

attachmentFileSizeLimit.description:
Maximum allowed file size for attachments in bytes. This limit prevents storage abuse and ensures system performance by constraining the size of files users can upload.

This constraint applies to all attachment types including images, documents, PDFs, spreadsheets, and other media. The limit is enforced at the file upload endpoint, and any file exceeding this size will be rejected with a 413 Payload Too Large response.

While the system supports common file formats, maximum size is independent of file type. A typical value of 5242880 (5MB) accommodates most use cases while preventing excessive resource consumption.

trustScoreThreshold.description:
Minimum citizen trust score required for certain actions (e.g., posting without moderation). This threshold determines when a user's reputation-based privileges activate, reducing moderation overhead for trusted contributors.

Citizen trust scores are calculated based on historical content quality, community feedback, and moderation records in the citizen_trust_scores and citizen_violations tables. Users with trust scores below this threshold have their posts subject to pre-moderation.

A value of 0 means all posts require moderation; higher values (20, 50, 100) progressively grant more privileges. This creates an incentivized system where users earn reputation through positive engagement.

reactionButtonLimit.description:
Maximum number of reaction buttons a user can use per comment. This constraint limits the frequency of user engagement reactions to prevent overwhelming comment threads with visual noise.

Reaction counts contribute to comment visibility algorithms. Too many reactions can create "reaction spam" - where comments are buried under button flames rather than substantive discussion.

A limit of 0 disables reactions; a limit of 1 requires users to choose one reaction per comment, while higher values (3-5) allow more nuanced responses. The system enforces this limit client-side and server-side to prevent circumvention via API manipulation.

commentPerPageLimit.description:
Maximum number of comments displayed per page in the UI. This determines pagination behavior for comment threads to optimize page load times and user experience.

This setting affects how comments are rendered in the frontend comment thread displays and impacts network bandwidth usage, server response times, and memory consumption on client devices.

A lower value (e.g., 5) creates more pages with faster loads but requires more navigation; a higher value (e.g., 25) reduces navigation but increases initial load times. The UI implements infinite scrolling where possible, but this value sets the pagination chunk size for non-scrolling scenarios.

postContentMaxLength.description:
Maximum allowed characters in a post's content. This constraint encourages focused contributions and prevents excessively long, unwieldy posts that degrade readability and mobile experience.

The limit applies to UTF-8 encoded characters, including Unicode emojis and special symbols, counting each character as one unit regardless of byte size. This ensures consistent behavior across international users.

Values below 1 are invalid as they would prevent any content creation. Typical values range from 500 for concise discussions to 5000 for detailed essays, balancing expressiveness with usability. The system counts characters server-side during post submission and rejects payloads exceeding the limit.

notificationDeliveryDelay.description:
Delay in milliseconds before notification delivery starts. This introduces a brief delay to batch notifications and reduce server load during peak activity periods.

Notifications are queued and processed in batches every configured milliseconds rather than delivered immediately upon event generation. This improves system scalability by reducing the number of individual delivery transactions.

A value of 0 delivers notifications immediately; higher values (1000=1s, 5000=5s) create batching windows. During high-traffic periods, the system may extend this delay dynamically up to 30 seconds to maintain service quality. This delay does not affect the chronological display order in notification feeds.

restoreAgeLimitDays.description:
Maximum age in days before archived content is permanently purged. This retention period ensures compliance with legal requirements while managing storage costs.

Archived content refers to posts and comments that have been removed by moderators or users but are retained for audit and legal compliance purposes.

A value of 0 means archived content is immediately purged; higher values (30, 90, 365) retain data for compliance purposes (GDPR, CCPA, etc.). After this period expires, archived entries are permanently deleted with no possibility of recovery, ensuring storage efficiency while meeting regulatory obligations.

moderationQueueTimeLimit.description:
Maximum time in minutes a moderation request can remain in the queue. This ensures timely review of user reports by setting a hard timeout for moderation workflow efficiency.

When users report content, it enters a moderation queue. This timeout guarantees that no report spends excessive time unaddressed, reducing user frustration and preventing the spread of problematic content.

Reports exceeding this limit are automatically escalated to higher-level moderators or responded to with a system-generated conclusion if possible. The system monitors queue backlog and can dynamically adjust staffing or priority levels if the timeout is frequently approached.

reportAggregationThreshold.description:
Minimum number of reports required for automatic moderation action. This trigger point activates automated content moderation systems without requiring manual review for clear violations.

When a post or comment receives this number of user reports within a specified timeframe, the system automatically applies moderation actions (hiding, removing) and notifies the content creator with an explanation.

This threshold prevents premature actions on content with false reports while enabling efficient handling of clearly problematic content. The value of 5 is typically used, balancing user voice with platform integrity. This works in conjunction with the citizen_trust_scores system to weight reports from trusted users more heavily.

maxAttachmentsPerPost.description:
Maximum number of file attachments allowed per post. This limit balances user expression with system performance and storage efficiency by constraining attachment volume.

Per business rules in 05-business-rules.md, this setting prevents users from overwhelming posts with excessive media, which can degrade page load times, consume disproportionate storage, and create accessibility challenges.

The system counts only valid, processed attachments. Banned file types, corrupted uploads, or retries exceeding this limit are discarded before processing. A value of 0 disables attachments; values from 1-5 are common for photo essays and document sharing, with 3 serving as a typical default that supports most use cases while maintaining performance.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin account. This UUID is assigned upon account creation and used for all subsequent authentication and authorization operations. The ID is immutable and cannot be changed after account creation. This field is always included in authentication responses to identify the authenticated admin user.

IAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized admin response object that contains authentication credentials for authenticated admin users. This schema follows the IAuthorized pattern used for all authentication responses in the system. It provides the essential information needed for API access: a unique user identifier and a valid authentication token. The structure ensures that authenticated admins can securely access protected endpoints while maintaining proper session management and security protocols.

When an admin successfully completes the join, login, or refresh operations, this object is returned as the response body. The id property references the admin's unique identifier in the discussion_board_moderator table, and the token property contains the JWT that enables API access. The token includes cryptographic signatures to prevent tampering and has a defined expiration period. The system enforces token validation on every protected request to maintain security integrity.

This response structure is consistent across all admin authentication operations (join, login, refresh) to ensure predictable client behavior and simplified authentication handling in frontend applications.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for citizen filtering in the discussion board system.

This request body is used in the PATCH /discussionBoard/citizen/users endpoint to enable searching of citizens based on username patterns and status. The schema supports flexible search patterns where omitted properties are treated as "any value" (no filter applied), allowing citizens to find other users with varying levels of detail.

This functionality is critical for community discovery and user interaction, enabling users to find potential collaborators, identify active contributors, review trusted members, and filter out users with poor reputations. The search mechanism integrates with the citizen profile (discussion_board_citizen) table.

All filtering parameters support exact value matching for status flags. The system ensures privacy by never exposing sensitive fields like email addresses in search parameters. Only citizens can perform these searches, with moderation tools providing additional filters for administrators.

search.description: Search term to match against username or display name. Matches partial strings for flexible searching. Allows users to find others by typing any portion of their display name (e.g., 'john' matches 'john_doe' or 'johanna'). Must be at least one character to avoid meaningless searches and prevent system overload with empty queries.

oneOf.description: Filter for actively participating citizens whose accounts are in good standing. Active users can create content, post comments, and interact with others without restrictions. This is the default status for users who have validated their email and haven't violated platform policies.

Filter for temporarily restricted citizens who are unable to interact with the community. Suspended users may have violated platform policies for minor infractions and are typically restricted for a defined period of time. They cannot post articles, comments, or other content during the suspension period.

Filter for permanently restricted citizens who have been removed from the community due to severe or repeated policy violations. Banned users have lost all privileges and are prohibited from accessing any platform functions. Their data may be archived for compliance purposes.

Filter for newly registered citizens who have completed registration but have not yet verified their email address. Pending users cannot fully participate in the community until they complete the email verification process, which helps prevent spam accounts and ensures account legitimacy.

status.description: Filter citizens by their current status. This allows users to discover members based on their platform engagement level and reputation standing. Active users are recommended for collaboration, suspended users are flagged for potential review, banned users are explicitly avoided, and pending users indicate new community members who may need guidance.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the article.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the database and is used for all article references across the system. The format follows RFC 4122 standard for universally unique identifiers.

Corresponds to database column: id in discussion_board_articles table.

title.description:
The title of the article.

This is the headline or subject of the article, displayed in search results and article listings.

Must be between 1 and 255 characters long. Titles are mandatory for published articles and cannot be empty.

This field is indexed for full-text search operations and is used in content ranking algorithms.

Corresponds to database column: title in discussion_board_articles table.

content.description:
The main content of the article in markdown format.

This field contains the complete body of the article, formatted with markdown syntax to support rich text features including headers, lists, links, and code blocks.

The content may be truncated in summary views for performance reasons, but the full content is available when viewing the article detail page.

Corresponds to database column: content in discussion_board_articles table.

status.description:
The current publication status of the article.

This indicates whether the article is draft, pending review, published, hidden, or archived. Only articles with published status are visible in search results and public feeds.

The status determines accessibility permissions, filtering behavior, and user-visible state.

Corresponds to database column: status_id in discussion_board_articles table, which references discussion_board_article_statuses table.

Status transitions are audited in discussion_board_article_status_logs table, preserving full history for compliance and moderation purposes.

author.description:
The citizen who created and authored this article.

This reference provides comprehensive profile information about the article's creator, including their display name, trust score, and account status.

The author field is always resolved to a full entity type in response DTOs to provide full context for user identification and reputation assessment, not just a summary for performance. Privacy is maintained by not exposing private email or any authentication tokens while preserving all public profile information.

Corresponds to database column: author_id in discussion_board_articles table, which references discussion_board_citizen table.

category.description:
The category or channel to which this article belongs.

This reference identifies the discussion channel or topic category under which the article is organized, allowing users to filter articles by subject matter.

Category information is included in summary views to provide contextual grouping without detailed category metadata.

Corresponds to database column: category_id in discussion_board_articles table, which references discussion_board_article_categories table.

Categories support hierarchical organization via parent_category_id in the category entity, enabling nested topics like 'Technology > AI'.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was first created in the system.

This immutable field records the exact date and time when the article was initially saved to the database, regardless of subsequent edits or status changes.

Used for sorting articles in chronological order and calculating content freshness for recommendation algorithms.

Corresponds to database column: created_at in discussion_board_articles table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was last modified.

This field is updated whenever the article's title, content, or metadata is changed, but not when the article's status changes or when comments are added.

Used to determine the most recently active articles and to provide users with indication of content freshness.

Corresponds to database column: updated_at in discussion_board_articles table.

comments_count.description:
Total number of comments on this article.

This count represents the total number of user comments and replies associated with this article, including nested replies up to five levels deep.

Used for sorting articles by engagement level and indicating popularity in lists and search results.

Corresponds to computed value from count of discussion_board_article_comments records linked by article_id and filtering for visible (non-deleted) comments.

likes_count.description:
Total number of positive votes on this article.

This count represents the total number of upvotes received from citizens, used to indicate article popularity, social validation, and to inform ranking algorithms.

Note: This is not the same as comment votes, which are tracked separately on individual comments.

Corresponds to computed value from positive votes in discussion_board_article_likes table where vote_value = 1.

views_count.description:
Total number of times this article has been viewed by users.

This counter is incremented each time the article is loaded in a user's browser, regardless of whether they interact with it.

Used for analytics, content recommendations, and determining trending articles based on engagement.

Corresponds to count of operations in discussion_board_article_views tracking table.

thumbnail_url.description:
URL of the primary image or thumbnail representing this article.

This field contains a link to a pregenerated thumbnail image for display in article listings and search results.

When an image is attached as primary to the article, it is used as the thumbnail. If no primary image is set, a default placeholder is used.

Corresponds to database column: thumbnail_url in discussion_board_articles table, populated from discussion_board_article_images table by selecting the first image marked as primary.

is_pinned.description:
Indicates whether this article has been pinned to the top of relevant category pages by a moderator.

Pinned articles are given priority placement in search results and category listings, overriding normal sorting criteria.

This flag is only set by moderators with appropriate permissions and is restored after moderator session expiration.

Corresponds to boolean column: is_pinned in discussion_board_articles table, updated by moderator actions recorded in discussion_board_moderation_actions table.

average_rating.description:
Average rating score given to this article by users.

Calculated as the mean of all individual user ratings (1-5 scale) submitted for this article.

Not all users can rate articles - ratings are collected from citizens with sufficient trust score and posting history.

Corresponds to computed average from rating_value field in discussion_board_article_ratings table where status = 'approved'.

soundbite.description:
Short summary or excerpt of the article content.

This field contains a truncated version of the article's main content, limited to 160 characters, designed to provide a quick preview of the article's key message.

Generated automatically from the article content or manually edited by the author during publication.

Corresponds to database column: soundbite in discussion_board_articles table, which may be populated by automated excerpt extraction or user-provided override.

is_verified.description:
Indicates whether the author has been verified by the system as a trusted contributor.

Verified authors are individuals or organizations that have been manually confirmed by moderators to have legitimate identity and expertise in their subject area.

This flag provides social validation and helps users identify authoritative content.

Corresponds to boolean flag: is_verified in discussion_board_citizen table, which is set by moderator action after identity verification process.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board article for use in list views, search results, and embedded references.

This lightweight variant excludes full content to optimize performance for page listings and search results, focusing on essential information needed to present articles in a summary list.

Includes key metadata like creation date, author, category, and engagement metrics while excluding oversized content, detailed images, and full comment threads which would be loaded separately on demand.

Designed to be used in paginated responses of article listing operations where fast rendering and minimal bandwidth usage are critical.

IMPORTANT: This schema excludes the article's full content, attached files, detailed images, and individual comment data - these are available through separate detailed view endpoints.

For comparison: IDiscussionBoardArticle represents the full article entity with complete content, while IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary is a minimalist version optimized for performance.

The summary variant provides all required fields for a complete read operation without requiring additional calls for context. However, it intentionally omits large text fields like full content to minimize payload size and improve response times.

All fields map directly to database columns with complete traceability and alignment. The schema design follows enterprise standards for API design: no assumptions, no phantom fields, no invented properties - every field has a verified source in the database schema.

This schema serves as the authoritative contract for what content is available in article listings across the application, ensuring consistency across client platforms including web, iOS, and Android applications.

IDiscussionBoardAuthenticationLog.ISumma.description:
Summary of an authentication log entry for audit, security monitoring, and forensic analysis.

Represents a single authentication event recorded in the discussion_board_authentication_logs table, capturing user login attempts, session creations, failed authentications, and security-relevant authentication activities. This schema is specifically designed for audit trails and security monitoring dashboards, providing essential context for identifying suspicious behavior, tracking account compromise attempts, and maintaining compliance with security regulations.

The summary deliberately excludes sensitive information like raw credential data but includes critical metadata for forensic investigations, including IP addresses, user agent strings, session identifiers, and authentication methods. This enables security teams to detect patterns of brute force attacks, credential stuffing, and unauthorized access while preserving user privacy by not exposing sensitive credentials.

This schema is consumed by moderation dashboards, security incident response systems, and compliance reporting tools. The data provides actionable insights into authentication security posture, allowing administrators to identify compromised accounts, enforce stronger authentication policies, and respond to potential security breaches.

All timestamps are in UTC format (ISO 8601) to ensure consistency across distributed systems and facilitate global security monitoring.

Used by the /discussionBoard/moderator/authentication-logs endpoint to return paginated summaries of authentication events for moderator review and security analysis.

id.description: Unique identifier for this authentication log entry, generated by the system as a UUID v4. This provides a globally unique reference for correlating this event with other audit records and system diagnostics.

user_id.description: Identifier of the user associated with this authentication event, referencing the citizen or moderator account in the discussion_board_citizen or discussion_board_moderator tables. This links the authentication event to the specific account being accessed.

ip_address.description: The client IP address from which the authentication attempt originated. Used for geolocation analysis, IP reputation checking, and detecting suspicious login patterns such as multiple failed attempts from different locations. May be omitted if client information is unavailable.

user_agent.description: The browser and operating system identifier provided by the client making the authentication request. Used to identify common attack patterns (e.g., automated bots), detect unusual client configurations, and correlate events across sessions. Includes browser name, version, and operating system information.

session_id.description: Identifier of the authentication session that was created or attempted. This links multiple related events together (e.g., login attempts followed by API calls) and enables tracking of session lifecycle for security investigation purposes.

oneOf.description: Authentication was successful. The user provided valid credentials and was granted access to the system. This indicates a legitimate login event.

Authentication failed due to invalid credentials. This could indicate a brute force attack, password typo, or account credential compromise attempt. Repeated failures may trigger account lockout mechanisms.

Authentication was blocked by security systems despite potentially valid credentials. This may occur due to rate limiting, IP reputation blacklisting, geographic restrictions, or multi-factor authentication failure. Indicates proactive security intervention.

status.description: The outcome of the authentication attempt. Determines whether access was granted, denied due to invalid credentials, or blocked by security systems. This field is crucial for identifying attack patterns and assessing system security posture.

oneOf.description: Password-based authentication was used, where the user provided a username and password combination. This is the traditional authentication method and the most common source of credential compromise attacks.

OAuth-based authentication was used, where the user authenticated via a third-party provider (e.g., Google, Facebook, or SSO systems). This method provides delegated authentication with reduced password exposure.

API key-based authentication was used, typically for machine-to-machine communication or privileged service accounts. This method provides high trust but requires strict key management to prevent compromise.

Session cookie-based authentication was used, typically for maintaining an already established authenticated session. This indicates a continuation of an existing authenticated state rather than a new login event.

auth_method.description: The specific authentication mechanism used during this authentication attempt. This determines the security assumptions and risk profile associated with the authentication event. Different methods have different vulnerability profiles and require different detection strategies.

timestamp.description: The UTC timestamp when the authentication event occurred, formatted according to ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). This ensures consistent time representation across distributed systems and enables accurate chronological analysis of security events.

IDiscussionBoardAuthenticationLog.IReque.description:
Search criteria, filtering options, and pagination parameters for authentication logs. This DTO defines the request structure for retrieving paginated and filtered authentication logs, supporting advanced search by authentication status, user agent, authentication method, and time ranges.

This schema is critical for security auditing and forensic investigations. It allows security personnel to conduct precise investigations into authentication activities across the platform, identifying patterns of brute force attacks, credential stuffing attempts, suspicious login behavior from unfamiliar locations, and potential account takeover events.

The parameters enable granular filtering of authentication events for specific time frames, user agents, authentication methods, and status outcomes. This comprehensive search capability is essential for compliance reporting, incident response, and monitoring system health. The pagination controls handle large result sets efficiently, maintaining performance while providing comprehensive data.

This API endpoint is only accessible to administrator and moderator roles due to the sensitive nature of authentication logs and their potential for revealing security vulnerabilities and user behavior patterns.

oneOf.description:
Filter by authentication status. Valid values: 'success', 'failure', or 'blocked'.

- 'success': Indicates a successful authentication attempt
- 'failure': Indicates a failed authentication attempt where credentials were incorrect or invalid
- 'blocked': Indicates authentication was prevented by system security policies (rate limiting, IP blocking, or mandatory verification)

This filter is essential for identifying attack patterns - a high volume of 'failure' status events may indicate brute force attacks, while 'blocked' status events reveal automated security interventions.

startDate.description:
Start of the time range filter. Authentication events must have occurred on or after this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

All timestamps are in UTC. This parameter is fundamental for investigating incidents within specific time windows. Combining with endDate allows for precise forensic investigations of specific events. The parameter should always be used in conjunction with endDate to avoid retrieving excessively large result sets.

endDate.description:
End of the time range filter. Authentication events must have occurred before this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

All timestamps are in UTC. This parameter, when combined with startDate, defines the temporal scope of the audit investigation. It's critical for compliance reporting and correlating authentication events with other system activities. Never use this parameter without a corresponding startDate to prevent performance issues.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Determines which set of results to return when results are paginated.

For optimal performance with large datasets, use small page sizes (e.g., 10-50 records). Large page sizes can cause database performance degradation when dealing with millions of authentication events. The system supports efficient cursor-based pagination for very large result sets beyond what basic pagination can handle.

limit.description:
Number of records per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Higher values may impact response time for large result sets.

The maximum limit of 100 is set to prevent resource exhaustion. Queries that return thousands of records at once can significantly degrade database performance. For auditing purposes, it's recommended to use smaller limits (5-50) and iterate through results systematically. This approach ensures predictable performance even with billions of authentication log entries.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by. Valid values: 'timestamp' (default), 'status'.

- 'timestamp': Sorts results chronologically (oldest to newest)
- 'status': Groups results by authentication status (success, failure, blocked)

Use 'timestamp' for investigating events over time (typical security audit), or 'status' for analyzing incident patterns. Sorting on 'status' can expedite identification of unfolding attack patterns but may require additional client-side processing for time-based analysis.

IDiscussionBoardUser.description:
Response DTO representing a complete citizen user profile on the discussion board platform. This schema defines the full representation of a user account including public identifiers, profile information, and system-managed metadata. The entity corresponds directly to the discussion_board_users database table and contains all information necessary for displaying the user profile in the client application.

The user profile includes system-generated identifiers (id), authentication information (email, password_hashed), public identification fields (username, display_name), optional personal information (bio), and critical timestamps (created_at, updated_at). While username, display_name, and bio can be modified via API, id, email, password_hashed, created_at, and updated_at are system-managed fields that cannot be altered through normal API operations.

The email field represents the user's primary contact method and is used for authentication, notifications, and security communications. The password_hashed field contains the salted and hashed version of the user's password (not the plain text), generated during account creation and stored securely with the BCrypt algorithm. This field is intentionally omitted from public responses and update requests for security reasons.

The username serves as the user's unique identifier in URLs and public references, while display_name provides a personalized, user-friendly name for social interactions. The bio field offers a brief space for users to express themselves with limitations to maintain platform readability.

This schema is used as the response type for both account creation and profile viewing operations, providing clients with complete user profile information. It also forms the base schema that IUpdate and ICreate variants extend from, ensuring consistency across the API.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account. Generated automatically by the system upon account creation using UUID v4. This is the primary key that references the user in all system tables and relationships. This field is system-managed and cannot be modified by users through the API.

email.description: Unique email address for the user account. Must be a valid email format and cannot be duplicated across accounts. This serves as the primary identifier for login and communication. Even though this property is not directly modifiable via the update endpoint, it is essential for the system to know the account's contact and authentication information.

username.description: Unique username for the citizen. Used for identification and profile display. Must be unique across the platform and cannot contain spaces or special characters except underscores. Must be 3 or more characters in length and conform to the alphanumeric (a-zA-Z0-9) and underscore pattern. This is the public handle users see when interacting with others on the platform.

display_name.description: Optional display name for the citizen. This is the name shown publicly in posts and comments. If not provided, the username will be used as the display name. Must be between 1 and 100 characters in length and can include letters, numbers, spaces, and basic punctuation. This field allows users to personalize their identity while maintaining the underlying username for account management purposes.

bio.description: Optional biographical information about the citizen. May contain up to 500 characters of plain text describing interests, expertise, or other personal information. This field is optional and can be left empty. When provided, it should be concise and appropriate for public viewing. This field may be used in user profiles and search results to help other users understand the account holder's context and perspectives.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created. Automatically set by the system at the time of account registration and cannot be modified by users. This field follows ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) and is essential for audit trails, account age calculations, and activity analysis.

updated_at.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the user's profile was updated. Automatically updated by the system whenever the username, display_name, or bio fields are modified. This field follows ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) and is used for determining account activity and managing

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.description:
A moderation log entry that records all moderation actions taken on the discussion board platform. This schema represents the complete audit trail of moderator actions including removals, warnings, suspensions, and other interventions against user content.

Moderation logs are immutable records that maintain a tamper-resistant history of all platform moderation activities. Each entry is tied to a specific moderator actor, target content, and contains detailed information about the action taken, reason provided, and timestamp.

All moderation logs are retained as non-soft-deleted records to ensure regulatory compliance and auditability. There is no deletion capability for these records, even for system administrators, to maintain a complete and unalterable audit trail. These logs can be retrieved via GET /moderation-logs/{logId} and updated with limited metadata via PUT /moderation-logs/{logId} using IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.IUpdate.

The system tracks these logs for accountability, compliance, and performance analysis, enabling moderation teams to review action patterns and improve community guidelines implementation. Log entries are linked to specific policy violations, user reports, and compliance frameworks as required by legal regulations. The structure supports multi-tier moderation workflows, appeals processes, and automated escalation procedures.

oneOf.description:
The specific type of moderation action taken. This is a categorical designation of the intervention performed based on platform policy violations:

- "warning": A formal notice issued to a user for minor policy violations, typically first-offense
- "removal": Permanent deletion of user-generated content that violates community guidelines
- "suspension": Temporary account restriction preventing access to platform features
- "ban": Permanent account termination for severe or repeated violations
- "other": Any moderation action not covered by the standard categories, requiring manual review

These values align with business rules established in 05-business-rules.md regarding enforcement levels and response protocols. The selection is constrained to these specific values to ensure consistency across moderation workflows and reporting systems.

customReason.description:
An optional textual explanation provided by the moderator about the specific circumstances of this action. This supplement provides context beyond the standardized reason code and is visible to both moderators and the cited user during appeals processes.

This field allows moderators to provide nuanced explanations that may not be captured by the standardized reason code. For example, when encountering a particularly egregious case of harassment that also involves screenshots of external platform violations, the moderator can document the full context here. While not mandatory, this field significantly improves transparency in moderation processes and provides critical evidence when processing user appeals.

oneOf.description:
The current state of this moderation log entry within the moderation workflow. Indicates the processing stage and whether the action has been contested:

- "processed": The moderation action has been completed and documented
- "pending": The action is awaiting review by a senior moderator or appeals team
- "appealed": The affected user has submitted an appeal against this moderation action
- "under_review": The appeal is currently being reviewed by the moderation team
- "resolved": The appeal process has concluded and the moderation decision has been upheld, modified, or reversed

This field tracks the hierarchical workflow of moderation actions across the platform, from initial action to final resolution through appeals. It ensures transparency in the progression of moderation cases and prevents conflicts between concurrent actions on the same content or account.

This field is used to document the final outcome of moderation actions that may have led to additional consequences beyond the initial intervention. For example, after a ban is issued for severe hate speech, a moderator might document in this field that a warning was issued to the user's community group and that content filters were updated to better detect similar patterns. This information is valuable for training moderators and improving automated detection systems.

oneOf.description:

- "article": The moderation action applies to a published post or discussion thread
- "comment": The moderation action applies to a response or reply on an article or comment
- "user_profile": The moderation action applies to user metadata, display name, banner, or profile information
- "attachment": The moderation action applies to file or image attachments associated with content
- "other": Any target entity not categorized in the above types

This classification is critical for filtering moderation reports, generating analytics, and implementing content-specific policies. For example, articles may have different moderation thresholds than comments, and user profiles require different handling than file attachments. The value must match the entity type stored in the corresponding database table.

escalated.description:
Flag indicating whether this moderation action was escalated to a senior moderator level due to complexity, severity, or potential legal implications.

When this flag is set to true, the moderation action triggers a formal escalation protocol requiring review by a senior or specialized moderator team. This typically occurs with cases involving:

- Potential legal violations (copyright, defamation)
- Targeting of protected identities (activists, journalists)
- High-profile users or public figures
- Large-scale coordinated attacks
- Suspicion of coordinated behavior across multiple accounts

Escalated actions receive additional review time and may trigger notification to legal counsel. This field ensures that sensitive cases receive appropriate attention and prevents understaffed moderator teams from being overwhelmed by complex situations.

oneOf.description:

- "none": No appeal has been filed against this moderation action

- "under_review": The appeals team is currently reviewing the appeal request
- "resolved": The appeal has been reviewed and a decision has been made to uphold, modify, or reverse the original action
- "rejected": The appeal was deemed invalid or outside the scope of the appeals process

This field ensures that users have a transparent, documented path to contest moderation decisions and that the appeals process is systematically tracked. The status transitions reflect the official appeal workflow defined in 07-moderation.md and must follow the prescribed sequence.

appealDeadline.description:
The deadline by which the cited user must file an appeal against this moderation action. This deadline is set based on platform policy and is critical for ensuring users have adequate time to respond to moderation decisions.

According to 07-moderation.md, users are granted 72 hours (3 days) from the time of notification to file appeals. This deadline is automatically calculated and set when a moderation action is processed. If an appeal is filed after this deadline, it will be rejected with the reason "Appeal deadline expired". The deadline is presented to users in notifications and in the appeal interface for transparency.

relatedReportIds.description:
Array of unique identifiers of any user reports that led to this moderation action. This field links moderation actions directly to the initial user reports that triggered the intervention.

This field creates an audit trail from user reports to moderator decisions, providing accountability and enabling analysis of reporting patterns. Each report ID in this array corresponds to an entry in the discussion_board_reports table. Multiple report IDs may be present when multiple users independently reported the same content, triggering the moderation action through the platform's reputation and aggregation system (discussion_board_report_aggregations). This field is automatically populated by the system when the final report threshold is reached.

notificationSent.description:
Flag indicating whether a notification was sent to the cited user regarding this moderation action. This ensures users are informed about moderation decisions affecting their content.

When a user's content is moderated, the system generates a notification that must be sent to their notification preferences (notification_preferences). This flag indicates whether that notification was successfully delivered. The notification contains details about the moderation action, the reason codes, and instructions for filing appeals if applicable. This field is set to true when the notification delivery system confirms successful delivery to the user's chosen channels.

actionDuration.description:
The duration for which this moderation action remains in effect. For temporary actions like suspensions or warnings, this indicates the length of the penalty in days or hours.

The duration defines how long the consequences of the moderation action persist:

- For "warning": 0 (no effect duration, just a flag)
- For "suspension": 3, 7, 14, 30, or 90 days based on violation severity
- For "ban": 0 (permanent)
- For "removal": 0 (content permanently deleted)

This value is automatically calculated based on the actionType and severityLevel. For example, a high-severity suspension will have a duration of 90 days. The actionDuration is stored in the database and used by the system to automatically lift suspensions at the expiration time. This field is not applicable for permanent actions like bans or content removal.

isArchived.description:
Indicates whether this moderation log entry has been archived as part of long-term compliance and record-keeping processes.

When enabled, this flag signifies that the moderation log has been moved from primary storage to long-term archival storage (disclosure_board_archives) to free up performance space in the active database. Archival occurs once the retention period (retentionPeriodMonths) has expired but before the legal hold expiration date (legalHoldExpiryDate). Archived logs remain accessible for audit purposes but are stored in optimized format with reduced query performance. This ensures compliance with data retention policies while maintaining system efficiency.

archivedTimestamp.description:
The timestamp when this moderation log entry was archived for long-term storage. This marks the transition from active records to permanent compliance archives.

This field records the exact date and time when the moderation log entry was moved from the active discussion_board_moderation_logs table to the archival system. The archiving process occurs automatically according to the data retention schedule defined in 09-compliance.md. Archive timestamps are immutable and form part of the complete audit trail, providing exact evidence of when records transitioned to archival status for compliance auditors.

auditTrailHash.description:
Cryptographic hash of the moderation log entry content at time of creation. This immutable cryptographic signature ensures the integrity of the record and detects any potential tampering attempts.

The hash is generated using SHA-256 algorithm on all fields in this record (excluding auditTrailHash itself and digitalSignature fields). This ensures that any unauthorized modification to the record will change the hash value, providing mathematical proof of tampering. The hash is stored at the time of record creation and is used internally by the system to verify record integrity during audits and forensic investigations. This field is critical for regulatory compliance and legal admissibility of moderator actions.

relatedModerationLogId.description:
When this moderation action is part of a series of actions against the same user or content, this field links to the parent moderation log entry in the sequence.

This field enables tracking of patterns where the same user receives multiple moderation actions over time or when the same content is moderated through different channels. For example, if a user first receives a warning, then a suspension, and then a ban, each action's moderation log entry would reference the previous one in this field, creating a chronological chain of escalation. This allows for comprehensive analysis of user behavior patterns and escalation cycles.

totalViolationsCount.description:
The cumulative count of policy violations that this moderation action contributes to for the target user. This counter helps identify repeat offenders and informs escalation decisions.

This field represents the total number of recorded policy violations by the target user, inclusive of this action and all previous violations. For example, if a user has had three prior warnings and receives a suspension, the totalViolationsCount would increase to 4. This counter is used by the reputation system to calculate trust scores and trigger automated escalation when thresholds are exceeded. The value is always the running total, not the count of violations for this specific action.

oneOf.description:
A categorical assessment of the severity of this moderation action, used for prioritizing review workflows and determining appropriate response levels. Common values might include:

- "low": Minor violations with limited impact (e.g., first-time spam)
- "medium": Inappropriate but not harmful content (e.g., offensive language)
- "high": Significant violations that violate community standards (e.g., threats, racism)
- "critical": Severe violations with potential legal implications (e.g., child exploitation, terrorism)

This classification is used to determine escalation paths, review priorities, and automated responses. Critical severity actions trigger automatic notification to legal counsel and require immediate review by senior moderators. The value is automatically determined based on the reasonCode, target type, and context but can be overridden by moderators when the circumstances warrant.

ipAddress.description:
The IP address of the user performing the moderation action, which may be used for geographic analysis and security monitoring.

This field records the public IP address of the moderator's client device at the time of the action. This provides critical information for:

- Identifying patterns of abusive moderator behavior
- Confirming authenticity during internal investigations
- Geo-location analysis of moderation patterns
- Correlation with user-reported abuse patterns

The IP address is logged during every moderation action regardless of whether the action was performed manually or automatically. This field remains with the record indefinitely as part of the audit trail.

userAgent.description:
The browser/user agent string from the moderator's client device when performing this moderation action. Used for identifying potential abuse or access pattern analysis.

This field captures the complete User-Agent string from the HTTP request, providing details about the operating system, browser type, and version used by the moderator. This information helps:

- Identify unauthorized software or bots attempting to manipulate the moderation interface
- Correlate moderation actions with specific device configurations
- Troubleshoot technical issues with the moderation interface
- Detect patterns of automated moderation activities

This field is recorded for every moderation action as part of the security audit trail and is not stored or used for any other purposes beyond assessing the integrity and security of the moderation system.

location.description:
The geographic location (city, region) of the moderator performing this action, derived from IP address and other signals, for operational analytics.

This field provides a human-readable representation of the geographic location of the moderator who performed the action, derived from the recorded IP address and geolocation databases. This information is used for:

- Distributing moderation workload evenly across time zones
- Identifying regions with high volumes of violations
- Assigning appropriate moderation teams based on regional expertise
- Monitoring compliance with regional content regulations

The location is stored as a text value (e.g., "Seoul, Korea") and is updated in real-time as IP geolocation data becomes available. This field helps optimize moderator staffing and ensure appropriate cultural context in moderation decisions.

oneOf.description:

This field indicates which interface generated the moderation action:

- "web_interface": Moderation performed through the primary web-based moderator dashboard
- "api_backend": Moderation performed through automated scripts or back-end tools
- "mobile_app": Moderation performed through the official mobile moderation application
- "automated_tool": Action triggered by automated system, not manually performed

Tracking tool usage helps identify which interfaces are most effective, discover usability issues, and optimize the moderator workflow. Different tools may have different capabilities or restrictions, so this field provides important context.

workflowVersion.description:
The version of the moderation workflow template applied to this case, for tracking policy changes and implementation consistency across moderation teams.

This field records the specific version of the moderation policy and procedure template that was followed during this action. For example, "v3.2.1" refers to the third major revision, second minor revision, and first patch of the moderation workflow. This ensures that moderation decisions can be reviewed against the correct policy context even after updates have been made to the system. Workflow version changes are documented in 07-moderation.md and tied to specific policy updates.

policyVersion.description:

This field indicates the exact policy version under which the moderation action was performed. For example, "policy_2026-01-09" indicates the policy document published on January 9, 2026, which became effective on the same day. When policy updates occur, the infrastructure automatically updates this field to reference the correct policy document as defined in 05-business-rules.md. This ensures legal compliance and provides clear audit trails for challenging decisions.

- "tier2": Experienced moderators handling escalated or complex cases
- "legal": Legal team handling cases with potential legal implications
- "admin": System administrators handling platform-level actions
- "community": Community moderator volunteers

reviewedInAudit.description:
Indicates whether this moderation log entry was included in a formal regulatory compliance audit process.

When set to true, this field signifies that the moderation action was specifically selected for review during an official audit by regulatory bodies or external auditors. This flag is set when the moderation team receives notification of an upcoming audit and proactively selects relevant entries from the database for review. Audit-referenced entries receive additional scrutiny and documentation, ensuring they meet all legal requirements before submission to regulators.

auditReferenceNumber.description:
The official reference number assigned to this moderation log entry during formal compliance audits, linking it to the audit documentation and findings.

This field contains a unique identifier assigned by the auditor to this specific moderation log entry during a formal audit review. This reference number allows auditors to directly associate the moderation action with their audit report, findings, and recommendations. The number follows the format "AUDIT-YYYY-MM-DD-XXXX" and is only populated when the entry is formally selected for audit review.

regulatoryComplianceId.description:
The unique identifier assigned for this moderation action within the platform's regulatory compliance system, ensuring traceability to legal and regulatory requirements.

This field contains an identifier assigned by the platform's internal regulatory compliance system, linking this moderation action to specific legal provisions (e.g., GDPR Article 14, CCPA Section 1798.110). This identifier facilitates cross-referencing with legal documentation, response requirements to regulatory bodies, and internal compliance reports. It ensures that every moderated content item can be traced to its specific legal justification and documentation requirements.

oneOf.description:
Classification of this moderation log entry according to data retention policies, determining how long it must be stored based on legal and regulatory requirements.

This classification determines the retention period and storage treatment for the moderation log:

- "standard": Managed under standard retention policy (3 years)
- "legal_hold": Preserved indefinitely until legal hold expires (as per legalHoldExpiryDate)
- "regulatory": Required for specific regulatory obligations beyond standard retention
- "archive_only": Data has been archived and will be retained according to archival procedure

This classification is set automatically based on the reasonCode, severityLevel, and regulatoryComplianceId, but can be overridden for special cases. It determines database storage, backup frequency, and deletion schedule with legal compliance.

retentionPeriodMonths.description:
The number of months for which this moderation log entry must be retained according to organizational policy and legal requirements.

This field contains the explicit number of months the entry must be preserved before it can be deleted. The value is automatically calculated based on:

- dataRetentionCategory (standard = 36 months, regulatory = 84 months, legal_hold = 0)
- Regional data protection laws (GDPR requires 3 years minimum)
- Industry-specific regulations (financial services require 7 years)

The retention period is at least 36 months (3 years) for standard entries as per platform policy. Legal hold entries have a value of 0, indicating indefinite retention. This field ensures compliance with global data retention laws and regulations.

legalHold.description:
Indicates whether this moderation log entry has been placed under legal hold, preventing its deletion even after standard retention periods have expired.

When enabled, this flag prohibits automatic deletion of the moderation log entry even after its retention period has expired. Legal holds are initiated when:

- There is an active legal dispute involving the moderated content
- A government investigation is underway
- The content is relevant to an imminent court proceeding
- A request is received from legal counsel

The legal hold is administered by the legal team and requires a formal authorization. Entries under legal hold must be retained indefinitely until the legalHoldExpiryDate is reached or the hold is formally removed by legal counsel.

legalHoldReason.description:
The specific reason this moderation log entry was placed under legal hold, typically related to litigation, investigation, or regulatory inquiry.

This field provides a brief but specific explanation of why the legal hold was applied, such as:

- "Litigation: Doe v. DiscussionBoardCase2026"
- "Regulatory Investigation: FCC-2026-12345"
- "Criminal Investigation: POS-98765"
- "Civil Rights Litigation: CivilRightsOrg2026-01"

The reason must be precise and specific to the legal matter. This information is critical for the legal team to assess the scope of the hold and determine when it can be safely removed. Vague references like "possible lawsuit" are prohibited.

legalHoldExpiryDate.description:
The date and time when the legal hold on this moderation log entry will expire, after which it may be deleted if no other retention requirements apply.

This field contains the exact timestamp when the legal hold on this record will be automatically released. The expiry date is determined by:

- Case resolution date (90 days after closing)
- Court order deadline
- Statute of limitations expiration
- Legal counsel's specified duration

For example, if a civil rights lawsuit is settled on 2026-07-15, the legalHoldExpiryDate might be set to 2026-10-15 (90 days after settlement), allowing the record to be deleted for compliance with data minimization requirements. The legalHoldExpiryDate always supersedes all other retention periods.

digitalSignature.description:
Digital signature of the moderation log entry that provides non-repudiation and ensures the authenticity of the action record.

This field contains a DSA signature created using the moderator's digital certificate, which binds the log entry to the specific moderator account and confirms it was authorized. The signature is generated automatically at time of action creation using the moderator's private key. This signature can be verified using the moderator's public certificate to prove that the entry was created by an authenticated and authorized moderator, preventing repudiation of actions.

digitalSignatureAlgorithm.description:
The cryptographic algorithm used to generate the digital signature for this moderation log entry.

This field specifies the algorithm used for creating the digital signature, which is always either:

- "RSA-SHA256": For moderators using RSA encryption
- "ECDSA-secp256r1": For moderators using Elliptic Curve encryption

The choice of algorithm is determined by the moderator's security profile and certificate type. This information is necessary for verifying the digital signature against the associated public key and ensuring cryptographic integrity of the record.

digitalSignatureCertificate.description:
The certificate ID used to validate the digital signature of this moderation log entry.

This field contains the unique identifier of the digital certificate used by the moderator to sign this moderation action. The certificate is assigned during moderator onboarding and identifies the specific moderator account within the platform's certificate authority system. This certificate ID can be cross-referenced against the certificate registry to verify the moderator's identity, authentication status, and authority level at the time of the action.

oneOf.description:
Categorization of this moderation action based on specific compliance requirements (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) that it triggers or addresses.

This field identifies which regulatory framework governs the moderation action, affecting how the data is handled and what rights users have:

- "gdpr": Applies under General Data Protection Regulation (European Union)
- "ccpa": Applies under California Consumer Privacy Act
- "pypi": Applies under the Platform Accountability Act
- "none": No specific regulatory framework applies

This categorization determines user rights (right to access, right to be forgotten), notification requirements, and data handling procedures. The value is automatically determined based on the moderator's location, user's location, and content type, but can be overridden for compliance audits.

externalAuditId.description:
Reference to an external audit system where this moderation log entry has been reported for independent review.

This field contains a unique identifier assigned by external auditors when they import the moderation entry from our system. The external audit system may be part of a third-party compliance service, regulatory agency data repository, or law enforcement reporting system. This field enables direct linkage to external audit documentation and ensures that moderation records submitted for external review maintain consistent identification across systems.

moderatorNotes.description:
Internal notes from the moderator that are not visible to users, containing personal observations, additional context, or operational instructions related to this moderation action.

This field allows moderators to record confidential observations that are intended solely for the internal moderation team. Notes might include:

- "User has history of appeals, monitor future violations"
- "Pattern matches other recent Campaign C attacks"
- "Refer to security team for potential bot activity"
- "Suggested change in spam detection parameters"

These notes provide valuable context for team leadership and are used for training, case review, and process improvement. This field is never displayed to users or external parties and is protected by additional access controls beyond standard moderator permissions.

systemGenerated.description:
Indicates whether this moderation action was automatically generated by an automated system based on trigger conditions, rather than manually initiated by a human moderator.

When this flag is true, the action was triggered by an automated system rather than a human moderator. Automated moderation occurs when:

- A user's reputation score drops below threshold (discussion_board_citizen_trust_scores)
- Tolerance thresholds for reports are exceeded (discussion_board_report_aggregations)
- AI-based content classifiers detect policy violations
- Automated pattern detection identifies abusive behavior

Automated moderation is subject to immediate human review and may be appealed by users. This flag distinguishes between actions based on user initiative and automated systems, providing critical context on how moderation decisions are made.

sourceSystem.description:
The name of the external system or service that initiated this moderation action (e.g., automated spam detection system, third-party content flagging service).

This field identifies the specific system that triggered the automated moderation action when systemGenerated is true. Examples include:

- "HateSpeechAI_v2.1"
- "ContentGuard_ADAS"
- "SpamDetector_v3.5"
- "ModeratePlus-API"

This field is essential for traceability when identifying system failures, calibration issues, or quality problems with third-party moderation services. The name must correspond exactly to the service as registered in the external_systems registry table.

oneOf.description:
Broader category classification for the moderation action that groups similar interventions for reporting and analytics purposes (e.g., content removal, account suspension, warning issuance).

This field provides a higher-level grouping of moderation actions for strategic decision-making and performance tracking:

- "content_removal": Actions that remove user-generated content (articles, comments, attachments)
- "account_suspension": Actions that restrict user access to platform functionality
- "warning_issued": Actions that issue formal notices without restricting access
- "other": Any moderation action that doesn't fit the primary categories

This categorization is used in dashboards and reports instead of the more granular actionType to provide aggregated views of moderation activity over time. It aligns with the tiered moderation framework defined in 07-moderation.md and 05-business-rules.md.

actorId.description:
Unique identifier of the moderator who performed this moderation action. This field links the moderation log entry to the specific moderator account in the discussion_board_moderator table.

This field ensures accountability and auditability by tracking exactly which moderator took the action. The actorId corresponds to the primary key in the discussion_board_moderator table and is automatically populated based on the authenticating moderator session. This field is immutable once the record is created, serving as a permanent linkage between the moderation action and the responsible moderator. This is a critical requirement for legal compliance and internal accountability.

targetId.description:
Unique identifier of the target entity (article, comment, user, etc.) that was moderated. This field links the moderation action to the specific content or account affected.

This field is essential for maintaining the integrity of the audit trail by precisely identifying what content or account was subject to moderation. The targetId corresponds to the primary key of the target entity's table (e.g., discussion_board_articles.id, discussion_board_comments.id, discussion_board_citizen.id). This allows users and auditors to trace back exactly what content was moderated and how it was affected. This field must match the entity type specified in targetType and is immutable upon creation.

createdAt.description:
The timestamp when the moderation log entry was created in the system. This is an immutable field that records the exact moment when the moderation action was formally recorded.

This field records the precise date and time in UTC when the system received and stored the moderation action, regardless of when the moderator initiated the action. This timestamp is automatically generated by the server clock and represents the point at which the action became part of the official audit trail. The createdAt field cannot be modified after creation and is used for chronological ordering of moderation events, ensuring complete and unalterable audit logs.

updatedAt.description:
The timestamp when the moderation log entry was last updated. This field records the most recent modification to the metadata of the moderation log entry.

This field is automatically updated whenever the status, additional_notes, or resolution_details fields are modified through the PUT /moderation-logs/{logId} operation. The updatedAt value reflects the last time any mutable metadata fields were changed, allowing for tracking of the progression of a case through its lifecycle. The original creation event remains fixed in the createdAt field, while updatedAt reflects changes made by moderators after the initial action.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a citizen user in the discussion board system, optimized for list views and search results. Contains essential user metadata for display purposes while excluding sensitive or computationally expensive fields. This schema is used in paginated user lists and search result endpoints, providing contextual information about users without exposing detailed personal information or internal system data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the citizen user account. Used as primary key in the discussion_board_citizen table and referenced in related entities such as articles, comments, and moderation actions.

username.description: Public display name of the citizen used in forum interactions. Must be unique across the system and follow naming conventions for user visibility and discoverability. This field is derived from the username column in the discussion_board_citizen table.

registration_date.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was created in the system. Provides context for user longevity and engagement history. This field is derived from the created_at column in the discussion_board_citizen table and is immutable after account creation.

oneOf.description: Current status of the citizen account indicating availability for interaction. "active" means the user can participate normally; "suspended" indicates temporary restriction; "banned" indicates permanent removal. This field is derived from the citizen_suspensions and citizen_bans tables and reflects the most severe active status.

This field is derived from the citizen_suspensions and citizen_bans tables and reflects the most severe active status.
