id.description:
Unique identifier for the status update record.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key in the discussion_board_article_status_logs table, ensuring each status change has a distinct, auditable record.

Used to track the entire history of an article's status changes and provides a reference for moderation audit trails.

articleId.description:
The unique identifier of the article whose status was updated.

This UUID references the discussion_board_articles table and links this status update to the specific article modified.

This field is critical for associating moderation actions with content and enables reporting and analytics on article status changes by article.

oneOf.description:
The article's new publication status after the update.

This represents one of three allowed states from discussion_board_article_statuses - published, hidden, or deleted.

This change bypasses normal publication workflows and is an admin-only privileged operation recorded in discussion_board_moderation_actions.

The article's new publication status after the update.

This represents one of three allowed states from discussion_board_article_statuses - published, hidden, or deleted.

This change bypasses normal publication workflows and is an admin-only privileged operation recorded in discussion_board_moderation_actions.

The article's new publication status after the update.

This represents one of three allowed states from discussion_board_article_statuses - published, hidden, or deleted.

This change bypasses normal publication workflows and is an admin-only privileged operation recorded in discussion_board_moderation_actions.

status.description:
The article's new publication status after the update.

This represents one of three allowed states from discussion_board_article_statuses - published, hidden, or deleted.

This change bypasses normal publication workflows and is an admin-only privileged operation recorded in discussion_board_moderation_actions.

changedAt.description:
The precise timestamp when the status change was applied.

This field records the exact time (ISO 8601 UTC format) when the admin's update request was processed and the article's status was modified in the database.

Used for auditing purposes and to determine the sequence of status changes for an article.

This timestamp is automatically generated by the system server and reflects UTC time, not client time.

changedBy.description:
The unique identifier of the moderator who initiated the status change.

This UUID references the discussion_board_moderator table and identifies which admin performed this moderation action.

This field enables accountability and attribution, allowing audit trails to link each status change to the specific moderator responsible.

The value is extracted from the authenticated moderator's JWT token during request processing, not provided by the client.

IArticleStatusUpdateResult.description:
Response DTO for updating an article's status. This object contains the complete details of the status change operation performed by an admin moderator.

Used as the response body for the PUT /admin/articles/{articleId}/status endpoint.

The object provides comprehensive information about the status update, including:

- The unique ID of the status log entry
- The article affected by the change
- The new status assigned (published, hidden, or deleted)
- The exact time the change was applied
- The moderator responsible for the change

This ensures complete auditability of all content moderation actions and provides clients with immediate confirmation of the update's success.

Note: All fields are required because every status update creates an immutable audit log entry. None of these fields are optional as they form a complete, self-contained record of the moderation action.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ICreate.description:
Registration credentials and profile information required to create a new citizen account for the discussion board platform.

This schema defines the input payload for user registration and corresponds directly with the discussion_board_users database table. Each property must be provided by the user during account creation and represents a core identity field that will be stored in the system.

The user registration process creates a new citizen account that serves as the foundation for all user activity on the platform. Upon successful registration, the system generates a session token for subsequent authenticated operations, and the new user begins with a default trust score of zero. The account becomes active immediately, and users can immediately begin posting and commenting.

All fields in this schema are mandatory and represent non-nullable database columns. Additional fields such as updated_at, created_at, id, emailVerified, and trustScore are system-generated and populated automatically on creation.

After registration, this user account can participate in discussions, create articles, comment on posts, and upload media. Account features are influenced by user behavior, and violations of community guidelines can trigger moderation actions that affect the user's status and trust score.

email.description:
Unique email address for the user account. Must be a valid RFC 5322 email format and cannot be duplicated across accounts. This serves as the primary identifier for login and communication. The system performs format validation and checks uniqueness against existing accounts before registration.

Email address is used for account recovery, notifications, and communication. Required for compliance with platform registration policies.

This field is required for all registrations and must be provided by the user during account creation.

password.description:
Plain text password for authentication. The system will hash and store this securely in the database as password_hashed using bcrypt with salt. This field is required for initial registration and must meet minimum security requirements: at least 12 characters in length, containing at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character.

The system will reject weak passwords and enforce secure password creation. For security, passwords are not stored in plaintext and are never returned in responses.

Professional users should choose complex, unique passwords to prevent account compromise.

username.description:
Unique username for the citizen. Used for public identification in post authorship, comments, and profile display. Must be between 3 and 30 characters long and can only contain alphanumeric characters and underscores. No spaces or special characters are allowed.

The system enforces uniqueness, and the username cannot be changed after account creation. This field is required for all registration attempts and cannot be left blank.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for the citizen. This is the name shown publicly in posts and comments. If not provided, the username will be used as the display name. Can contain letters, numbers, spaces, and basic punctuation.

This field allows users to personalize their public identity while keeping their username secure and unique. If provided, it must be between 1 and 100 characters in length.

bio.description:
Optional biographical information about the citizen. May contain up to 500 characters of plain text describing interests, expertise, or other personal information. This field is optional and can be left empty.

When provided, the bio should be concise and appropriate for public viewing. This field is stored as plain text and will be rendered in user profiles. Profile bios contribute to community trust and can influence how users interact with the account.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new moderation action record in the system to document moderator decisions on content. This schema defines the structure of data that must be submitted to create an immutable audit trail entry for moderator actions including content removal, user warnings, suspensions, or any other moderator-defined actions against posts or comments. The operation ensures traceability and accountability by recording the moderator's ID (inferred from authentication), target content identifier, action type, reason, and timestamp.

This DTO corresponds to the discussion_board_moderation_actions database table and is critical for platform compliance and auditability. Every moderation action must be logged with full context to ensure transparency and provide evidence for appeals. The record is permanently stored in the database and cannot be deleted or modified, preserving a complete and immutable audit trail.

All moderation action requests must originate from authenticated moderators with appropriate privileges. The authentication system automatically associates the moderator's identity with the audit record. The system does not allow moderation actions against other moderator accounts as a security measure. The action_type must be one of the pre-defined values: "CONTENT_REMOVAL", "USER_WARNING", "USER_SUSPENSION", "DEACTIVATION", "CONTENT_RESTORE", or "CONFLICT_RESOLUTION".

IDiscussionBoardActivityLog.IRequest.description:
Filters, sorting options, and pagination parameters for activity log queries.

This request schema defines the parameters for querying activity logs in the discussion board system, supporting comprehensive filtering, sorting, and pagination functionality. It is used exclusively with the PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/activity-logs endpoint to retrieve audit records for system monitoring, compliance audits, and moderation reviews.

The schema enables granular control over result sets by allowing filtering by actor role, activity type, and date range. It supports sorting by multiple fields including timestamp, actor_id, activity type, and target resource identifier. Pagination is fully implemented with configurable page sizes and supports retrieving results in ascending or descending order.

This request structure follows the system's consistent pattern for search and filter operations, ensuring compatibility with the system's layered security model where moderators can access detailed audit trails while citizens are limited to specific views.

All parameters in this schema are optional except for actorType, activityType, sortBy, and sortOrder, which form the core filtering criteria.

Note on validation: While the schema defines constraints, actual enforcement is handled at the service layer to ensure optimal performance and flexibility in query execution.

This object is designed to be used in the context of the activity_logs table and its associated audit trail system, which records every significant system event from user actions to administrative decisions.

actorType.description: The type of actor who performed the activity. Must be one of: 'user', 'moderator', or 'system'. This filters activity logs by the actor's role in the system.

activityType.description: The type of activity that occurred. Must be one of: 'login', 'post', 'remove', 'warn', 'ban', 'comment', 'reply', 'report', 'appeal', 'notification', 'configuration', 'security', or 'audit'. This filters logs by the specific action performed.

startDate.description: The start of the time period to filter logs by. This is an inclusive boundary for filtering, meaning logs from this exact timestamp will be included. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

endDate.description: The end of the time period to filter logs by. This is an inclusive boundary for filtering, meaning logs up to and including this exact timestamp will be included. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

sortBy.description: The field to sort the results by. Must be one of: 'timestamp', 'actor_id', 'activityType', or 'targetId'. This determines how the paginated results are ordered.

sortOrder.description: The direction to sort the results. Must be either 'asc' for ascending order or 'desc' for descending order. This works in conjunction with sortBy to determine result ordering.

page.description: The page number to retrieve. Pagination is 1-indexed, meaning the first page is page 1 and subsequent pages follow incrementally from there. This parameter controls which chunk of results is returned.

limit.description: The maximum number of records to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100 items. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest boundary. This controls the density of information in each response.

includeDetails.description: Whether to include detailed information in the responses. When false, only summary information is returned for performance optimization. When true, additional context and metadata are included in the results.

filterByHashtags.description: An array of hashtag strings to filter activities by. Activities with any of these hashtags in their associated description field will be included in results. For example, filtering by ['#politician','accountability'] will return activities mentioning either hashtag. Hashtags are case-insensitive and must follow the pattern #keyword.

searchTerm.description: A text string to search within activity descriptions. This performs a case-insensitive, substring match against the description field of activity logs. Partial matches are returned, making it useful for finding activities related to specific topics, events, or actor names.

targetId.description: Identifier of the resource targeted by the activity. This filters log entries by the specific entity affected by the action, identified by its unique identifier. For example, if filtering for activities related to a specific article, this would contain the UUID of that article. Must be a valid UUID v4 format.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the moderator action record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the discussion_board_moderator_actions table and uniquely identifies each moderation event.

Used to reference this specific action in audit trails, appeal cases, and system logs. This identifier remains immutable after creation.

Each action in the moderation system, whether content removal, user suspension, or warning issuance, is assigned a unique ID to ensure precise tracking and accountability.

action.description:
Type of moderation action performed.

Specifies the specific moderation action taken by the moderator.

Possible values include: "remove_content", "suspend_account", "warn_user", "approve_appeal", "dismiss_report", or "restore_content".

This field is critical for categorizing actions and generating statistical reports on moderation patterns. It indicates the nature of the intervention, not just that moderation occurred.

reason.description:
Detailed explanation for the moderation action.

A human-readable description of why this specific moderation action was taken.

This field must include the policy violation cited, evidence observed, and any additional context the moderator deems relevant.

While the action field categorizes the type of intervention, this field provides the substantiating rationale. It ensures transparency in moderation decisions and provides necessary context for appeals.

Minimum length: 10 characters. Maximum length: 2000 characters.

target_id.description:
Identifier of the target entity affected by the moderation action.

References the content, user, or other system entity that was subject to the moderation decision.

The target can be:
- A user ID (for account suspensions or warnings)
- A post/article ID (for content removal)
- A comment ID (for comment moderation)
- A report ID (for dismissal or approval of reports)

The actual database table associated with this ID depends on the action type. This field enables correlation between actions and targeted content.

For system-level actions (like user bans), this may reference the citizen ID.

target_type.description:
Type of entity targeted by the moderation action.

Specifies the database entity type that the moderation action was applied to.

Possible values:
- "citizen" (user account)
- "article" (discussion board post)
- "comment" (user comment)
- "report" (user-generated report)
- "attachment" (file or image attachment)
- "channel" (content category)

This field, combined with target_id, uniquely identifies the target entity in the system. It ensures that different types of entities can be targeted with consistent moderation protocols.

actor_id.description:
Identifier of the moderator who performed the action.

References the user account of the moderator responsible for this moderation decision.

This field links the action to the specific moderator account, ensuring accountability within the moderation system.

The actor is always a user with "moderator" role - standard users cannot perform these actions.

timestamp.description:
Date and time when the moderation action was executed.

Represents the exact moment when the moderation decision was applied to the system.

This is a server-generated timestamp, eliminating any possibility of client tampering.

Used for:
- Establishing chronological order in audit trails
- Calculating moderation frequency and response times
- Correlating with user activity patterns
- Determining eligibility for appeals based on time windows

Follows ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone.

status.description:
Current status of the moderation action.

Denotes whether the action has been applied, pending, or reversed.

Possible values:
- "applied" (action has been executed)
- "pending" (action in queue, awaiting execution)
- "reversed" (action has been appealed and overturned)
- "expired" (temporary restriction has expired)

In most cases, the status will be "applied". The "reversed" status is critical for appeal cases, indicating that a moderator's decision has been overruled by a higher authority or automated system.

has_appeal.description:
Indicates whether an appeal has been filed against this moderation action.

If true, a user has formally challenged this moderation decision through the appeals process.

Appeals are an important part of our moderation system's transparency and fairness mechanism.

When true, this action record must be linked to an appeal record in the discussion_board_appeals table.

This boolean flag allows filter searches for potentially controversial or contested moderation decisions.

is_system_generated.description:
Denotes whether this action was initiated by automated systems rather than a human moderator.

If true, allows the moderation system to autonomously act on violations without direct human review.

Used for:
- Automatically deleting content that violates explicit, unambiguous policies
- Enforcing suspension thresholds (e.g., after 5 report activations)
- Flagging accounts with high-risk behavior patterns

Automated actions are subject to enhanced review protocols. Even when auto-generated, the action is logged for accountability and can still be appealed.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorAction.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a moderator action on the discussion board platform.

A lightweight view of moderation activities designed for display in audit logs, reporting dashboards, and administrative interfaces.

This summary type provides essential information about moderation actions to administrators and moderators without exposing sensitive contextual data or detailed content of actions.

It focuses on the key facts: who performed which action on what target, when, and with what result.

This schema is used in paginated responses for the moderation logs endpoint (/discussionBoard/moderator/moderation-logs), enabling administrators to quickly assess moderation activity across the entire platform without retrieving full audit data for each case.

The summary keeps response sizes small for efficient querying of large datasets - when detailed information is required, the complete action record can be accessed through the individual action endpoint.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the discussion board channel.

Each channel is assigned a universally unique identifier (UUID) upon creation, ensuring global uniqueness across distributed systems. This ID is used as the primary key in the database and as the reference in all related operations.

The ID remains immutable throughout the channel's lifecycle and is used in all API endpoints to identify the specific channel, such as in GET /discussionBoard/channels/{channelId} requests.

This field is required for all operations that interact with a specific channel and is always included in response payloads.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the discussion board channel.

This field contains the display name that users see when browsing channels. It must be unique within the system to avoid ambiguity and provide clear identification for users.

The name is used for filtering and searching channels and forms the primary basis for channel organization in the UI. It should be descriptive enough to convey the channel's purpose while remaining concise for display purposes.

This field is subject to length constraints to ensure consistent display across all interfaces and to prevent technical issues with URL encoding or database indexing.

description.description:
Detailed description of the discussion board channel's purpose and rules.

This field provides additional context about the channel's intended use, topic focus, community guidelines, and any special rules or expectations for participants. It is displayed to users when they view the channel details.

Longer descriptions allow for comprehensive guidance on community norms, while shorter descriptions are suitable for broad categories. This field may be moderated to ensure compliance with platform policies and should maintain professional, inclusive language.

category.description:
The category to which this channel belongs.

This is a reference to an independent entity (category) that provides hierarchical organization for channels. Categories group related channels together (e.g., "Technology", "Arts", "Support").

When a channel is displayed in a list or search result, the category reference provides immediate context about the channel's purpose and helps users understand its place in the broader system structure.

This field replaces the category_id foreign key field from the database, following the requirement to transform all association foreign keys to object references with .ISummary in Response DTOs.

parent_channel.description:
The parent channel in a hierarchical structure.

This is a reference to another channel that serves as a parent in a nested organization system, where some channels can be organized under other channels (e.g., "General Discussion" -> "Off-topic" -> "Random chat").

When a child channel is displayed in a list or search result, having a reference to its parent provides valuable context about its position in the hierarchy and helps users understand its relationship to broader channels.

This field replaces the parent_channel_id foreign key field from the database, following the requirement to transform all association foreign keys to object references with .ISummary in Response DTOs.

is_public.description:
Whether the channel is accessible to all users or requires special privileges.

Public channels are visible to all authenticated users and can be joined without special permissions. Private channels require explicit authorization to view or participate in and are typically used for moderated discussions, private groups, or sensitive topics.

This boolean flag controls the access control logic in the system and determines whether users can discover the channel through search or listing operations. Public channels appear in general channel directories while private channels require direct links or invitations.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the channel is currently available for new discussions.

Active channels can receive new posts, comments, and interactions. Inactive channels are archived but not deleted, preserving historical content while preventing new activity. This allows for temporary suspensions without losing conversation history.

Inactive status is used for channels that are under review, temporarily closed for maintenance, or being phased out. This differs from deletion, as content remains accessible for moderation and archival purposes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the channel was created in the system.

This field records the exact date and time when the channel was first established, providing a chronological record of the platform's development. It is automatically set by the server when the channel is created and cannot be modified by clients.

The created_at field is used for sorting channels chronologically, calculating channel age for analytics, and establishing the order of channel creation in administrative interfaces.

color.description:
The hexadecimal color code used for visual identification of this channel.

Each channel can be assigned a unique color that appears in the UI as a visual indicator (e.g., background, border, or icon accent). This helps users quickly recognize and distinguish between channels in lists and navigation menus.

The color is stored as a standard 6-digit hexadecimal code (e.g., "#FF5733") and must follow the CSS color syntax. It is used in conjunction with channel icons to create a distinctive visual identity for each community. The color does not affect functionality, only user experience.

icon.description:
URI to a visual icon representing this channel.

This field points to an image resource that serves as the channel's icon in UI displays. The icon provides immediate visual identification of the channel's purpose or theme (e.g., a book icon for literature, a gear for technology).

The icon must be a publicly accessible URI (e.g., CDN URL) to a valid image file format (PNG, JPG, SVG). This field supports custom branding and community identity. When null, a system default icon is used.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board channel optimized for list displays and overview views.

This DTO provides a lightweight version of the channel entity suitable for displaying in channel directories, search results, and overview pages. It includes essential information about the channel without including potentially large or computationally expensive data like recent posts or member lists.

The ISummary variant is used in paginated responses (IPageIDiscussionBoardChannel.ISummary) and ensures efficient data transmission for list views where full detail is not necessary. Fields included are carefully selected to support fast rendering, easy categorization, and quick identification of active and relevant channels, while excluding fields that would increase payload size or require additional database joins. All fields in this schema are sourced from the discussion_board_channels database table. The channel entity maintains relationships with categories (IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary) and parent channels (IDiscussionBoardChannel.ISummary) through references. The is_active and is_public fields control visibility and access, while the updated_at field helps track changes. Additional metrics (member_count, post_count, last_activity_at) provide engagement insights, and the color and icon fields enhance visual identification in user interfaces.

IDiscussionBoardArchive.IUpdate.description:
Update request for archived discussion board articles. This schema defines the fields that can be modified for archived article records in the discussion_board_archives table.

Archived articles are immutable historical copies of previously published articles that have been removed from public view, typically due to moderation actions, policy violations, or content updates. This update operation permits authorized moderators to modify the archive record itself - for example, to add a moderation note explaining why the article was archived, update the reason code, change the archive timestamp, or correct metadata. Importantly, this is not a restoration operation - the original article record remains unchanged and the article stays archived.

These updates maintain audit integrity while allowing necessary corrections to archival metadata. The archive record contains sensitive information about moderation decisions, making strict access control critical. Only users with moderator privileges can perform these updates.

This schema is used specifically for update operations (PUT /discussionBoard/moderator/archives/{archiveId}) and follows the principle of partial updates where only specific fields can be modified. The archivalVersion field ensures proper tracking of metadata revisions, while archivalNote provides detailed context that may be referenced during appeals or compliance investigations.

reasonCode.description: Code identifying the specific policy violation or reason for archiving the article. This standardized code helps with reporting, analytics, and consistent moderation practices across the platform. Must be one of the approved moderation reason codes defined in system configuration: 'policy_violation', 'dead_content', 'repost', 'user_request', 'legal_compliance', 'copyright_violation', 'spam_content', 'harassment'. This field enables automated analytics on moderation patterns and ensures consistent application of community guidelines.

archivalVersion.description:
Version number of this archival record.

This sequential number tracks revisions to the archived record itself (not the original content). Each time the archived record is updated (e.g., adding an archival note, changing legal hold status), the version number is incremented.

This ensures an audit trail of changes to the archival metadata while preserving the original content as immutable. The version starts at 1 when the archive record is initially created and is incremented with every subsequent update to the archive record metadata.

url.description: The full URL to the thumbnail image file. Must be a valid, accessible URI pointing to the thumbnail asset in storage.

filename.description: Original filename of the thumbnail image. Used for display and metadata purposes. Must contain only allowed characters and not exceed 255 characters.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the thumbnail file, indicating its format (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png). Must be a valid MIME type from the supported list of thumbnail formats.

IDiscussionBoardThumbnail.IUpdate.description: Request payload for updating an existing thumbnail record in the discussion_board_thumbnails table. This DTO specifies the fields that may be modified during an update operation. All fields are optional except for url, filename, and mimeType which are required to ensure the thumbnail remains valid. The thumbnailId is provided as a path parameter and should not be included in this body. This schema follows the update pattern where only the fields being changed need to be provided, and all other fields retain their existing values.

caption.description:
A brief title or summary describing the activity log entry. This field may be updated to provide clearer context about the activity being recorded.

The caption is optional and allows moderators to provide more descriptive context when correcting or refining log entries for audit purposes. It should be descriptive enough to convey the nature of the activity without being overly verbose.

Note: This field corresponds to the 'caption' column in the discussion_board_activity_logs table, which is defined as a nullable string field.

object.description:
The type of object being acted upon in this activity log entry.

This field identifies the nature of the target object involved in the activity, such as 'article', 'comment', 'user', or 'report'. It helps categorize the activity for filtering, reporting, and monitoring purposes.

The object field is optional and may be updated when the target context changes or becomes more accurately specified. This field corresponds to the 'object' column in the discussion_board_activity_logs table, which is defined as a nullable string field.

details.description:
Detailed textual information about the specific activity that occurred.

This field provides comprehensive context about the nature of the log entry, including any relevant metadata, changes made, or specific circumstances surrounding the activity. It may include structured information about actions taken or values changed.

The details field is optional and is used to record comprehensive information when a moderator revises or provides additional context about an activity log entry. This corresponds to the 'details' column in the discussion_board_activity_logs table, which is defined as a nullable string field.

comment.description:
A moderator's explanatory note regarding the change to the activity log entry.

This field allows moderators to document the reason for updating the log entry, such as correcting erroneous information, clarifying ambiguous context, or explaining regulatory compliance requirements.

While optional, this field is strongly encouraged for audit trail completeness. It corresponds to the 'comment' column in the discussion_board_activity_logs table, which is defined as a nullable string field.

IDiscussionBoardActivityLog.IUpdate.description:
Update request for a discussion_board_activity_logs entry. This schema defines the optional fields that can be modified when a moderator corrects or refines an existing activity log entry.

This update schema reflects the partial nature of activity log corrections - only fields that need revision are included, preserving the immutable nature of the original audit record.

The fields are all optional, reflecting that a moderator may choose to update none, one, or multiple properties in a single operation based on the specific correction needed.

This structure supports a flexible audit framework where activity logs remain complete and immutable records, while allowing for contextual refinement when necessary.

This schema maps directly to the discussion_board_activity_logs database table, which includes fields for caption (nullable string), object (nullable string), details (nullable string), and comment (nullable string) that correspond to each of the properties defined in this update request.

url.description: The full URL to the thumbnail image file. Must be a valid, accessible URI pointing to the thumbnail asset in storage.

IDiscussionBoardThumbnail.description: Request payload for updating an existing thumbnail record in the discussion_board_thumbnails table. This DTO specifies the fields that may be modified during an update operation. All fields are optional except for url which is required to ensure the thumbnail remains valid. The thumbnailId is provided as a path parameter and should not be included in this body. This schema follows the update pattern where only the fields being changed need to be provided, and all other fields retain their existing values.

id.description: Unique identifier for the citizen account. This UUIDv4 value is the primary key in the discussion_board_citizen database table and is used to reference this citizen across all related entities and operations.

username.description: The citizen's chosen display name or handle used within the discussion board. This field is unique across the platform and serves as the primary identifier for interactions. Minimum 3 characters, maximum 50 characters.

oneOf.description: The current status of the citizen account within the platform's moderation system. Valid values are 'active' (standard access), 'suspended' (temporary access restriction), or 'banned' (permanent access restriction). This status determines the citizen's ability to interact with the platform.

The current status of the citizen account within the platform's moderation system. Valid values are 'active' (standard access), 'suspended' (temporary access restriction), or 'banned' (permanent access restriction). This status determines the citizen's ability to interact with the platform.

account_status.description: The current status of the citizen account within the platform's moderation system. Valid values are 'active' (standard access), 'suspended' (temporary access restriction), or 'banned' (permanent access restriction). This status determines the citizen's ability to interact with the platform.

IDiscussionBoardCitizen.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary representation of a citizen's profile for display in lists and search results. This DTO provides essential information for community navigation and moderation oversight without exposing sensitive or detailed account information. Primarily used in paginated citizen lists (IPageIDiscussionBoardCitizen.ISummary) and when granting moderation teams quick visibility into citizen reputation metrics. Fields are carefully selected to balance transparency with privacy, omitting contact details like email in some contexts and focusing on reputation indicators and moderation history.

IDiscussionBoardThumbnail.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a system-generated thumbnail used to optimize visual rendering in client interfaces.

Thumbnails are automatically created by the system from article image attachments, scaled to 150px width while preserving aspect ratio. They serve as lightweight visual preview assets for article listings, search results, category feeds, and recommendation engines.

All thumbnail data is derived and immutable - users cannot upload, modify, or delete thumbnails directly. Access is restricted to users with read permission to the associated article.

This summary type excludes complex relationships and nested objects to minimize payload size for high-volume read operations.

When displayed: Thumbnails appear next to article titles in list views. If the article is hidden or deleted, the thumbnail won't appear even if it exists in storage.

Usage context: Mobile clients use thumbnail metadata (fileSize, original dimensions) to optimize image loading and caching strategies. Desktop clients use aspect ratio data for responsive layout calculations.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the thumbnail record.

A system-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this thumbnail instance. Used for caching, direct access, and internal referencing within the platform.

url.description:
Public URL to access the generated thumbnail image from CDN or storage service.

This is a fully-qualified HTTP(S) URL pointing to the thumbnail resource. When accessed, the thumbnail is served with appropriate content headers and caching directives for optimal client-side rendering.

The thumbnail is generated as a compressed PNG optimized for web delivery at 150px width, preserving aspect ratio from the original image. Access is subject to the same permissions as the parent article.

Example: "https://cdn.discussionboard.com/thumbnails/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8.png"

fileSize.description:
Size of the thumbnail file in bytes, used for bandwidth and caching optimization.

Represents the actual file size on storage after compression and optimization. Helps with bandwidth calculations and CDN cache strategy decisions.

Typical values range from 1,000 bytes (minimal graphics) to 15,000 bytes (complex images), with an average around 6,000 bytes.

This value is critical for mobile clients who need to manage data usage and for systems performing usage analytics.

originalWidth.description:
Width of the source image in pixels before thumbnail generation.

This represents the width of the original image file uploaded by the user, not the thumbnail itself. This metadata allows clients to understand the aspect ratio that was preserved during thumbnail generation.

Crucial for layout systems that need to reserve appropriate space even before the image loads.

Valid range: 1 to 10000 pixels.

originalHeight.description:
Height of the source image in pixels before thumbnail generation.

This represents the height of the original image file uploaded by the user, not the thumbnail itself. Combined with originalWidth, this provides the source aspect ratio.

Used by client applications to maintain visual consistency in layout and to potentially provide "view original" functionality.

Valid range: 1 to 10000 pixels.

mimeType.description:
MIME type of the generated thumbnail, typically 'image/png' for optimized output.

Indicates the file format of the thumbnail image served at the URL.

The system generates thumbnails as PNG files with optimized compression for web delivery, even when the source image was JPG or GIF.

Values may include:
- "image/png" (99% of cases)
- "image/jpeg" (rare cases with specific quality requirements)
- "image/webp" (experimental, for supported platforms)

Clients should use this value to set correct Content-Type headers when serving the image.

uploadTimestamp.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the thumbnail was generated and stored by the system.

This is not the upload time of the original image, but rather the timestamp when the system processed it and created the thumbnail version.

This allows clients to implement freshness checks and cache invalidation strategies. Thumbnails are generated asynchronously after image upload, typically within 1-5 seconds.

Used for sorting in chronological views and for identifying the most recent thumbnail versions.

Example: "2026-01-09T12:45:30.123Z"

articleId.description:
Reference to the parent article ID to which this thumbnail is associated. This is a non-nullable foreign key that links the thumbnail to its originating article content.

The thumbnail is derived directly from an image attachment to a specific article and represents a processed version of that content.

This association is fundamental: Each thumbnail must be linked to exactly one article, and the thumbnail's visibility is inherited from the article's status (published, hidden, deleted). Thumbnails of hidden or deleted articles are never returned in responses.

This metadata enables efficient querying - clients can fetch all thumbnails for an article by its ID without needing to fetch the article itself first.

Any attempt to reference a thumbnail without a valid articleId will result in the thumbnail being considered orphaned and is filtered out by the system.

status.description: The new publication status of the article. This field must be consistent with the defined article status types in the discussion_board_article_statuses table. Updates to this field trigger corresponding audit logs and may affect content visibility to users. Valid values include: 'draft', 'pending', 'published', 'hidden', 'deleted'.

reason.description: A detailed explanation for the status change, providing context and justification for the action taken. This should include the specific reason for the status update, such as policy violation, technical error, or editorial decision. This field supports up to 500 characters of text and is used for compliance records and appeal processes.

notes.description: Internal administrative notes about the status change that are not visible to users. These notes may include information about supporting evidence, communication with the content owner, or next steps in the moderation workflow. This field supports up to 1000 characters of text and is used for internal audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardStatusLog.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing status log entry in the discussion board system. This DTO contains the updated information for a specific status log identified by its unique logId in the path parameters. The update operation allows administrators to correct or modify status information when discrepancies arise between the system record and actual event outcomes.

This status update affects the article's visibility and accessibility within the platform, triggering notification systems and potentially initiating further moderation actions. The update must include complete and accurate information reflecting the current state to ensure audit trail integrity and accurate system state representation.

Note: The logId parameter in the path is automatically extracted from the URL and mapped to the correct status log entry in the database. This update does NOT create new status logs but modifies existing ones, with the entire change history preserved in the discussion_board_moderation_audit_trails table. The moderator_id field is NOT included in this request body - it is automatically extracted from the authenticated user's JWT token by the server for security and audit purposes. This field is essential for compliance and audit purposes, as it links every modification to the specific moderator responsible for the action. The moderatorId is required in the response to maintain traceability while remaining excluded from client input to prevent spoofing or tampering. This ensures system-wide integrity of the

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. This parameter controls which 1-100 record slice of the audit log is returned for efficient navigation through large datasets.

Essential for audit trail monitoring and compliance reporting, as it enables reviewers to traverse historical events incrementally without overwhelming system resources. Every request must include a valid page number to ensure predictable and scalable access to legacy data.

limit.description:
Number of records per page. Must be between 1 and 100 to prevent excessive resource usage.

This parameter balances performance and usability by restricting batch sizes for the discussion_board_status_logs table. Values below 1 are invalid and will cause validation errors. Values above 100 are prohibited due to potential performance degradation and system integrity risks.

Recommended use: 25 records per page for general monitoring, 50 for investigative reviews, and 100 for bulk data exports.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Allows sorting by timestamp (most recent first), statusType (change type), entityType (type of affected entity), or affectedEntityId (specific entity identifier).
Field to sort results by. Allows sorting by timestamp (most recent first), statusType (change type), entityType (type of affected entity), or affectedEntityId (specific entity identifier).
Field to sort results by. Allows sorting by timestamp (most recent first), statusType (change type), entityType (type of affected entity), or affectedEntityId (specific entity identifier).
Field to sort results by. Allows sorting by timestamp (most recent first), statusType (change type), entityType (type of affected entity), or affectedEntityId (specific entity identifier).

sortBy.description:
Field to sort results by. Allows sorting by timestamp (most recent first), statusType (change type), entityType (type of affected entity), or affectedEntityId (specific entity identifier).

Determines the sequence in which audit logs are returned. This enables investigators to prioritize recent events (timestamp) or group similar types of actions together (statusType or entityType).

- timestamp: Chronological order with newest events first (default)
- statusType: Group by type of change (e.g., all 'published', 'hidden', 'deleted', 'suspended' events)
- entityType: Group by target type (e.g., all 'article', 'comment', 'user' changes)
- affectedEntityId: Group by specific entity (e.g., all changes to article 'abc123')

Used in forensic investigations, compliance audits, and real-time monitoring systems.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is 'desc'.
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is 'desc'.

order.description:
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is 'desc'.

Defines the sequencing of ordered results based on the sortBy parameter:

- asc (ascending): Oldest events appear first in results
- desc (descending): Newest events appear first in results

Audit operations typically use 'desc' to focus on recent activities, while retrospective compliance investigations may use 'asc' to analyze events chronologically from a historic starting point.

statusType.description:
Filter logs by specific status change type (e.g., 'published', 'hidden', 'deleted', 'suspended'). Case-sensitive match against system-defined status types.

This field enables targeted querying of audit logs based on the nature of the database status transition recorded in the 'status_type' column of the discussion_board_status_logs table. The value must exactly match one of the predefined system status types:

- 'published': Article or comment was made publicly visible
- 'hidden': Content was made invisible to end users (temporary removal)
- 'deleted': Content was permanently removed from the system
- 'suspended': User account access was temporarily restricted
- 'approved': Appeal or report was accepted and processed
- 'rejected': Appeal or report was denied
- 'banned': User account was permanently terminated
- 'unbanned': User account access was restored
- 'system_update': Internal system configuration change
- 'moderation': General moderation action on content
- 'auto-moderation': Automated AI-based moderation action

Only logs matching the specified status type will be returned. Multiple status types cannot be selected simultaneously - use separate queries for multiple values.

oneOf.description: Filter logs by type of entity affected by the status change. Options are: 'article', 'comment', 'user', 'attachment', or 'moderation'.
Filter logs by type of entity affected by the status change. Options are: 'article', 'comment', 'user', 'attachment', or 'moderation'.

entityType.description:
Filter logs by type of entity affected by the status change. Options are: 'article', 'comment', 'user', 'attachment', or 'moderation'.

This filter corresponds to the 'target_entity_type' column in the discussion_board_status_logs database table. It allows users to isolate audit records related to specific types of system entities:

- 'article': Status changes to discussion board articles (publication, deletion, hiding)
- 'comment': Status changes to user comments on articles
- 'user': Changes to citizen account status (suspension, ban, trust score update)
- 'attachment': Status changes to uploaded files and images associated with content
- 'moderation': System-level moderation actions that don't target a specific entity (such as configuration changes)

Used in forensic investigations to trace patterns of behavior across entity categories.

startDate.description:
Start date and time for filtering logs. Only logs with timestamp equal to or after this value are included. Must be in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

This optional filter corresponds to the 'created_at' column in the discussion_board_status_logs table. It enables temporal bounding of audit queries related to compliance investigations, data breach detection, or historical trend analysis.

Examples of valid ISO 8601 formats:
- "2026-01-09T18:00:00Z"
- "2026-01-09T18:06:13.117Z"
- "2026-01-09T18:06:13Z"

When combined with endDate, forms a precise time window for audit trail analysis. If unspecified, the system will return all logs from the earliest available record.

endDate.description:
End date and time for filtering logs. Only logs with timestamp equal to or before this value are included. Must be in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

This optional filter corresponds to the 'created_at' column in the discussion_board_status_logs table. It enables temporal bounding of audit queries related to compliance investigations, data breach detection, or historical trend analysis.

Examples of valid ISO 8601 formats:
- "2026-01-09T18:00:00Z"
- "2026-01-09T18:06:13.117Z"
- "2026-01-09T18:06:13Z"

When combined with startDate, forms a precise time window for audit trail analysis. If unspecified, the system will return all logs up to the most recent record available.

actorId.description:
Filter logs by the actor who triggered the status change. Only logs where this user performed the action are included. This is a UUID of a moderator or system actor.

This optional filter corresponds to the 'actor_id' column in the discussion_board_status_logs table. It allows administrators to audit actions performed by specific individuals:

- Moderator UUIDs: Identified through discussion_board_moderator table
- System actor: UUID for automated system processes (e.g., automated moderation)

Used for accountability tracking, privilege monitoring, and compliance reporting. When provided, only logs where the 'actor_id' matches this UUID will be returned.

affectedEntityId.description:
Filter logs by the specific entity affected by the status change. Only logs affecting this entity (article, user, etc.) are returned. This is a UUID of the target entity.

This optional filter corresponds to the 'target_entity_id' column in the discussion_board_status_logs table. It enables granular tracing of all events related to a specific object in the system:

- Article UUID: From discussion_board_articles table
- Comment UUID: From discussion_board_comments table
- User UUID: From discussion_board_citizen table
- Attachment UUID: From discussion_board_attachments table

Essential for forensic investigations, user support cases, and impact analysis. For example, querying all status changes to article "abc123" reveals its entire history of moderation actions, publication status changes, and public availability events.

oneOf.description: Filter logs by the source that triggered the status change. 'system' for automated processes, 'moderator' for manual actions, 'auto-moderation' for AI-automated moderation actions.
Filter logs by the source that triggered the status change. 'system' for automated processes, 'moderator' for manual actions, 'auto-moderation' for AI-automated moderation actions.
Filter logs by the source that triggered the status change. 'system' for automated processes, 'moderator' for manual actions, 'auto-moderation' for AI-automated moderation actions.

statusUpdateSource.description:
Filter logs by the source that triggered the status change. 'system' for automated processes, 'moderator' for manual actions, 'auto-moderation' for AI-automated moderation actions.

This field matches the 'source' column in the discussion_board_status_logs table and provides critical context for understanding the origin of each status transition:

- 'system': Internal system processes (e.g., cleanup tasks, scheduled updates)
- 'moderator': Human moderator actions via admin interface
- 'auto-moderation': AI-based automated moderation system decisions

This distinction is crucial for accountability, compliance reviews, and system analysis. For example, audit reports may require separating human actions from automated decisions to assess policy fairness and system reliability.

IDiscussionBoardStatusLog.IRequest.description:
Request body for fetching paginated and filtered status change logs from the discussion board system.

This schema defines the parameters for querying the discussion_board_status_logs table, which tracks all automated status transitions across articles, comments, users, attachments, and moderation actions. The system generates these logs for every status change including article publication, comment moderation, user suspension, and content deletion events.

The log records contain timestamps, status types, affected entity identifiers, and actor information when applicable. This request allows comprehensive filtering and sorting to support audit trails, security investigations, and platform monitoring.

Filters can be combined to narrow results to specific criteria, such as all user suspensions by a particular moderator within a date range. Pagination ensures scalability even for large audit datasets.

Security Note: Only users with moderator authorization can access these logs due to the sensitive nature of audit data. All parameters are validated server-side to prevent injection attacks and resource exhaustion.

oneOf.description:
Filter moderators by their current status.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequest.description:
Filter criteria and pagination parameters for moderator search and sorting.

This request schema defines the parameters used to filter and sort the list of moderators returned by the admin dashboard.

ModAdmins can use a combination of status filters, date ranges, activity thresholds, and sorting options to identify specific subsets of moderators for management purposes.

The parameter set allows for sophisticated queries that return only relevant moderators based on multiple criteria simultaneously.

All fields except page and limit are optional - omitting them returns moderators matching default filters.

Used exclusively in the PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/moderators operation to retrieve filtered and paginated moderator lists.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the activity log entry.

Each activity log is systematically assigned a universally unique identifier (UUID) upon creation to ensure global uniqueness across all systems and time.

Used as the primary key for the discussion_board_activity_logs table, this field uniquely identifies each audit event in the system.

This UUID is generated by the system and cannot be overridden by clients.

This field is automatically populated by the database system and is immutable after creation.

actor_id.description:
Identifier of the actor who performed the action.

References the user or system entity that initiated the logged activity.

This field connects the activity log to the citizen, moderator, or system account responsible for the action.

For system-generated events, this typically references the system's internal account identifier.

The actor_id value is derived from the authenticated session and cannot be modified by clients.

This field is essential for accountability and audit trail completeness.

Note: In all request DTOs (ICreate, IUpdate), this field is excluded from the payload since it is automatically determined from the authentication context of the requester.

action_type.description:
Type of activity performed.

Represents the specific category or classification of the logged event.

Predefined system actions include: "article_created", "article_published", "article_deleted", "article_reported", "comment_created", "comment_reported", "comment_deleted", "moderation_action", "login", "logout", "account_suspended", "account_banned", "session_created", "system_maintenance", and "configuration_changed".

This field enables granular filtering of audit logs by action category and is used in compliance reporting.

The values are standardized across the system to ensure consistent interpretation and analysis of activities.

Note: This field does not represent the raw database column name (which might be action_name) but the conceptual action type.

target_type.description:
Type of resource targeted by the activity.

Identifies the category of entity affected by the action.

Common target types include: "article", "comment", "user", "attachment", "category", "channel", "moderation_action", "configuration", and "system".

This field enables efficient indexing and filtering of activity logs by targeted resource type.

Together with target_id, it forms a complete reference to the affected entity, even if that entity is later deleted or modified in the system.

The target_type provides context for interpreting the target_id value.

target_id.description:
Identifier of the resource targeted by the activity.

References the specific entity affected by the logged action, identified by its unique identifier.

For example, if the action_type is "article_reported", this field would contain the UUID of the reported article.

If the action targets a user account, this would contain the user_id of the affected citizen or moderator.

This field, combined with target_type, provides a complete, immutable reference to the entity affected by the action, even after the entity itself may be deleted or modified.

The target_id value must align with the target_type - a target_type of "article" must reference an existing article_id, etc.

Note: This field is automatically populated by the system and is never included in request bodies.

description.description:
Human-readable explanation of the activity.

Provides a concise, standardized text description of what action occurred and why.

This field includes summary information about the event, such as "User reported article for spam content" or "Moderator removed comment for violating community guidelines".

The description is generated by the system based on the action_type, actor_id, and target entities to ensure consistency in audit records.

This field is intended for human review and audit purposes, providing context beyond the technical fields.

It is not used for machine processing of audit logs but is crucial for investigating incidents.

metadata.description:
Structured additional context about the activity.

This object contains optional but highly valuable metadata that provides additional context about the logged event.

It includes fields such as IP address, user agent, and referrer that capture technical details about the client interaction.

This structured approach allows for flexible inclusion of new metadata fields in the future while maintaining a consistent structure for known fields.

All properties in this object are optional, meaning the object may be empty if no additional metadata is available.

This metadata is automatically collected by the system at the time of action and cannot be modified by clients. It is crucial for forensic analysis and security investigations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the activity log entry was created.

The exact date and time when the event was recorded in the system.

This field uses ISO 8601 format with timezone (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to provide precise chronological ordering of events.

The timestamp is automatically generated by the system server at the moment the event is logged and cannot be overridden by clients.

This field is critical for audit trail integrity, performance monitoring, compliance reporting, and court-admissible evidence.

The created_at field is considered the definitive time of the event and should be used for all time-based analysis of the activity log.

is_system_generated.description:
Indicates whether the activity was automatically generated by the system or triggered by a user action.

A value of true means the activity was created by system processes (scheduled jobs, automated moderation, system health checks, etc.) whereas false indicates a citizen or moderator initiated the action through the user interface or API.

This field distinguishes between human-initiated activities (for accountability) and automated system events (for monitoring system behavior).

System-generated activities are typically not shown to end users in activity feeds but are still logged for operational auditing.

This field is set automatically upon creation based on the context of the action originating from an authenticated user session or an automated system process.

IDiscussionBoardActivityLog.description:
Activity log entry representing a documented system event.

The IDiscussionBoardActivityLog type represents a single, immutable audit trail entry in the discussion board system, capturing every significant user and system action.

This entity serves as the foundational architecture for platform transparency, user accountability, regulatory compliance, and forensic analysis.

Each activity log entry systematically records: who performed the action (actor_id), what action was taken (action_type), what resource was affected (target_type and target_id), when it occurred (created_at), why it occurred (description), and the technical context (metadata).

Activity logs are designed to be append-only and immutable by default, ensuring the integrity of the audit trail.

The system creates these entries automatically in response to user actions (comments, posts, reports) and system events (moderation actions, configuration changes, authentication events).

Disclosure Rules:
- Citizen users can only view activity logs related to their own actions or reports they've filed.
- Moderators can access all activity logs within their jurisdiction.
- Regulatory review for legal compliance requires full access regardless of user role.

The entity's serialization excludes any sensitive personal information not directly required for auditing (e.g., the full session token, passwords, or authentication credentials). While targeted resources like article titles or comment content may be referenced via their IDs, the entities themselves are not embedded as arrays to prevent circular references and excessive payload size.

This schema is used for:
- Response body of GET /discussionBoard/citizen/activity-logs/{logId}
- Response body of GET /discussionBoard/moderator/activity-logs/{logId}
- Response body of POST /discussionBoard/moderator/activity-logs
- Response body of PUT /discussionBoard/moderator/activity-logs/{logId}

The associated models in the database system (discussion_board_activity_logs) define the source of truth for this type. This schema directly maps to this table's structure, ensuring full data integrity between the API and persistence layer.

IDiscussionBoardCitizen.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for citizen filtering.

This schema defines the query structure used to retrieve filtered and paginated lists of citizens from the discussion board system. It enables advanced search operations on the discussion_board_citizen table by providing parameters for textual matching, status filtering, reputation thresholds, date ranges, and sorting preferences.

Used exclusively with the PATCH /discussionBoard/citizens endpoint for administrative, moderation, and user discovery workflows. This is a read-filtering schema (not a data creation schema), so all properties are optional, and its purpose is to specify search criteria rather than define data structure.

Critical for platform scalability: Without these filtering parameters, listing millions of citizens would impose unsustainable load on the database and client interfaces. The pagination and filtering design ensures the system remains performant as the user base grows.

username.description:
Partial username match for searching citizens. Accepts substrings within the username field for flexible search.

Used to find citizens by partial name matching when exact username is unknown.

Example: Searching with "john" will match "john_doe", "johnson123", and "john_smith". This supports moderation workflows where administrators need to find accounts based on partial identifiers without knowing full usernames.

oneOf.description: Filter citizens by account status. Valid values: 'active', 'suspended', 'banned'. Used to find citizens with specific moderation states for administrative review.
Filter citizens by account status. Valid values: 'active', 'suspended', 'banned'. Used to find citizens with specific moderation states for administrative review.
Filter citizens by account status. Valid values: 'active', 'suspended', 'banned'. Used to find citizens with specific moderation states for administrative review.

status.description:
Filter citizens by account status.

Valid values: 'active' (standard access), 'suspended' (temporary access restriction), or 'banned' (permanent access restriction).

This filter is essential for moderation teams to identify citizens requiring attention based on their current access level status. Used in compliance audits to identify suspended/banned users for further review.

minTrustScore.description:
Minimum trust score threshold for citizen filtering.

Filters citizens to those with trust scores equal to or above this value.

Trust scores range from 0 to 100, where 0 represents new users with no reputation and 100 represents highly trusted users with long histories of positive contributions.

Example: Setting to 75 finds citizens with good reputations who have consistently produced valuable content and received minimal moderation actions.

maxTrustScore.description:
Maximum trust score threshold for citizen filtering.

Filters citizens to those with trust scores equal to or below this value.

Trust scores range from 0 to 100, where 0 represents new users with no reputation and 100 represents highly trusted users with long histories of positive contributions.

Example: Setting to 50 finds citizens with average or lower reputations who may need additional review.

minRegistrationDate.description:
Earliest registration date for citizen filtering.

Filters citizens who registered on or after this date.

Use ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ) for date-time specification to ensure consistent parsing across systems.

Example: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" finds citizens registered since January 1, 2024. Useful for onboarding audits and analyzing user growth trends.

maxRegistrationDate.description:
Latest registration date for citizen filtering.

Filters citizens who registered on or before this date.

Use ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ) for date-time specification to ensure consistent parsing across systems.

Example: "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z" finds citizens registered before the end of 2024. Useful for cohort analysis by year of registration.

oneOf.description: Field to sort citizens by in the result set. Valid values: 'username', 'registrationDate', 'trustScore', 'status'. Determines which property the citizen list is organized by before pagination.
Field to sort citizens by in the result set. Valid values: 'username', 'registrationDate', 'trustScore', 'status'. Determines which property the citizen list is organized by before pagination.

sortBy.description:
Field to sort citizens by in the result set.

Valid values: 'username' (alphabetical order), 'registrationDate' (chronological), 'trustScore' (reputation ranking), or 'status' (moderation state).

This parameter determines the primary sort order of results before pagination is applied. Sorting by trustScore is recommended for moderation dashboards to prioritize users needing review.

oneOf.description: Sorting order for the result set. Valid values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Determines whether results are ordered from lowest to highest or highest to lowest based on the sortBy field.

Sorting order for the result set. Valid values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Determines whether results are ordered from lowest to highest or highest to lowest based on the sortBy field.

sortOrder.description:
Sorting order for the result set.

Valid values: 'asc' (ascending) and 'desc' (descending).

For username: asc = A-Z, desc = Z-A
For registrationDate: asc = oldest first, desc = newest first
For trustScore: asc = lowest reputation first, desc = highest reputation first
For status: asc = active, suspended, banned; desc = banned, suspended, active

When sorting by reputation (trustScore): prefer 'desc' to surface highly trusted users first
When searching for problematic accounts: prefer 'asc' to list SUSPENDED and BANNED users first

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

Specifies which page of results to return when the citizen list is divided into pages.

Pagination helps manage large result sets by returning a limited number of citizens per page, preventing performance degradation on the server and reducing network bandwidth usage for clients.

Example: page=2 returns citizens 21-40 when limit=20. Page numbers must be 1 or higher to avoid confusion in client interfaces. Page 0 has no business meaning in this system.

limit.description:
Number of citizens to return per page.

Controls the size of each pagination chunk.

Typical values range from 10 to 100 to balance performance and usability. Values outside this range can impact server performance.

Example: limit=25 returns 25 citizens per page. 

Performance considerations: 
- Below 5: Increases HTTP request overhead
- Above 100: Increases database load and response time
- Above 200: May exceed system limits

Best practice: Use 25-50 for most use cases

id.description:
Unique identifier for the attachment record.

This is the primary key in the discussion_board_attachments database table. Generated automatically upon creation and used for all reference relationships with other entities like articles, comments, and moderation logs.

When an attachment is created, the system assigns a UUID that remains immutable throughout its lifecycle. This ID is used in all API endpoints that interact with the attachment (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).

The format follows RFC 4122 UUIDv4 standard, ensuring global uniqueness and collision resistance.

object_id.description:
Foreign key identifying the content item this attachment is associated with.

References a record in the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, or other content tables. The exact target entity type is determined by the attachment_type field.

This field establishes the relationship between the attachment and the content it supplements. If the association is with an article, this will reference the article's ID; if with a comment, it will reference the comment's ID.

Note: If attachment is for system-level use (not content-related), this field may be NULL when the attachment_type is 'system'.

file_url.description:
Secure, time-limited URL to access the actual attachment file.

This is the fully qualified URI to the cloud-based storage (e.g., AWS S3) where the file content is hosted. The URL is generated after successful upload and valid for a defined period (typically 24 hours).

Clients must not attempt to generate or modify this URL. It should only be retrieved through this API and used to download the file directly. The URL is automatically refreshed by the system after expiry if the attachment is still active and the user has appropriate permissions.

Encoding: Uses standard URI format with proper escaping of special characters. All URLs are served over HTTPS.

content_type.description:
MIME media type of the file content.

Describes the file format according to IANA standards (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf', 'application/zip'). This is determined automatically based on the file signature and extension upon upload.

This field is used by clients to determine how to handle the content (e.g., display images inline, download documents). The system validates that content type matches the allowed file types and prevents upload of potentially dangerous file types.

Values must be from validated list: 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf', 'text/plain', 'application/msword', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document', 'application/zip'.

file_size.description:
Size of the attachment file in bytes.

There is a system-imposed maximum file size restriction of 20,971,520 bytes (20MB). All uploaded files must be below this threshold.

This field is automatically calculated and verified by the system during upload. It's used for: 
1. Storage allocation monitoring
2. Data transfer calculations and bandwidth estimation
3. Displaying file size information to users in UI
4. Preventing abuse by large file uploads

Minimum value is 0 bytes (representing empty files), though system typically rejects 0-byte files as invalid.

original_filename.description:
Original filename as provided by the user during upload.

This field preserves the user's intended filename for display purposes, including the file extension. It is not used for storage or retrieval (the file is stored with internal UUID-based naming).

System imposes a 255-character limit to prevent path traversal attacks and database performance issues. Special characters are sanitized to ensure compatibility with filesystems and web browsers.

The filename is never trusted for security purposes - content type and file signature are the authoritative sources for determining file type.

oneOf.description:
Categorizes the attachment by its primary purpose and content type.

Defines the relationship context and usage rules:

- 'image': Visual media intended for display (JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP). May trigger thumbnail generation and CDN optimization.
- 'file': Non-image documents or archives (PDF, ZIP, DOCX, TXT). Documents are processed for content moderation and metadata extraction.
- 'system': System-generated attachments for audit, logs, or internal purposes. Typically not visible to end-users and cannot be uploaded by citizens.

This field determines processing behavior, access permissions, display methods, and moderation rules. Every attachment must be assigned one of these three types.
