The system uses UTC format with date-time format to ensure consistency across all time zones (Asia/Seoul and others), enabling accurate audit trails and compliance reporting.

IDiscussionBoardCommentVote.description:
This schema represents the discussion_board_comment_votes database model, which records individual community feedback (votes) on comment content within the discussion board system.

The model captures user sentiment through upvotes (+1) and downvotes (-1) on comments made within articles. Each vote is uniquely associated with a specific citizen and comment, creating a relationship between users and content engagement. The system enforces a composite unique constraint @@unique([citizenId, commentId]) to ensure that each citizen can cast only one vote per comment.

The schema structure aligns directly with the discussion_board_comment_votes table in the database, providing a complete type-safe representation of the vote data model. The vote_value field accepts values in {-1, 0, 1} with 0 indicating vote removal, as specified in the API operations for both create and update actions.

This schema is used as the response body type for multiple operations:
- GET /discussionBoard/comments/{commentId}/votes/{voteId} (retrieve specific vote)
- GET /discussionBoard/comment-votes/{voteId} (retrieve specific vote by ID)
- POST /discussionBoard/comments/{commentId}/votes (create vote)
- PATCH /discussionBoard/citizen/comment-votes/{commentId} (update or remove vote)

It is also referenced by the request body schema IDiscussionBoardCommentVote.ICreate and IDiscussionBoardCommentVote.IRequest, which contain only subset fields for submission purposes.

The field mapping ensures consistency between the database schema and API surface, maintaining data integrity throughout the request-response cycle.

status.description:
The new status for the article report.

This field determines how the moderator's review concludes.

- 'resolved': The report has been addressed and no further action is needed. This closes the moderation case and notifies the reporter of the outcome.
- 'dismissed': The reported content was reviewed and deemed not in violation of community guidelines. This maintains the content's visibility while closing the report. Moderators must provide explicit justification to prevent reporter appeal.
- 'escalated': The report requires further review by senior moderation team or legal compliance review. The original action is suspended while higher-level moderation processes engage. This triggers system notification to senior moderators and creates an audit trail entry.

System consequences:
- 'resolved' and 'dismissed' status changes finalize the moderation decision and archive the report
- 'escalated' triggers cross-team notification and creates a priority case in the moderation queue

All status changes are immutable audit trail entries and cannot be changed after being applied.

reason.description:
The moderator's official justification for the report status update.

This field contains the detailed reasoning behind the moderation decision, which forms part of the public audit trail and legal compliance record.

Business context:
- This reason becomes an immutable part of the case history and may be used in legal proceedings or regulatory inspections
- Must comply with data protection and content moderation transparency regulations
- Should be written in clear, objective language that can be understood by both users and legal authorities
- Must avoid emotional language, personal attacks, or vague statements

Legal and compliance requirements:
- Must be retained for minimum 7 years as part of compliance audit records
- Must provide sufficient detail to enable external review by regulatory bodies, even when the reporter is anonymous
- Must reference specific platform policy sections when applicable

Requirements:
- Must be between 1 and 1000 characters
- Must not be empty or whitespace-only
- Should provide clear, specific details about why the report was handled in this way
- Must reference specific platform policies when applicable

Examples of acceptable reasons:
- "Content was misleading but not intentionally false"
- "Violates Community Guidelines Section 3.2 about personal attacks"
- "Reported content is a historical document with academic value"
- "Multiple reports were submitted in error by the same user"

This field replaces any previous reason provided and becomes the definitive record for this moderation action.

IDiscussionBoardArticleReport.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating the status and reason of a discussion board article report.

This schema defines the data structure for moderating reports on articles. When a citizen submits a report on an article, moderators must review it and update its status with a clear justification.

The report system enables community self-governance by allowing citizens to flag potentially violating content. Moderators then use this update endpoint to manage these reports and maintain platform standards.

The status field controls the workflow outcome, while the reason field creates transparency by documenting the moderation decision rationale. Both fields are mandatory to ensure accountability and consistent application of platform policies.

Note: This schema is strictly for updating existing reports. To create new reports, use the IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate schema instead.

expires_at.description:
The new expiration timestamp for the suspension. Setting this to a future date extends the suspension. Setting this to a past date immediately expires the suspension (triggers status transition to "expired"). This field is optional; if not provided, the suspension's expiration date remains unchanged. A value of null will clear any existing expiration date, effectively canceling the suspension.

This field represents the end of the suspension period and is critical for compliance with platform policies. The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone (e.g., "2024-12-01T00:00:00Z").

This property is used in various moderation workflows, including temporary suspensions, appeal-based suspensions, and administrative reviews.

Note: When the suspension's expires_at date is reached, the system automatically lifts the suspension and notifies the citizen via notification system. This field must not be used to reset a suspension to a previous date.

reason.description:
Updated reason for the suspension modification. This field provides context about why the suspension duration or status is being changed. The reason must be a detailed explanation of the moderation decision, typically reflecting a review of the citizen's previous behavior or a change in platform policy.

This field is optional; if not provided, the original suspension reason remains in effect. When provided, it replaces the previous reason and becomes part of the audit trail. The reason should reference specific violations and may include references to platform policy sections.

The description should be professional, specific, and avoid vague terms like "policy violation" without context. Recommended format includes: "Updated based on review of multiple recent violations of section 3.2 regarding abusive behavior. The original suspension period has been extended due to pattern of repeated infractions."

This field is required only when changing the reason; otherwise it is optional for partial updates. The system will store this text in the moderation audit logs and may make it available to citizens during appeal processes. The reason should always align with status changes to maintain audit trail integrity.

oneOf.description: Current status of the suspension. Must be either 'active' indicating the suspension is currently in effect, or 'expired' indicating the suspension period has concluded and access restrictions have been lifted. Status transitions from active to expired occur either automatically at end_date, or manually by setting this field to 'expired'. Manual setting to 'active' after expiration is not permitted.

IDiscussionBoardSuspension.IUpdate.description:
Update request for discussion board suspension records. This schema defines the properties that can be modified for an existing suspension record by moderator actors. All fields are optional to support partial updates, and the system automatically handles audit logging and actor context from the authenticated session.

The suspension update operation allows moderators to extend the suspension duration, modify the reason for suspension, or transition the status to "expired" (which completes the suspension period). This is a PATCH-style operation where only the fields that need to be changed are provided in the request body. All other suspension properties remain unchanged.

This schema must ONLY contain properties that can be updated after the suspension has been created. Authentication context fields (moderator_id, actor_id) are automatically derived from the JWT token and must not be included in this request body as they represent the acting moderator, not the suspended citizen.

The updated_at field is automatically managed by the system and should not be provided in this request. Suspensions cannot be undone - they can only be extended or marked as expired. The explicit status field enables precise status transitions in the audit trail, with automatic transitions from active to expired occurring at the end_date timestamp when expires_at is not provided.

IDiscussionBoardCommentModAction.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a moderation action on a comment. This schema defines the parameters for moderator decisions such as remove, warn, hide, or dismiss actions, including the reason for the action and notification preferences.

This DTO is used in POST and PATCH operations on /discussionBoard/moderator/comments/{commentId}/mod-actions.

The action_type must be one of the predefined values: 'remove', 'warn', 'hide', or 'dismiss' as defined in the discussion_board_comment_mod_actions table schema. The moderator_id is automatically populated from the authenticated moderator's JWT token and must not be included in this request.

Business Logic: When a moderator applies an action, this record creates an immutable audit trail for accountability. The action does not alter the comment's visibility status directly - comment states are managed by the discussion_board_comment_statuses table. If the action is 'dismiss', the associated comment report is closed. If the action is 'remove' or 'hide', notification may be sent to the comment author based on the notify_author flag.

This schema is designed to capture the moderator's intent for moderation while maintaining separation of concerns: this action records the decision, while content visibility is controlled by a separate system (discussion_board_comment_statuses).

This field directly corresponds to the action_type column in the discussion_board_comment_mod_actions table and is a required field for all moderation actions.

action_type.description:
The type of moderation action to apply to the comment. Must be one of the predefined values: 'remove', 'warn', 'hide', or 'dismiss'.

- 'remove': Indicates the comment has been removed from public view
- 'warn': Issues a warning to the comment author about the violation
- 'hide': Makes the comment invisible to non-moderators but retains it in the system
- 'dismiss': Closes the report without any action, indicating no violation was found

This field directly corresponds to the action_type column in the discussion_board_comment_mod_actions table and is a required field for all moderation actions.

reason.description:
The reason for applying this moderation action. Must provide specific details about why the action is being taken, referencing the violation of community guidelines or specific content rules.

This reason will be visible to the comment author if notify_author is true and will be stored in the moderation audit trail.

The reason should be factual and descriptive, avoiding vague terms like 'inappropriate' or 'offensive'. Instead, specify the exact guideline violation (e.g., 'Contains personal information', 'Spamming multiple posts', 'Harassment directed at specific user').

Minimum length: 10 characters
Maximum length: 500 characters

notify_author.description:
Determines whether the comment author should receive a notification about the moderation action.

When true, a notification will be sent to the comment author containing the action_type and reason. This is important for transparency and allows the author to understand why their comment was moderated.

When false, the action is logged, but no notification is sent to the author. This may be appropriate for dismiss actions or when the reason is confidential.

The default behavior is true, but moderators may choose to suppress notifications for administrative reasons, such as when dealing with repeat offenders or when the violation is a policy violation that doesn't require individual notification.

notify_community.description:
Determines whether the moderation action should be announced to the broader community.

When true, a non-identifying announcement may be made in community channels (e.g., 'A comment was removed for policy violation') to reinforce community standards and demonstrate enforcement.

When false, the action remains confidential and visible only to moderators and the affected author.

This flag is typically used for significant actions involving major violations. It is not recommended for minor actions like warnings on first offenses.

The default behavior is false, maintaining moderation discretion for most cases.

tags.description:
Optional tags to categorize the moderation action for reporting and analytics purposes. These tags help moderate moderation patterns and identify common types of violations.

Each tag must be a concise identifier (max 50 characters) and should follow consistent naming conventions: snake_case with lower case letters.

Common tag examples: 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'doxxing', 'impersonation', 'trolling', 'nudity', 'threats', 'copyright_violation', 'repeated_violation'

Tags are used for generating moderation analytics reports and identifying trends in community behavior. The available tag options are predefined by the system, but moderators can create new tags as needed for emerging violation patterns.

status.description:
The target publication status that the article should change to as part of this audit trail update.

This field must be explicitly provided in every update request to ensure the immutable audit trail accurately reflects the intended status transition. Even though this is an 'update' operation, the status change must be documented as a discrete event in the audit log, and the target status is a critical component of this historical record.

Without this field, the audit trail cannot be reliably reconstructed to determine the final state of an article after a series of status changes.

The status value must exactly match one of the valid statuses defined in the database schema (draft, pending, published, hidden, deleted). This field is required to ensure compliance with platform audit requirements, which mandate complete visibility into every status transition event.

Examples:
- "published" when an article should be made visible to users
- "hidden" when an article has been deemed non-compliant
- "deleted" when an article has been permanently removed from public view

oneOf.description: The publication status that the article had before this transition. This enables auditing of status change history.
The publication status that the article had before this transition. This enables auditing of status change history.

previous_status.description:
The publication status that the article had immediately before this update was applied.

This field is mandatory for maintaining an accurate and complete audit trail. It establishes the context for the change by documenting the previous state before the transition occurred, enabling the system to verify the integrity of the sequence of status changes.

Every status transition must be documented with both the previous state and the new state to create a complete historical record. This is essential for compliance, dispute resolution, and forensic analysis.

The previous_status value must exactly match one of the valid statuses defined in the database schema (draft, pending, published, hidden, deleted). This field is required to satisfy regulatory requirements around audit trail completeness.

Examples:
- "pending" when changing from pending to published
- "published" when changing from published to hidden
- "hidden" when changing from hidden to published
- "deleted" when changing from deleted to published (recovery of archived content)

It is not derived from the database - it must be explicitly provided in every update by the client to prevent audit trail tampering.

IDiscussionBoardArticleStatusLog.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating metadata details of an article's publication status log entry. This schema defines the fields that can be modified after the system automatically creates the initial status log record following a publication status change. This interface does not change the article's live status but allows administrators to update the audit trail with additional context.

The IDiscussionBoardArticleStatusLog.IUpdate is designed for administrative refinement of historical records, not for altering the current state of content. When a moderator receives reports about an article's publication status, they may need to add commentary, update reconciliation status, or document internal reviews - these are the operations this DTO facilitates.

However, this DTO was previously incorrectly designed as if it could update only metadata fields while leaving the core audit trail unchanged. This approach violated core integrity principles: every status change must be explicitly documented with both target and preceding states to maintain a complete, tamper-proof audit trail.

The corrected schema now requires explicit definition of "status" and "previous_status" in every update request, aligning with the immutable nature of the audit trail system. When a moderator updates a status log entry, they are not merely adding commentary - they are formally documenting a new transition event that must be precisely defined with its full context.

This design ensures the audit trail remains complete and verifiable even when modifications occur after the initial log creation. The status field represents the intended final state of the article after the update, while the previous_status field represents the state before the update. This creates a complete transition record that cannot be reconstructed from indirect means.

All fields in this DTO are required (status and previous_status) or optional, reflecting that this is both an update to metadata AND a formalization of the audit transition. This approach ensures compliance with platform integrity standards and regulatory requirements for verifiable audit trails.

Fields that are not permitted to be modified through this interface include the article_id, log_id, and created_at - these are fixed historical facts that must remain immutable to preserve the integrity of the audit trail. This DTO operates at the metadata layer of historical records, not at the core record level, but crucially requires the core transition data (status and previous_status) to be explicitly provided for each update.

content.description:
The original content that was archived, preserving the complete text of the article, comment, or post before moderation actions.

This field captures the exact content that triggered the archival action, ensuring compliance with legal requirements for record-keeping. It includes all formatting, metadata, and context as originally submitted.

This field becomes the primary source of truth for archival audits and legal discovery, as it represents the content in its pre-moderation state.

The value is immutable after archival and cannot be modified, ensuring the integrity of the archival record.

reason.description:
A descriptive explanation of why the content was archived, including specific policy violations, legal considerations, or compliance requirements that motivated the archival decision.

This field contains the moderator's reasoning for the archival action, providing transparency and justification within the moderation workflow.

The reason must be specific and detailed enough to support audit requirements and potential legal challenges, while respecting privacy constraints.

This field is critical for compliance documentation, appeal processes, and legal discovery scenarios.

source_content_id.description:
The unique identifier of the original content type (article, comment, etc.) that was archived.

This field links the archival record to its source content in the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, or related entity tables, enabling traceability of the content's origin.

This identifier allows for cross-referencing between the archive and the original content records, supporting forensic analysis and content recovery workflows.

The source_content_id ensures that even if the original content record is deleted or modified, the archive maintains a verifiable link to the original entity.

source_type.description:
The type of content that was archived, indicating whether it originated from an article, comment, attachment, or other system entity.

This field categorizes the archived content by its origin, enabling organizational filtering and specialized handling rules for different content types.

Supported values include: 'article', 'comment', 'attachment' - with case-sensitive exact matching required for consistency with the database schema and related moderation workflows.

This field determines how the archived content is indexed, searched, and displayed in compliance and audit interfaces.

IDiscussionBoardArchive.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating an archival record of removed content in the discussion board system.

This schema defines the structure for an archival request that permanently stores content that has been removed from public view through moderation actions.

The archival preserves the original content, metadata, and moderation context for compliance, legal discovery, or regulatory audit purposes.

This DTO must be used when a moderator or admin initiates the archival of an article, comment, or other entity that has been flagged and removed from public access.

Key constraints:
- The content field captures the exact text of the removed material
- The reason provides justification for compliance purposes
- The source_content_id and source_type identify the original content

This request type is strictly reserved for authorized moderator and admin actors, with authentication enforced through JWT tokens.

IDiscussionBoardSuspension.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for suspension filtering. Used in the PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/suspensions endpoint to retrieve filtered and paginated suspension records.

This request schema enables moderators and administrators to search for suspension records across multiple dimensions with precise filtering capabilities. The schema supports advanced queries that combine citizen, status, timing, and reason criteria to identify suspensions that meet specific moderation operational requirements.

The seasonal nature of content moderation requires robust filtering options to handle periodic spikes in problematic activity. Users can filter suspensions by specific citizens, suspension status (active/inactive), duration type (temporary/permanent), and date ranges to retrieve targeted results for review cycles, leadership reporting, or compliance audits. Additional filters by reason text allow for semantic searching across violation notes.

Pagination controls ensure performance efficiency when retrieving large result sets, with configurable page sizes and sorting options that leverage database indexing for optimal query performance. Sort criteria include creation time, expiration date, and duration - all indexed fields in the discussion_board_suspensions table.

All fields are optional to allow for flexible search patterns. When no filters are applied, the system returns the most recent suspensions ordered by creation date - a common pattern for moderator oversight dashboards.

Applications should validate that page numbers are positive integers and limit values remain within system bounds (1-100) to prevent resource exhaustion attacks.

This schema represents a critical operational interface in the discussion board moderation workflow, allowing for precise targeting of enforcement actions based on historical patterns and context.

citizen_id.description:
Filter suspensions by specific citizen identifier. Matches against the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions or discussion_board_suspensions tables.

This field is commonly used to investigate patterns of behavior from specific users. Suspension searches by citizen ID can be chained with other criteria to identify all suspensions imposed on a given account, or to verify if a previously suspended user is again active. The database has a compound index on citizen_id and created_at for efficient querying.

Example use cases: When a user reports being unfairly suspended, moderators search by citizen_id to review their entire suspension history. For identifying repeat offenders, this filter combines with status=active and suspension_type=temp to find users with multiple current suspensions.

oneOf.description: Filter suspensions by their current status. Select 'active' for currently enforced suspensions or 'inactive' for expired or lifted suspensions.
Filter suspensions by their current status. Select 'active' for currently enforced suspensions or 'inactive' for expired or lifted suspensions.

status.description:
Filter suspensions by their current status. Select 'active' for currently enforced suspensions or 'inactive' for expired or lifted suspensions.

Corresponds directly to the 'status' field in the discussion_board_suspensions table.

Active suspensions are those currently in effect, meaning the citizen's access has been restricted. Inactive suspensions include those that have expired, been revoked, or reversed through the appeal process.

This field is crucial for moderator worklists where the focus is typically on active suspensions that require ongoing oversight.

The database table uses a boolean-like enum design where 'active' and 'inactive' are the only valid states.

oneOf.description: Filter suspensions by type. 'temp' for temporary suspensions, 'perm' for permanent suspensions. Matches the suspension duration classification in database.
Filter suspensions by type. 'temp' for temporary suspensions, 'perm' for permanent suspensions. Matches the suspension duration classification in database.

suspension_type.description:
Filter suspensions by type. 'temp' for temporary suspensions, 'perm' for permanent suspensions. Matches the suspension duration classification in database.

Corresponds directly to the 'type' field in the discussion_board_suspensions table.

Temporary suspensions (type="temp") have defined expiration dates and duration hours in the database, allowing for automatic reactivation. Permanent suspensions (type="perm") have null end_date and duration_hours, representing indefinite access removal.

This filter is essential for understanding the polarity of moderation actions and may be used in reports to analyze the ratio of temporary versus permanent enforcement decisions.

start_date.description:
Filter suspensions that started on or after this date. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format to match discussion_board_suspensions created_at or start_date fields.

This filter targets suspensions based on their initiation timing. It matches both the "created_at" timestamp (when the suspension record was created) and the "start_date" field (when the restriction actually took effect), as these may differ slightly in systems allowing scheduling of future suspensions.

Common use cases include reviewing suspensions from a specific time period, such as during a security event or surge in policy violations. When used with end_date, this creates a date range for temporal analysis.

The database has a compound index on (created_at, status) to optimize range queries involving this field.

Example request: "2026-03-15T00:00:00Z" to find all suspensions initiated on or after March 15, 2026.

end_date.description:
Filter suspensions that ended on or before this date. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format to match discussion_board_suspensions end_date or expiration_date fields.

This filter targets suspensions that have concluded by the specified point in time. It matches both the "end_date" field (when the suspension formally concluded) and "expiration_date" (when the restriction lift is scheduled to occur).

This is particularly useful for identifying suspensions that have recently expired, which may require review to determine whether restrictions should remain lifted or be reinstated. When combined with status=inactive, it provides a complete picture of past moderation actions.

The database maintains a separate index on (end_date) for efficient expiration-period analysis.

Example request: "2026-06-01T23:59:59Z" to find all suspensions that ended on or before June 1, 2026.

reason.description:
Filter suspensions by moderator action reason or violation description. Performs substring match against suspension reason or violation notes in the database.

This text-based search utilizes PostgreSQL's full-text search capabilities over a dedicated "reason" column in discussion_board_suspensions that contains the violation description provided by the moderator.

Keyword matches are case-insensitive and use word stemming to find related terms. For example, searching "spam" will match "spamming", "spammed", and "anti-spam policy violation".

This field is essential for identifying patterns of violation types across multiple suspensions - such as finding all suspensions related to "hate speech", "impersonation", or "doxxing".

Example request: "threat" to find all suspensions involving threats of violence, or "impostor" to find impersonation cases.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer. Default is page 1.

Controls which 1-100 result set to return, enabling clients to navigate large result sets without overwhelming network bandwidth or client memory.

To prevent resource exhaustion, page values above 1000 (resulting in 100,000+ records) will be rejected with an error. This protects the system from deep pagination attacks.

For first-page requests (page=1), the system returns the most recent results ordered by created_at DESC, which provides immediate relevance for moderation dashboards. For subsequent pages, results are consistent across page requests by using ORDER BY #__orderby__ and LIMIT #__limit__.

This field interacts with limit to determine the total number of records retrieved: page × limit = total records.

limit.description:
Number of items per page for pagination. Must be between 1 and 100. Default is 20. Used for rate limiting and performance optimization.

Controls how many suspension records are included in each API response page, balancing between delivery speed and result completeness.

Lower limits (1-10) are useful for debugging or first-load scenarios on low-bandwidth devices. Standard limits (20-50) provide optimal performance for most moderation workflows. Higher limits (80-100) are recommended when retrieving full report datasets but may impact server response time on systems with large suspension databases.

The database has a composite index (status, sort_by, created_at) optimized for the combination of limit=20 and default sort settings, making this a high-performance default.

System performance will degrade for limit > 75 on databases exceeding 1M suspension records, so clients should prefer smaller limits and iterate through pages.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Options: 'created_at' for suspension creation time, 'end_date' for when the suspension ends, 'duration_hours' for total suspension length in days.
Field to sort results by. Options: 'created_at' for suspension creation time, 'end_date' for when the suspension ends, 'duration_hours' for total suspension length in days.
Field to sort results by. Options: 'created_at' for suspension creation time, 'end_date' for when the suspension ends, 'duration_hours' for total suspension length in days.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by. Options: 'created_at' for suspension creation time, 'end_date' for when the suspension ends, 'duration_hours' for total suspension length in days.

Corresponds directly to indexed columns in the discussion_board_suspensions table.

- 'created_at': Sorts by when the suspension was recorded in the system (most common default)
- 'end_date': Sorts by when the suspension restriction will be lifted (critical for identifying imminent expirations)
- 'duration_hours': Sorts by the total length of the suspension in hours (useful for analyzing penalty severity patterns)

The database maintains separate B-tree indexes on each of these fields for optimal sorting performance. When combined with the order parameter, this enables efficient range queries with minimal disk seeks.

Default sorting is 'created_at' in descending order to prioritize recent cases.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is descending.
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is descending.

order.description:
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is descending.

Determines the sequence of results when sorted by the selected sort_by field.

Descending order ('desc') is the system default because moderator worklists prioritize the most recent actions. Ascending order ('asc') is primarily used for retrospective analysis of historical trends.

Database performance characteristics vary by sort direction. Descending sorts on created_at are highly optimized on the table's primary index, making them faster than ascending sorts, especially when combined with LIMIT clauses.

Maximum sorting is capped at 1000 records; results beyond this will be truncated. For historical analysis beyond that limit, clients should use export functions rather than paginated APIs.

moderator_id.description:
Filter suspensions by the identifier of the moderator who imposed the suspension.

Matches against the moderator_id field in the discussion_board_suspensions table, linking to the discussion_board_moderator table.

This filter is used to audit specific moderator actions, identify patterns in moderation escalation, or find all suspensions issued by a particular moderator during a given time period. It enables accountability and quality assurance in community governance.

When filtering by moderator_id, it's common to combine with status=active and end_date criteria to identify in-progress actions under review. The system enforces that only super-admins can search by moderator_id of other moderators to ensure privacy and prevent misuse.

duration_hours.description:
Filter suspensions by their total duration in hours.

Matches against the duration_hours field in the discussion_board_suspensions table, which contains the integer number of hours for temporary suspensions.

This filter allows for identifying suspensions of specific lengths - such as all 24-hour suspensions, or suspensions longer than 72 hours. It helps analyze whether moderation penalties are being consistently applied according to policy guidelines.

Valid values are integers from 1 to 8760 (365 days), with permanent suspensions (type="perm") not having this field populated.

Beyond 30 days (720 hours), suspensions are typically categorized as permanent, making this field most relevant for media-term penalties.

appeal_status.description:
Filter suspensions by the status of any associated appeal process.

Matches against the appeal_status field in the discussion_board_suspensions table that tracks the procedural state of citizen appeals.

Valid states include:
- 'pending': appeal has been submitted but not yet reviewed
- 'under_review': appeal is currently being considered by an appeals board
- 'rejected': appeal was denied and original suspension remains in effect
- 'approved': appeal was granted and suspension has been lifted or reduced
- 'withdrawn': citizen withdrew their appeal before resolution

This filter enables moderators to focus on appeals that require immediate attention, particularly 'pending' and 'under_review' cases which have SLA-based response deadlines.

This field complements status and created_at to provide complete lifecycle tracking of each moderation decision.

A switch field to indicate whether the report is for an article or a comment. This enables the system to route the report appropriately to the correct moderation workflow.

This field is required when using the /moderation/report endpoint. When reporting via /articles/{articleId}/reports endpoint, this field is implicitly 'article' and does not need to be included in the request body.

Valid values: 'article', 'comment'

This field helps the backend validate and process the report appropriately based on the content type and ensures proper database relations.

description.description:

This field allows users to provide additional context about why the content is being reported.

While the report_type categorizes the violation, this field provides qualitative detail that helps moderators understand the specific nature of the issue.

Example: "This post contains doxxing information including the victim's home address and phone number."

The description is limited to 1000 characters to prevent abuse while still allowing meaningful context.

This text is stored unmodified and displayed to moderators during review.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for submitting a report against a content item on the discussion board platform.

The IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate DTO is used by citizens to formally report violations of platform policies, triggering a moderation review process. This DTO accepts only the essential reporting information that citizens can provide at the time of reporting, while excluding all system-managed fields that are automatically populated.

The structure follows strict separation of concerns: citizen-provided content (target content identifier, report type, and optional description) versus system-managed metadata (ID, timestamps, status, reviewer ID, etc.). This design ensures security and data integrity by preventing client-side tampering with critical system attributes.

Critical security principle: All identity-related fields are automatically populated from the authentication context (JWT token) and are strictly prohibited from client input. This prevents impersonation attacks of the reporter identity.

When reporting against an article, the target_article_id must be provided and target_comment_id must be omitted. When reporting against a comment, the target_comment_id must be provided and target_article_id must be omitted. The target_content_type field serves as a validity check to ensure these exclusivity constraints are maintained.

The report_type field uses a standardized taxonomy to ensure consistent moderation triaging, automated filtering, and analytical reporting across the platform. Values are constrained to predefined enum options to prevent abuse of free-text reporting categories.

The description field is optional and limited to 1000 characters to balance between allowing meaningful context and preventing report spam. This field enhances moderator efficiency by providing additional situational context beyond the standardized category.

id.description: Unique identifier for the notification record in the database. This primary key allows retrieval of specific notification records by its globally unique ID.

comment_id.description: The unique identifier of the comment this notification is associated with. This foreign key links the notification to the original comment in the discussion_board_comments table.

recipient_id.description: The unique identifier of the citizen who will receive this notification. This is automatically set to the author of the comment and cannot be modified by the client. The recipient is derived from the comment's author during notification creation.

oneOf.description: The type or category of notification being triggered. This field indicates the reason for the notification and is set by system events: "reply" for a reply to the comment, "report" for a report on the comment, "upvote" for an upvote, or "downvote" for a downvote.

is_read.description: Indicates whether the notification has been read by the recipient. Default is false (unread) and is automatically updated to true when the user views the notification in the UI. This affects the display of unread indicators in notification feeds and bell icons.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the notification record was created in the database. This field is automatically generated by the system and represents when the triggering event occurred, in Asia/Seoul timezone (UTC+9).

IDiscussionBoardCommentNotification.description:
Notification record for actions on discussion board comments. This DTO represents a single notification generated by user interactions with comments, such as replies, reports, or votes. Each notification is associated with a specific comment and recipient, and records the nature of the triggering event.

The notification system delivers these notifications to users via email, in-app alerts, or push notifications based on their preference settings. The notification type indicates the action that triggered the notification (reply, report, upvote, downvote), while the recipient_id is automatically set to the author of the target comment and cannot be modified by clients.

Changes to the is_read status are handled automatically by the system when the user views notifications, and the timestamps are maintained by the database. The most often associated operations are GET /comments/{commentId}/notifications/{notificationId} for retrieval and POST /comments/{commentId}/notifications for creation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the report in the discussion_board_reports table.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the database and allows for efficient lookup and tracking of individual reports across the system.

All operations related to this report (viewing, resolving, appealing) reference this unique identifier to ensure accurate association with the correct report record.

reported_content_id.description:
Identifier of the content being reported (article, comment, attachment, etc.)

This field links the report to specific content in the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, or discussion_board_attachments tables.

System ensures the reported content exists by verifying against the corresponding entity tables during report creation.

This ID is used to scope the report to its target content and enables moderation actions to be targeted accurately.

report_reason.description:
Text description of why the content was reported.

This field captures the reporter's reason for flagging the content, helping moderators understand the nature of the violation.

The system enforces a maximum length of 500 characters to ensure concise reporting while allowing sufficient detail for context.

Report reasons are categorized into predefined types (harassment, spam, etc.) to facilitate automated triaging.

Minimum length of 1 character ensures reports cannot be submitted empty. Empty reports trigger system validation errors.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the report's moderation process.

- 'pending': Report has been submitted but not yet reviewed by any moderator
- 'reviewed': Moderator has examined the report and made a preliminary assessment
- 'dismissed': Moderator determined no violation occurred; report is closed without action
- 'resolved': Moderator took action (e.g., content removed, user warned); report is closed with resolution

This field controls report visibility in moderation dashboards and determines whether further action is required.

Status transitions are tracked in the moderation audit log, ensuring full accountability.

All new reports are automatically created with 'pending' status. Only authorized moderators can transition status via dedicated API endpoints.

Invalid status values will cause API validation errors. This is a required field with no default value.

severity.description:
Automatically determined severity level for the reported content on a scale of 1-5.

Level 1: Minor violation (e.g., off-topic comment)
Level 2: Moderate violation (e.g., mild harassment)
Level 3: Significant violation (e.g., threatening language)
Level 4: Severe violation (e.g., hate speech, explicit content)
Level 5: Critical violation (e.g., illegal content, imminent threat)

Severity is calculated based on keywords, context analysis, and pattern matching against previously resolved reports with similar content.

This value helps prioritize moderator workload and determine appropriate response levels.

This field is non-nullable and automatically calculated by the system when a report is submitted. It cannot be manually set via the API.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was submitted by the citizen.

This field uses ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) to ensure consistent date/time representation across systems.

Used for sorting reports chronologically in moderation queues and determining report age for time-based automation rules (e.g., auto-dismissal after 7 days without action).

System automatically populates this field at time of report creation and it is immutable after creation.

- What information should be included in the content_summary
- Which UI components to display for moderation actions

Always true for regular citizens reporting content, as protected by privacy policy.

This ensures citizens can report violations without fear of retaliation, encouraging community participation in content moderation.

System ensures this field is TRUE for all citizen-submitted reports, regardless of moderator action. This field will never be false for citizen reports.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a discussion board report for moderation dashboards and reporting interfaces.

Represents a lightweight, non-sensitive overview of reported content for moderators to quickly assess priorities without exposing sensitive user information or complete content details.

This summary type is specifically designed for:
- Moderation team dashboards
- Bulk report reviews
- Analytics and reporting
- Administrative oversight

Contains all essential context for moderation decisions while excluding:
- Full reported content details
- Identifiable user information
- Internal system flags
- Unnecessary metadata

The summary maintains necessary information to:
- Track report status
- Understand severity and prioritization
- Identify responsible moderators
- Analyze reporting patterns
- Ensure compliance requirements

Used in API responses for GET /discussionBoard/{actor}/articles/{articleId}/reports and GET /discussionBoard/moderator/reports endpoints, where full report details are not required.

For full report details, use the parent IBoardReport entity or retrieve via dedicated report detail

IDiscussionBoardAppeal.IUpdate.description:
Updated details for the appeal record, including new status and moderator justification.

The IDiscussionBoardAppeal.IUpdate schema defines the properties that can be modified when updating an appeal record in the discussion_board_appeals table.

This schema is used exclusively for PUT requests to /discussionBoard/moderator/appeals/{appealId}, allowing moderators to change the appeal's status and provide a justification for their decision.

Important constraints:
- Only status and moderator_comment fields can be updated
- All other fields (appeal_reason, reporter_id, target_content_id) are immutable
- Status transitions are restricted to valid states
- Once status is set to "approved" or "rejected", no further updates are permitted
- moderator_comment is required when status changes, but can be omitted if status remains unchanged

The schema follows API security best practices by only exposing modifiable fields and excluding all system-controlled or immutable attributes.

Note: The appeal_id property is not included here as it is provided as a path parameter in the API endpoint and cannot be changed in the request body.

oneOf.description:
The new status of the appeal. Must be one of: "pending", "in-progress", "approved", "rejected".

Transition rules:
- Only transitions from "pending" to "in-progress" or to "approved"/"rejected" are allowed
- "in-progress" is a temporary state for ongoing moderator review
- "approved" and "rejected" are final states - no further updates are permitted once set

This field is REQUIRED when changing the appeal status. If status remains unchanged, this field can be omitted.

Valid values must exactly match one of the enum values as specified in the business rules.

A detailed comment from the moderator explaining the decision made on this appeal.

Length constraints: 1-10000 characters.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. This parameter controls the result set offset for moderation dashboards, with default set to 1 for first page of reports. Used by moderators to navigate through large volumes of reports without overwhelming system resources.

limit.description: Number of reports per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Default is 20. This controls pagination size for moderation workflows. Lower values improve response time for interactive UIs, while higher values reduce API calls for bulk reviews. Maximum of 100 prevents excessive resource consumption on the moderation server during high-volume request periods.

oneOf.description: Field to sort reports by. Allowed values: createdAt (creation date), severity (report severity level), or status (current moderation status). Defaults to createdAt. This is the primary sorting criterion for moderation workflows, as most moderators prioritize reports in chronological order to maintain first-in-first-out processing. The default (createdAt) ensures that newer reports receive timely attention. Sorting by severity or status is used for advanced filtering when moderators need to address high-priority cases first.

Field to sort reports by. Allowed values: createdAt (creation date), severity (report severity level), or status (current moderation status). Defaults to createdAt. Used when moderators prioritize reports based on risk level. Reports with higher severity (4-5) will appear first in the queue, allowing immediate response to potential crises such as hate speech, threats, or illegal content before lower-severity issues.

Field to sort reports by. Allowed values: createdAt (creation date), severity (report severity level), or status (current moderation status). Defaults to createdAt. Enables moderators to group reports by their current state, facilitating batch processing. For example, sorting by status allows teams to first complete all 'pending' reports before moving to 'reviewed', ensuring no reports remain stagnant in workflow queues.

sortBy.description: Field to sort reports by. Allowed values: createdAt (creation date), severity (report severity level), or status (current moderation status). Defaults to createdAt. This parameter determines how citizen-submitted reports are ordered in moderator dashboards. The sorting strategy directly impacts moderation efficiency and response prioritization. Since most moderation workflows are time-sensitive, the system defaults to createdAt to ensure chronological processing, but allows switching to severity or status for targeted review sessions focused on risk levels or resolution status.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. Allowed values: asc (ascending) or desc (descending). Defaults to desc. Ascending order shows oldest reports first, which is rarely used but valuable for historical analysis or auditing past moderation decisions. Default is descending (newest first), which aligns with standard moderation workflow where newer reports require more immediate attention and should be prioritized over older ones.

Sort order direction. Allowed values: asc (ascending) or desc (descending). Defaults to desc. Descending order is the standard for moderation workflows, presenting the most recently submitted reports first. This aligns with the principle of timely response to community concerns, ensuring the latest violations are handled before they escalate. Most moderation dashboards default to this setting for optimal efficiency.

order.description: Sort order direction. Allowed values: asc (ascending) or desc (descending). Defaults to desc. Determines whether reports are displayed from oldest to newest (asc) or newest to oldest (desc). The system defaults to descending order because moderation workflows prioritize recent activity. This setting allows moderators to respond to fresh violations quickly without scrolling through older, potentially resolved reports. The choice of order impacts workflow speed and the effectiveness of case triage strategies.

oneOf.description: Filter reports by moderation status. Can be: pending (new reports), in_review (being evaluated), resolved (action taken), or dismissed (invalid report). 'pending' identifies reports that have been submitted by citizens but have not yet been reviewed by any moderator. This filter shows new submissions that require urgent attention and are often the primary focus during active moderation shifts. A high volume of pending reports may indicate an overload in the moderation queue.

Filter reports by moderation status. Can be: pending (new reports), in_review (being evaluated), resolved (action taken), or dismissed (invalid report). 'in_review' shows reports that a moderator has started examining but has not yet determined a final resolution. This filter helps track ongoing investigations and prevents duplicate reviews by multiple moderators on the same report. It's useful for monitoring workload distribution and identifying bottlenecks in case processing.

Filter reports by moderation status. Can be: pending (new reports), in_review (being evaluated), resolved (action taken), or dismissed (invalid report). 'resolved' includes all reports where a moderator has taken an action - either enforcing policy (e.g., removing content, warning user) or applying a final decision. This filter is essential for reporting, analytics, and confirming that reports have been properly handled. Moderators use this to verify their completion rate and ensure accountability.

Filter reports by moderation status. Can be: pending (new reports), in_review (being evaluated), resolved (action taken), or dismissed (invalid report). 'dismissed' identifies reports that were reviewed and determined to have no policy violation. This may occur when reports are submitted in error, contain false claims, or misinterpret community guidelines. This filter helps moderators and administrators analyze false reporting patterns and potentially improve automated detection systems to reduce unnecessary moderation workload.

status.description: Filter reports by moderation status. Can be: pending (new reports), in_review (being evaluated), resolved (action taken), or dismissed (invalid report). This parameter enables moderators to segment reports based on their position in the moderation workflow. The status values represent key transition points: submitted -> reviewed -> resolved/dismissed. This filtering capability is critical for maintaining an efficient moderation pipeline, allowing teams to focus on reports at specific stages - whether addressing new submissions, monitoring ongoing reviews, or auditing resolved cases for quality assurance.

oneOf.description: Filter reports by severity level. Can be: low (minor issue), medium (potential violation), high (clear policy breach), or critical (urgent abuse). 'low' severity reports indicate minor policy concerns that typically don't require immediate action, such as off-topic comments or minor etiquette breaches. These are often handled by automated systems or assigned to junior moderators during lighter workflow periods. Examples: minor insults, inappropriate but non-harmful humor, minor spam.

Filter reports by severity level. Can be: low (minor issue), medium (potential violation), high (clear policy breach), or critical (urgent abuse). 'medium' severity indicates a likely policy violation that requires direct moderator review. These reports represent borderline behavior that may escalate if ignored, such as subtle harassment, misinformation, or suggestive content. Moderate severity is the most common category and represents the primary workload for frontline moderators.

Filter reports by severity level. Can be: low (minor issue), medium (potential violation), high (clear policy breach), or critical (urgent abuse). 'high' severity indicates an unambiguous policy violation that requires swift action, such as threats, hate speech, or targeted harassment. These reports trigger automatic notifications to senior moderators and may lead to account restrictions. Moderators typically prioritize handling these reports before addressing lower severity issues due to potential legal or safety risks.

Filter reports by severity level. Can be: low (minor issue), medium (potential violation), high (clear policy breach), or critical (urgent abuse). 'critical' severity denotes immediate threats to user safety, illegal activity, or severe violations requiring emergency response. These reports trigger escalation protocols and may involve legal authorities. Examples: child endangerment, incitement to violence, public disclosure of private information. Moderators handling critical reports must follow strict response protocols and document all actions for audit purposes.

severity.description: Filter reports by severity level. Can be: low (minor issue), medium (potential violation), high (clear policy breach), or critical (urgent abuse). This parameter enables moderators to prioritize responses based on risk level. Severity is automatically calculated by the system using a combination of natural language analysis, historical data on similar reports, and user reputation factors. A higher severity indicates higher likelihood of actual violation, urgency of response needed, and potential impact on community health. This classification directly informs whether the report appears on a standard moderation queue or an emergency alert list.

startDate.description: Start date for filtering reports created after this timestamp. In ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). This allows moderators to audit reports within specific timeframes, such as investigating spikes in reporting activity after notable events, reviewing reports from specific moderation shifts, or analyzing historical patterns over days/weeks/months. Using a start date without an end date allows for reviewing all reports since a specific date, useful for post-event analysis or compliance reporting.

endDate.description: End date for filtering reports created before this timestamp. In ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). This enables moderators to focus on reports that were submitted within a specific window leading up to an event or change in moderation policy. Useful for evaluating the impact of recent changes to community guidelines, tracking report volume before/after enforcement actions, or preparing compliance reports with defined date ranges. Can be used alone or combined with startDate to define precise time boundaries for audit trails.

reporter_id.description: Filter reports by the ID of the reporting citizen. Must be a valid UUID. This parameter allows moderators to investigate patterns of reporting behavior from specific users. It can identify citizens who frequently report content (positive community participation) or repeatedly file false reports (potential abuse). Used to understand citizen moderation engagement, distinguish community-driven reporting from targeted reporting campaigns, and ensure reports from legitimate users are given appropriate weight in moderation decisions. This field respects citizen anonymity in response data but provides traceability for internal moderation workflows.

reported_content_id.description: Filter reports by the ID of the reported content (article, comment, attachment, etc.). Must be a valid UUID. This is essential for moderators who need to review all reports targeting a specific piece of content, either to investigate whether one item has been repeatedly reported (indicating coordinated harassment or spam) or to assess cumulative risk of content that has received multiple reports. This allows for holistic review of problematic content rather than isolated reports, enabling more effective moderation of persistent sources of community conflict.

reason.description: Filter reports by keyword in the reason text. Case-insensitive partial match. Used for efficient triaging of large volumes of reports by finding common themes or patterns in citizen-reported reasons. This helps identify emerging issues, repeated misuse cases, or common misunderstandings of community guidelines. For example, searching for 'hate' would return reports mentioning hate speech, racism, or discrimination - allowing moderators to group related reports for coordinated response. Matches any part of the reason text, so 'spam' will match 'spam advertisement' or 'this is spam'. Maximum length of 255 characters prevents overly vague or abusive search queries which could overwhelm the system.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for report filtering. This schema defines the request body for the patch /discussionBoard/moderator/reports endpoint, allowing moderators to filter and paginate through citizen-submitted reports for moderation review. All parameters are optional to support flexible querying. When no filters are provided, all reports are returned in descending order of their creation date (sortBy: createdAt, order: desc) by default. This enables comprehensive moderation workflows where teams may need to review reports by time, urgency, status, or source in a single unified interface. The system supports multi-dimensional filtering so moderators can combine criteria (e.g., severity=high AND status=pending) to identify high-priority cases. The design prioritizes performance by keeping the schema lightweight and avoiding redundant data, focusing solely on essential filtering and pagination controls needed for real-time moderation operations in a high-volume community platform.

IDiscussionBoardBan.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a ban record for moderation dashboards, providing essential information about banned citizens while maintaining privacy and audit compliance.

This schema is used in paginated responses for moderator views of banned users. It includes the core identifiers, timing information, and disciplinary level necessary for moderation decisions, while excluding sensitive details like the complete ban reason text or violation history.

Ban records are permanent historical documents that track all violations of platform rules. There is no "unban" or "soft delete" operation available - bans remain in the system indefinitely for audit and compliance purposes. This summary provides the essential information moderators need to manage the system without exposing private citizen data.

The ban summary includes references to the banned citizen, the moderator who imposed the ban, and the timing of the ban. The actual citizen details and moderator details are accessible through separate API calls when needed.

This schema does not include the complete ban reason text or detailed violation history - those are available via the detail view and audit trail endpoints.

Validation rules:
- All fields are required
- id, citizen_id, moderator_id must be valid UUIDs
- created_at must be a valid ISO 8601 timestamp
- expires_at must be a valid ISO 8601 timestamp or null
- reason_summary must be a string with maximum 200 characters
- banning_level must be the string constant "permanent" as defined

Edge cases:
- When expires_at is null, the ban is permanent and will never expire
- When banning_level is "permanent", the ban is irreversible through automated means
- When a ban is temporarily expired, the record remains for audit purposes
- The moderator_id may refer to a moderator who has since been removed from the system, but the record is preserved for historical accuracy

id.description:
Unique identifier for the ban record in the system.

This UUID v4 value uniquely identifies each ban entry in the discussion_board_bans table. It serves as the primary key for all ban-related operations and appears in audit trails.

citizen_id.description:
Unique identifier of the citizen who has been banned.

References the citizen's record in the discussion_board_citizen table. This is required to identify the banned user without exposing their personal information directly in the ban summary.

The matching citizen record must exist in the database, but may have been deleted elsewhere if the citizen account was later permanently removed.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the ban was imposed.

Returns the exact date and time when the ban was first applied by a moderator.

This value is never modified after creation and is used for determining ban age, prioritizing moderation actions, and in compliance reporting.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when the ban will expire (for temporary bans), or null for permanent bans.

When a temporary ban is imposed, this field contains the expiration date and time.
When a permanent ban is imposed, this field is null to indicate there is no expiration.

A ban is considered active if expires_at is in the future or is null. A ban is expired if expires_at is in the past and not null.

This field controls the ability to view or edit content associated with the banned citizen during the ban period.

reason_summary.description:
Brief summary of the reason for the ban, limited to 200 characters for display in moderation lists.

This is a condensed version of the complete ban reason provided by the moderator when issuing the ban. It is designed for display in tables and lists where space is limited.

The complete reason text (up to 5000 characters) is available in the ban details endpoint. This summary must capture the essence of the violation while remaining concise.

Policy categories are typically reflected here (e.g., "Threatening language", "Spamming", "Impersonation").

banning_level.description:
The level of disciplinary action taken. This field categorizes the severity of the ban for filtering and prioritization in moderation dashboards.

This is a const value of "permanent" to indicate that all bans are permanent administrative actions on the platform.

Although there are temporary and permanent bans in the database, the API currently only exposes permanent bans through this endpoint. This reflects the platform's policy that all bans are permanent records, even those with expiration dates.

This design ensures consistency in the API contract for all ban records, as every ban is treated as a permanent historical record for audit purpose, regardless of its expiration status.

moderator_id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderator who imposed the ban.

References the moderator's record in the discussion_board_moderator table. This field provides accountability for the moderation action.

Allows for tracking which moderator imposed a specific ban, enabling auditing of moderator actions and identification of patterns in moderation behavior. The actual moderator profile is accessible through separate API endpoints.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an article category for display in lists and selection interfaces.

This DTO contains essential information for presenting category information to users without the full detail that might be available in a detailed view.

Designed for pagination responses and category selection components.

Includes only fields relevant for display purposes, omitting sensitive metadata and internal system fields.

Directly derived from the discussion_board_article_categories database table, with filter applied to remove mutable or non-display fields intended only for administrative interfaces.

Application use cases:
- Category lists in sidebars and navigation menus
- Article creation forms with category selectors
- Search result filters
- Moderation dashboard category overview panels

Reference types:
- IPageIDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary - Paginated container for this type
- IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory - Full detail version for editing
- IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.IRequest - Search filter parameters
- IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ICreate - Creation parameters
- IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.IUpdate - Update parameters

id.description:
Unique identifier for the article category.

This UUID is automatically generated by the system when a new category is created and is used as the primary key in the database.

All references to this category from other entities (articles, comments) use this identifier.

title.description:
Human-readable title of the article category.

This is the visible name displayed to users in category lists and selection interfaces.

Must be unique across the system and follow title case formatting conventions.

No special characters except spaces, hyphens, and apostrophes are permitted.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier for the article category.

This lowercase, hyphenated string is used in URLs to provide readable, SEO-friendly paths.

Example: 'Technology News' becomes 'technology-news'.

Must be unique and generated automatically from the title if not provided.

description.description:
Detailed description explaining the purpose and scope of this category.

Provides context for moderators and users about appropriate article topics in this category.

Used as tooltip text and category overview information.

May be left empty for simple categories with obvious scope.

status.description:
Current operational status of the category.

- 'active': Category is visible to all users and articles can be posted.
- 'inactive': Category is hidden from public view but still accessible to moderators.
- 'archived': Category is permanently retired and no longer visible to anyone.

Default value: 'active'.

Archived categories preserve historical data but prevent new content creation.

This field directly maps to the status column in the discussion_board_article_categories database table.

parent_category_id.description:
Reference to the parent category for hierarchical organization.

Allows creation of category trees (e.g., 'Electronics' > 'Smartphones').

Null indicates a top-level category.

All children categories inherit restrictions from their parent categories when applicable.

This field references the id field of the same table, enabling self-referential hierarchical relationships.

article_count.description:
Current number of published articles assigned to this category.

This is a computed field updated automatically as articles are created, moved, or deleted.

Used for sorting categories by popularity and display in category navigation interfaces.

Does not include draft or hidden articles.

This field is not stored directly in the database but calculated from the article table and its category foreign key.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the category was created in the system.

This is automatically set upon category creation and cannot be modified by users.

Used for sorting categories chronologically and calculating category age.

Maps directly to the created_at column in the discussion_board_article_categories table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last modification to this category's metadata.

Updated whenever the title, description, status, or parent category changes.

Does not update when article counts change or when articles under this category are modified.

Maps directly to the updated_at column in the discussion_board_article_categories table.

order_index.description:
Manual sort priority for display ordering in category lists.

Categories are displayed ascending by order_index, then alphabetically by title when order_index is equal.

Default value: 0 (lowest priority).

Higher values display higher in the user interface.

Supports coarse-grained manual ordering while preserving alphabetical sorting as a secondary criterion.

color_code.description:
Hexadecimal color code for category visual styling.

Used to color-code category labels, badges, and navigation elements.

Format: #RRGGBB (e.g., #3498db for blue).

Null indicates no specific color - the system default will be used.

Validated against the hex color format at both application and database levels to ensure consistent rendering.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the suspension record.

Each suspension is uniquely identified by this UUID, allowing precise reference throughout the system. This ID is used for all related operations, lookups, and audit trails.

citizen_id.description:
Identifier of the citizen receiving the suspension.

Links to the discussion_board_citizen table, identifying which user account has been suspended. This field represents the target of suspension actions and enables tracking of individual user moderation history.

moderator_id.description:
Identifier of the moderator who imposed the suspension.

Links to the discussion_board_moderator table, providing accountability for moderation decisions. This traceability ensures transparency in community governance and enables review of moderator actions.

type.description:
Classification of the suspension type.

Determines the nature of the suspension, which can be 'temporary' or 'permanent'. Temporary suspensions have a defined duration, while permanent suspensions are indefinite. This classification directly impacts user experience and system behavior for the affected account.

reason.description:
Detailed explanation for the suspension decision.

Specifies the policy violation or behavior that led to the suspension. This provides transparency to the affected user and serves as documentation for future appeal processes and moderation audits.

start_date.description:
Timestamp when the suspension became active.

Indicates when the suspension took effect, which is typically immediately upon imposition. This field is essential for calculating suspension duration and determining expiration times.

end_date.description:
Timestamp marking when the suspension will expire.

Applies only to temporary suspensions and indicates the exact moment access restrictions are lifted. For permanent suspensions, this field is set to null as there is no expiration date.

duration_hours.description:
Total duration of the suspension in hours.

Provides a standardized measurement of suspension length, facilitating consistent application of penalties and automated scheduling of expiration processes. This value is calculated from start_date and end_date for temporary suspensions.

status.description:
Current state of the suspension.

Reflects whether the suspension is active, expired, or revoked. This status determines whether the citizen's access restrictions are currently enforced, allowing for dynamic management of moderation actions.

appeal_status.description:
Current state of any associated appeal process.

Tracks whether an appeal has been filed, is under review, or was resolved (approved/rejected). This status indicates the procedural stage of the citizen's challenge to the suspension and its current handling state.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this suspension record was created in the system.

Provides an immutable audit trail of when the moderation action was recorded in the database. This field is automatically generated by the system and cannot be modified.

IDiscussionBoardSuspension.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a citizen suspension for list views and overview displays.

The IDiscussionBoardSuspension.ISummary schema provides a compact, optimized representation of suspension records for display in moderation dashboards, search results, and overview interfaces. This summary excludes detailed content fields to reduce payload size and improve performance when listing multiple suspensions.

It includes only essential metadata required to identify the suspension, understand its context, and determine its current status. The schema retains the core information needed for moderation workflows: who was suspended, by whom, when, why, and what the current status is.

This summary type is designed for scenarios where multiple suspensions are displayed simultaneously, such as in moderator panels or search results pages, where a lightweight representation is crucial for performance and usability.

page.description:
The page number for pagination results. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

This parameter allows clients to navigate through paginated moderation action records. Each page contains a fixed number of records (typically 20-100), and the page number specifies which set of results to retrieve.

For example, page=1 returns the first 20 records, page=2 returns the next 20 records, etc.

When no page parameter is provided, the system defaults to page=1 for first-time queries.

limit.description:
The number of records to return per page in pagination. Must be between 1 and 100.

This parameter controls the density of results returned in each response. Higher limits reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve large result sets, while lower limits improve response times and reduce bandwidth usage.

The value must be within the allowed range of 1-100. Requests outside this range will be rejected with validation errors.

For compliance with system performance quotas, values above 50 are restricted for non-administrator moderators.

oneOf.description:
The field by which the moderation actions should be sorted. Only specific fields are allowed for sorting.

This parameter determines the ordering of moderation action records in the response. The system supports sorting by:
- 'timestamp' (default): Sorts chronologically from oldest to newest
- 'severity': Sorts by action severity level (low, medium, high)
- 'actionType': Sorts alphabetically by the type of moderation action

Sorting by other fields is disabled for performance and security reasons.

The default sort order is ascending (oldest first). Use the 'order' parameter to reverse the order.
