status_changed_at.description:
The exact timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) when the status transition was recorded in the system. This represents the moment the change took effect and was persisted to the database.

This field enables chronological ordering of all status transitions for an article and is used for timelines, history reconstruction, and compliance reporting. The timestamp is captured server-side at the moment of database persistence, ensuring accuracy and preventing client-side timestamp manipulation.

status_changed_reason.description:
An optional human-readable explanation provided by the acting actor when transitioning the article's status. This explanation is intended to provide context for the change, such as "Policy violation: offensive content" or "Author requested revision".

When a system automates a status change (status_changed_by: "system"), this field will be null, as automated actions do not require human justifications. When a moderator makes the change (status_changed_by: "moderator"), this field may be populated with their comment, though it is not mandatory.

For compliance purposes, moderation decisions may be recorded in a separate, more detailed audit trail (discussion_board_moderation_audit_trails), but this field provides a lightweight summary directly within the status log.

is_final.description:
Indicates whether this status transition represents the current, final state of the article. This boolean flag simplifies usage in UI components where it's important to distinguish between historical transitions and the article's present state.

- true: The status represented by this log entry is the article's current, active status.
- false: The status represented by this log entry is an historical state, followed by one or more subsequent transitions.

This property improves display efficiency in moderation interfaces, allowing for direct identification of the latest status without requiring additional queries to find the maximum timestamp or reordering the full history.

oneOf.description:
The article's publication status immediately prior to this transition. This field enables accurate reconstruction of status evolution sequences and change verification.

By comparing prev_status with status, moderators and system administrators can clearly see the direction of change (e.g., 'published' → 'hidden' indicates content being taken down, while 'draft' → 'pending' indicates submission for review).

This field supports forensic audit capability, helping to identify unauthorized or accidental status changes. When the article is first created (initial state), this value will be null, as there is no prior state to reference.

read_at.description:
Timestamp when the notification was marked as read. This field is updated to the current time when a citizen marks a notification as read. The value is null when the notification remains unread.

Only citizens can update this field to mark notifications they own as read. Moderators can update this field for any notification in the system.

This field is part of the notification's metadata tracking and indicates user engagement with the message.

For compliance purposes, this timestamp is immutable after setting and cannot be reset to null once set.

priority.description:
The priority level of the notification. Can be set to 'high', 'normal', or 'low' to adjust how prominently the notification is displayed.

Moderators can update this field to re-prioritize notifications for administrative purposes. Citizens can only update priority for notifications they own, and are limited to setting it to 'normal' unless system permissions allow more.

This field affects the UI display order and notification delivery behavior.

Valid values: 'high', 'normal', 'low', null.

category.description:
The category classification for the notification, such as 'system', 'moderation', 'community', 'personal', etc.

Allows users and moderators to organize notifications by type for filtering and reporting purposes.

Moderators can change this field to reclassify notifications, while citizens can only alter it for their own notifications within system permissions.

This field enables targeted notification preferences and user segmentation.

is_visible.description:
Determines whether the notification should be displayed in the user interface. When false, the notification is hidden from normal views but still exists in the system for audit purposes.

This field is used to temporarily hide notifications without deleting them, such as when a user has seen a notification and wants to dismiss it from view.

Moderators can set this flag to manage visibility for all users, while citizens can only hide notifications they own.

When set to null, the system uses the default visibility value from system configuration.

is_important.description:
Marks the notification as important, triggering enhanced delivery mechanisms and UI indicators such as bold text or special icons. This field is used for critical system messages and moderation actions.

This flag helps users prioritize notifications that require immediate attention. Moderators can set this flag for system-wide important messages.

Citizens cannot modify this flag for notifications they don't own, but can use system settings to mark their own notifications as important if allowed by configuration.

When set to null, the system determines importance based on notification type and content.

expires_at.description:
The expiration date and time for the notification. After this time, the notification is automatically marked as expired and hidden from views.

Used for time-sensitive notifications like events, deadlines, or temporary announcements. When set to null, the notification never expires.

Moderators can set expiration dates on any notifications to ensure temporary messages don't clutter the system indefinitely.

Citizens cannot set expiration dates on notifications they own unless explicitly permitted by system configuration.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationRecord.IUpda.description:
Request DTO for updating notification record properties. This type represents the fields that can be modified in a notification record by users. The update operation allows citizens to mark notifications as read and moderators to update other metadata fields for administrative purposes.

The IUpdate type follows a partial update pattern where only the fields included in the request are modified, while all other fields remain unchanged. This allows for fine-grained updates without requiring clients to send the entire notification object.

Fields that can be updated are intentionally restricted to metadata properties, not the core notification content or ownership information.

This DTO is used for both citizen and moderator notification updates, though permissions are enforced at the service layer based on the actor type.

All fields in this DTO are optional to support partial updates. Setting any field to null removes its value from the notification record, except for fields like archived_at which have immutable semantics once set.

reason.description:
Updated explanation of the community guideline violation that merits this warning. This field describes the specific behavior or content that violated the platform's policies and justifies the warning action.

Note: The reason must accurately reflect the nature of the violation, with sufficient detail for the recipient to understand the specific conduct that was problematic. This field supports rich text to allow for clear communication of moderation decisions.

The reason should be written in clear, objective language that focuses on the specific behavior rather than making personal attacks. Examples include: "Repeatedly sharing unverified misinformation about public health" or "Engaging in targeted harassment of another user".

This field must align with established moderation policies and provide specific evidence or observations to support the warning decision. It serves as the primary justification for the warning in any appeal process and helps maintain transparency in community governance.

oneOf.description:
The severity level assigned to this warning, which determines the consequences and escalation path. This field controls the warning's impact on the user's reputation and account privileges.

The system supports three distinct levels:

- 'none': Indicates no active warning, used for clearing previous warnings
- 'moderate': A standard warning for minor policy violations that carries moderate consequences
- 'severe': A serious violation that results in significant restrictions and potential account suspension

The level field must be one of these exact values and represents the organization's assessment of the violation's severity. Updates to the level should be consistent with the moderation policy and community guidelines.

Only authorized moderators may increase a warning's level beyond what was initially assigned, and all level changes are recorded in the audit trail for accountability.

context.description:
Additional context or relevant information about the warning update that provides deeper insight into the moderation decision. Use this field to include supporting details not covered in the reason field, such as prior violations, specific evidence, or mitigating circumstances.

This field is required and must be populated to ensure complete documentation of the moderation action. The context should be factual and objective, focusing on information that helps the recipient understand the full picture of the moderation action. It is not intended for personal commentary but for providing factual background about the violation history or circumstances surrounding the update.

Examples include: "This is the user's third violation within the past month" or "The user has apologized and removed the offending content".

This field is critical for compliance and audit purposes as it provides additional context that may be reviewed during appeals, investigations, or regulatory reviews. It helps distinguish between similar violations based on contextual factors that may influence the appropriate level of response.

IDiscussionBoardWarning.description:
This schema defines the complete representation of a discussion board warning issued to a citizen for policy violations. The warning system tracks violations of community guidelines and moderation actions, serving as a permanent audit record that contributes to citizen reputation scoring and suspension eligibility.

The warning entity contains comprehensive metadata about the violation, including the citizen affected, moderator who issued the warning, severity level, detailed reasons, and associated evidence. It supports a complete moderation workflow including citizen appeals, administrative reviews, and compliance reporting.

Key characteristics:

- Persistent and immutable: Warnings cannot be deleted, only appealed or overruled
- Reputation impact: Each warning contributes to a citizen's trust score calculation
- Escalation capability: Severe warnings can trigger automatic suspension
- Transparent: All warnings include evidence and justification for accountability
- Audit trail: Comprehensive metadata ensures legal compliance
- Multi-stage workflow: Supports appeals, reviews, and resolution processes

The schema includes both system-generated metadata and moderator-provided information, with fields carefully structured to support both operational moderation and legal compliance requirements.

The context field is required and must contain complete documentation of the moderation decision's supporting factors, ensuring sufficient information is available for appeals, audits, and compliance reviews. This field bridges the gap between the concise reason description and the full evidence trail maintained in the system.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAggregatedReport.description:
Aggregated statistics on article reports and statuses across the discussion board platform.

Provides comprehensive analytics for system administrators and moderators by combining data from article reports, status logs, and article records. This schema represents the response format for the GET /discussionBoard/reports/articles/aggregated endpoint, delivering high-level metrics on content health, moderation effectiveness, and reporting trends without exposing individual user identities or article details.

The aggregated report includes total article count, reporting activity metrics, status distribution, and temporal trends, enabling data-driven moderation decisions while preserving privacy through anonymized statistics. The metrics help identify content quality issues, track moderation performance, measure community engagement, and detect potential abuse patterns.

This schema supports the platform's commitment to transparency and community governance by providing actionable insights into content moderation operations without compromising user privacy. The data allows moderation teams to prioritize interventions, identify emerging trends, and evaluate the effectiveness of community guidelines.

The statistics are calculated from JOIN operations between the discussion_board_article_reports, discussion_board_article_status_logs, and discussion_board_articles tables, ensuring data integrity and accuracy through database constraints including foreign key relationships and unique key validations.

total_articles.description: Total number of articles published across the platform. This count represents all articles regardless of status (published, draft, hidden, or deleted). This metric provides a baseline for content volume and helps contextualize other reporting metrics.

total_reports.description: Total number of reports submitted by users against articles. This metric reflects overall community moderation engagement and identifies content that has attracted user concern. A rising total report count may indicate increasing community participation in moderation or growing platform issues.

average_reports_per_article.description: Average number of reports received per article. Calculated as total_reports / total_articles. Values above 1.0 indicate articles frequently attracting reports, potentially signaling quality or moderation issues, indicating subjects that may require increased moderator attention or community guidelines clarification.

published_articles_count.description: Number of articles currently in 'published' status. These are live articles visible to all users and represent the platform's active content pool. This metric provides insight into the scale of content available to the community and helps assess the ratio of active content to moderated content.

draft_articles_count.description: Number of articles in 'draft' status. These are articles created by citizens but not yet published, often works in progress or under review. This metric indicates the level of content creation activity and potential backlog in the publication workflow.

hidden_articles_count.description: Number of articles in 'hidden' status. These articles have been removed from public view by moderators but remain in the system for audit purposes. This metric tracks moderation interventions and provides data on content that violates policies but has not been permanently deleted.

deleted_articles_count.description: Number of articles in 'deleted' status. These articles have been permanently removed from the system, typically following moderation decisions. This metric indicates the severity of policy violations and overall content hygiene of the platform.

reported_articles_count.description: Number of unique articles that have received at least one report. This metric identifies articles that have triggered community moderation actions, separate from total report count. It helps distinguish between articles with a single report versus multiple reports, indicating severity distribution.

report_resolution_rate.description: Percentage of reports that have been resolved by moderators. Calculated as resolved_reports / total_reports. High resolution rates indicate effective moderation operations, while low rates suggest staff shortages or systemic issues with report triage and resolution processes.

article_status_change_frequency.description: Average number of status changes per article. Tracks content volatility and moderation activity level. High values may indicate unstable article states, frequent moderation interventions, or policy conflicts, potentially signaling content that is repeatedly flagged and restored.

monthly_report_trend.description: Change in report volume compared to previous month, expressed as a percentage increase (+) or decrease (-). Positive values indicate growing community reporting activity, which may reflect increased community engagement or worsening content quality issues. Negative values indicate reduced reporting, which may signal user disillusionment or improved content quality.

weekly_report_trend.description: Change in report volume compared to previous week, expressed as a percentage increase (+) or decrease (-). Helps identify short-term trends and recent moderation events, such as viral content attracting large numbers of reports or new policy enforcement triggering rapid reporting activity.

top_reported_category_count.description: Number of distinct article categories that have received at least one report. Indicates how widespread reporting activity is across content areas. A high count suggests broad community concerns, while a low count may indicate issues concentrated in specific topics.

top_reported_category_name.description: Name of the category with the highest number of reported articles. Identifies content domains most frequently flagged by users for potential policy violations. This information helps target moderation resources and inform policy updates for specific topic areas.

moderator_active_count.description: Number of moderators who have taken at least one action (dismiss, remove, warn) on articles in the reporting period. Measures moderator workload and engagement level. This metric helps assess whether moderation efforts are distributed across the team or concentrated among a few individuals.

report_age_distribution.description: Distribution of report ages categorized in time intervals. Indicates whether issues are being reported promptly or if reporting is delayed. Short delays may indicate active moderation engagement, while prolonged delays may suggest users are waiting for signs of systemic action before reporting.

report_rejection_reason_distribution.description: Distribution of reasons why reports were rejected by moderators. Helps identify problematic reporting patterns and potential abuse, such as users submitting false reports or misunderstanding community guidelines. High rejection rates indicate user education needs.

reporter_anonymity_rate.description: Percentage of reports submitted anonymously (without user account identification). High anonymity rates may indicate fear of retaliation, lack of platform trust, or concerns about privacy. This metric helps gauge community willingness to participate openly in moderation processes.

moderator_action_timing.description: Metrics tracking the speed of moderator responses to reports. Quick response times indicate efficient moderation operations and encourage user participation, while delays suggest resource constraints or systemic issues that require more attention.

report_accuracy_rate.description: Percentage of reports that resulted in moderator actions (dismiss, remove, warn). This indicates how effectively reports identify actual policy violations. High accuracy rates suggest a well-informed user base and effective community guidelines, while low accuracy indicates potential abuse or vague reporting criteria.

moderation_efficiency_ratio.description: Ratio of moderator actions to total reports. A high ratio indicates that each moderator action addresses multiple reports, suggesting efficient triage and systemic policy enforcement rather than individual review. This metric helps identify opportunities to improve moderation workflow efficiency.

total_unique_reporters.description: Total number of unique users who have submitted reports. Measures community participation in moderation efforts, independent of report volume. A high number relative to total users suggests good community engagement in governance, while a low number indicates participation may be concentrated among a few users.

top_moderator_action_count.description: Highest number of actions taken by any single moderator during the reporting period. Identifies most active moderators and potential burnout indicators. Finding moderators with exceptionally high action counts can reveal top performers or those who may need support and workload balancing.

moderator_action_type_distribution.description: Distribution of moderator action types among all resolved reports. Shows the balance between different moderation tools (dismiss, remove, warn, suspension, ban). Helps assess whether moderation is appropriately calibrated, minimizing overuse or underuse of penalty actions.

report_satisfaction_rate.description: Estimated percentage of reporters who would consider the resolution of their report satisfactory, based on historical response patterns and feedback trends. This estimate combines resolution rates with observed reporting behavior to gauge perceived effectiveness of moderation actions.

total_resolved_reports.description: Total number of reports that have received a final resolution (dismiss, remove, warn, suspension, or ban). This represents completed moderation cases and demonstrates the system's ability to process community feedback effectively.

total_unresolved_reports.description: Total number of reports awaiting final moderator resolution. These are pending actions that require attention and indicate current system capacity limits or backlog levels that may require additional moderator resources.

report_backlog_count.description: Count of reports that have been pending for more than 72 hours. Highlights potential system overload or staffing gaps in moderation operations. A backlog exceeding 24 hours may impact user trust and encourage self-moderation outside official channels.

status_change_ratio.description: Ratio of status changes to total articles. High values may indicate content instability, frequent moderation interventions, or policy conflicts, potentially signaling content that is repeatedly flagged, contested, or restored, which can create perception of inconsistent policy enforcement.

reported_article_ratio.description: Percentage of total articles that have received at least one report. Indicates how widespread reporting activity is across the platform's content. A high ratio suggests broad community surveillance, while a low ratio may indicate underreporting or content that is rarely controversial.

moderator_utilization_rate.description: Percentage of available moderator work capacity being actively utilized. Reflects whether the moderation team is underloaded, optimally utilized, or overloaded. Ideal utilization ranges from 70-85%; below 50% may indicate inefficiency, above 90% indicates risk of burnout and declining quality.

total_moderator_actions.description: Total count of all moderator actions taken (dismiss, remove, warn, suspension, ban) on articles during the reporting period. Measures overall moderator workload and provides context for other moderation metrics such as efficiency ratio and resolution rate.

article_retention_rate.description: Percentage of published articles that remained available at the end of the reporting period. Indicates content stability and the prevalence of deletion or removal actions. High retention rates suggest constructive dialogue, while low rates may indicate an environment where content is frequently attacked.

moderation_response_coverage.description: Percentage of moderation actions taken in response to user reports, as opposed to proactive moderation actions not triggered by reports. Measures system reliance on community reporting for content oversight. High coverage indicates effective community governance, low coverage suggests overreliance on automated moderation or team-initiated actions.

report_type_distribution.description: Distribution of report reason categories (e.g., harassment, spam, misinformation, etc.). Identifies primary policy violation types on the platform. This distribution helps prioritize policy education, guide automated moderation systems, and target specific behavior patterns that require intervention.

overall_platform_health_score.description: Composite score from 0-100 representing overall platform health based on reporting patterns, moderation efficiency, article retention, and user engagement. Higher scores indicate healthier community dynamics with effective moderation and low policy violations. The score is calculated using weighted factors including resolution rate, accuracy rate, retention rate, and utilization rate.

last_updated.description: Timestamp indicating when these aggregated statistics were last recalculated and updated. Ensures users understand the timeliness of the reported data. Updates occur at least hourly for real-time systems or daily for batch-processed systems to maintain data accuracy and user trust.

- "REPORT_SUBMITTED": Triggered when a content report is received

IDiscussionBoardNotificationTriggerReque.description:
Request DTO for triggering a system notification. This schema defines the data needed to initiate a notification based on a specific event type. The triggerType field specifies the nature of the event, while the context field provides additional reference data to customize the notification content. This DTO is used by system services and moderator actions to send notifications according to pre-configured templates and user preferences, ensuring alignment with the discussion board's notification architecture.

The notification system operates on a trigger-based model where specific system events invoke predefined notification templates. This DTO is the central mechanism controlling notification delivery in the platform, interacting with multiple systems including notification_templates, notification_preferences, and notification_records tables. Without the context field, the system cannot determine recipients, personalize content, or properly audit the relationship between notifications and content items.

All notification triggers must include both triggerType and context, even if the context object is empty, because the system requires a structured record of every notification event for compliance and audit purposes. This ensures traceability from system events to user communications, maintaining transparency and accountability in the platform's notification mechanisms.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IUpdatePreferences.description:
Request body for bulk updating notification preferences for multiple users. This schema defines the structure for modifying notification settings for a list of users as part of an administrative bulk operation. The operation applies identical preference settings across multiple users, typically during onboarding, policy changes, or system-wide configuration updates.

Each field maps directly to the notification preference configuration in the discussion_board_users table's relationship with notification preferences. The user_id references a citizen account which must exist, and preference fields determine what types of notifications the user receives.

The preference fields follow the notification system configuration and align with the discussion_board_notification_preferences table schema, which is managed through the discussion_board_users entity's one-to-one relationship. This design ensures data integrity by preventing direct access to the subsidiary notification_preferences table.

When this schema is used in the PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/notifications/preferences/bulk operation, the server validates that each user_id corresponds to an existing citizen record and updates or creates notification preference records as needed, with all changes logged for audit purposes.

preferences.description: Set of notification preference flags that will be applied to each user specified in the user_id array. Each boolean property controls a specific notification type. All preference fields must be explicitly set to true or false; the system will not preserve or inherit previous values. This object defines the complete desired state of notification preferences for the target users.

enabled.description:
Global toggle for all notifications. If set to false, suppresses all types of notifications regardless of other preference settings. If true, individual preference settings control notification delivery. This acts as a master switch for the user's entire notification experience.

When false, it effectively disables the user's ability to receive any notifications, similar to an opt-out state. This is useful for users who wish to temporarily disengage from all system communications, such as during extended leave, vacations, or when dealing with notification fatigue.

Default behavior: If not explicitly provided in the request, the system will NOT retain previous values but will instead treat the field as undefined, requiring explicit value assignment.

Note: Even when this is true, individual notification types may still be disabled via their respective flags, allowing granular control of notification delivery.

email_notifications.description:
Enables or disables email delivery of notifications. When true, system will send email messages for all notification types that are enabled and have email as a delivery channel. When false, email notifications are suppressed even if other delivery channels (like push notifications) are enabled.

This preference is independent of other delivery mechanisms. A user may receive push notifications but not email notifications, or vice versa.

Common use cases: This setting is often used by users who prefer mobile notifications over email, or by organizations that want to reduce email traffic.

Note: This does NOT affect system emails (password reset, account verification) which are mandatory system communications and always sent regardless of this preference.

push_notifications.description:
Enables or disables push notifications delivered to the user's mobile devices or browser. When true, notifications are sent as instant alerts to devices where the user has active client sessions. When false, those notifications are queued or suppressed entirely.

Push notifications are prioritized for urgent system alerts, moderator actions, and direct user interactions (e.g., replies to comments you've posted).

This preference is particularly useful for users who wish to reduce device interruptions while still receiving email updates or for those who prefer to check notifications manually through the web interface.

Note: Device registration and push token management are handled separately in the client application; this flag only controls whether the system will attempt to send notifications to already-registered devices.

in_app_notifications.description:
Enables or disables notifications displayed inside the application's user interface. When enabled, users will see visual indicators (banners, counters on the notification icon) within the web or mobile application, allowing them to review notifications at their convenience.

This does NOT send any external communications, but only affects UI elements within the platform. This is often the least intrusive notification channel and is commonly enabled even when email or push notifications are disabled.

Use case: Ideal for users who want to remain informed about platform activity without being interrupted by external alerts. This preference is typically always active unless the user has completely opted out of the platform's notification system.

daily_digest.description:
Enables or disables the daily summary email that compiles all notification activity from the previous day into a single digest message. When true, system sends one aggregated email containing summaries of all notification types at a scheduled time (typically early morning).

This preference is independent of individual notification settings and serves as a low-intensity alternative to real-time notifications. It helps reduce email clutter while keeping users informe about overall platform activity.

When disabled, users receive no daily summary, but can still receive real-time notifications (if enabled) and see in-app notifications.

Note: Daily digests are only sent if at least one notification type is enabled; if all notifications are disabled, no digest is sent regardless of this setting.

weekly_summary.description:
Enables or disables the weekly summary email that compiles notification activity from the past week into a single comprehensive message. This provides an overview of longer-term engagement patterns. When true, a single email is delivered at the start of each week.

This preference is designed for users who prefer a high-level review of platform activity rather than frequent updates. It's particularly useful for users with high-volume interactions who find daily digests too frequent.

Note: Weekly summaries are only sent if the daily_digest option is disabled (to avoid duplication) and at least one notification type is active. The system automatically suppresses weekly summaries if the user has both daily_digest and weekly_summary enabled.

moderation_alerts.description:
Enables or disables notifications related to moderator actions against your content. When true, you will be notified when your posts, comments, or other contributions are: flagged, hidden, deleted, or moderated by platform moderators.

This includes notifications for both automated system actions and manual moderator interventions.

Use case: Critical for active contributors who want to be immediately aware of moderation events on their content, especially if they wish to appeal decisions.

Note: This setting does NOT affect notifications you receive when you perform moderator actions on other users' content. That is handled by a separate system.

comment_replies.description:
Enables or disables notifications when someone replies to your comments. When true, you'll receive a notification every time a new reply is posted in a thread where you've originally commented.

This allows users to follow conversations they've participated in without manually refreshing or monitoring threads. Useful for collaborative discussions or Q&A threads.

Note: Notifications are triggered only for direct replies to your specific comment, not for replies to other users' replies in the same thread (unless you're also participating in that thread).

article_comments.description:
Enables or disables notifications when someone comments on an article you've written or authored. When true, you'll be notified of each new comment on your content, allowing you to engage with readers.

This is especially important for users who create and moderate their own articles. It enables active community management by ensuring authors are promptly informed of reader feedback.

Note: This setting only applies to articles where you are listed as the author; it does not notify you of comments on articles authored by others.

following_activity.description:
Enables or disables notifications about activity from users you're following. When true, you will receive alerts when followed users post new articles, comment on content, or engage with the platform in significant ways.

This preference is designed to keep users apprised of updates from communities or individuals they've chosen to follow. It helps maintain personal networks within the platform.

Note: The system uses a 'follow' relationship system which is separate from the notification preference system. This setting only affects whether notifications are triggered for those relationships.

direct_messages.description:
Enables or disables notification of direct messages from other users. When true, you will be notified when someone sends you a private message through the platform's direct messaging system.

This is important for users who want to stay connected for private conversations and maintain communication channels outside of public discussions.

Note: This setting does NOT affect system-generated messages (like password resets or terms updates) which are always delivered regardless of this preference.

admin_updates.description:
Enables or disables notifications about official platform announcements, policy updates, or maintenance schedules from administrators. When true, you will receive alerts about major updates, scheduled downtime, system upgrades, or changes to community guidelines.

This preference ensures users stay informed about important platform-wide developments and allows them to prepare for changes that may affect their experience.

Note: This setting does NOT affect moderator-specific alerts (see moderation_alerts) or notifications about your own content. It is purely for official administrative communications from the platform management team.

security_alerts.description:
Enables or disables notifications about security-sensitive events related to your account. When true, you'll be notified of: new login locations, password changes, suspicious activity, or potential account compromise attempts.

This preference is critical for account security and should always be enabled for security-conscious users. It provides real-time monitoring of account integrity.

Note: These are mandatory security alerts that pertain specifically to account activity. Even when all other notification types are disabled, security_alerts cannot be turned off by users for compliance and safety reasons. The system enforces this at the backend level, so this flag is effectively ignored in terms of disabling, but is included in the API for consistency and audit purposes.

api_access.description:
Enables or disables notifications related to API access and integration activities. When true, you will be notified when API keys are created, modified, revoked, or when API usage thresholds are approached or exceeded.

This preference is designed for developers and administrators who use or manage programmatic access to the platform's API.

Note: This setting does NOT affect system API notifications (like rate limits being applied) which are always sent regardless. This only affects user-specific notifications about API lifecycle events.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the notification delivery log entry. This primary key corresponds to the id field in the discussion_board_notification_delivery_logs database table and is used to uniquely identify each delivery attempt.

This identifier is automatically generated by the system when a notification delivery attempt is recorded, and is immutable throughout the log entry's lifetime. It enables precise lookup of individual delivery records and is used as the path parameter in the GET /notifications/delivery-logs/{logId} and PUT /notifications/delivery-logs/{logId} operations.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and prevents identifier collisions.

notification_id.description:
Identifier of the notification record that this delivery log entry corresponds to. This foreign key links the delivery attempt to the specific notification message that was sent.

The notification_id references the primary key of the discussion_board_notification_records table, establishing a one-to-many relationship between notifications and their delivery attempts. This allows tracking of all delivery attempts associated with a single notification event, which is essential for understanding delivery reliability and monitoring delivery status changes over time.

This field is automatically populated by the notification service when it creates a delivery log entry as a side effect of attempting to send a notification.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the notification delivery attempt. This field indicates the outcome of the delivery operation.

- 'pending': The delivery attempt has been queued but not yet processed
- 'sent': The system has sent the notification to the delivery channel (email provider, push notification service, etc.)
- 'failed': The delivery attempt encountered an error and did not complete successfully
- 'delivered': The notification was successfully received by the recipient's device or mailbox

This is a critical state field for monitoring notification system reliability and is updated by the system as delivery attempts progress through their lifecycle. The status changes are immutable after they occur, creating an audit trail of the delivery process.

delivery_method.description:
Method used for delivering the notification (email, push notification, SMS). This field specifies which communication channel attempted to deliver the message.

Possible values correspond to the notification delivery technologies integrated into the system: 

- 'email': The notification was sent via email service
- 'push': The notification was delivered via operating system push notification service
- 'sms': The notification was sent via Short Message Service

This field allows for reporting and analysis of delivery performance across different communication channels and helps identify whether delivery failures are specific to one delivery mechanism.

error_message.description:
Detailed error message explaining why the delivery attempt failed. This field contains human-readable diagnostic information when status is 'failed'.

The error message provides context about delivery failures including technical details such as:

- 'Email address invalid'
- 'Push notification service unreachable'
- 'Network timeout during delivery'
- 'Recipient device inactive'
- 'Quota exceeded on delivery service'

This field is populated automatically by the delivery system's error handlers and is invaluable for debugging delivery issues and improving system reliability.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the delivery log entry was created. This indicates when the system first recorded the delivery attempt.

This field is automatically generated by the database when the record is inserted and is immutable. It represents the moment the notification system initiated the delivery attempt and created the tracking record in the database.

This timestamp is crucial for determining the order of delivery attempts and understanding the timeline of notification delivery events.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the delivery log entry was last updated. This indicates when the delivery status or error details were modified.

This field is automatically maintained by the database and is updated every time the delivery log entry is modified, such as when the status changes from 'pending' to 'failed' or when the error message is populated.

This field allows tracking of the evolution of delivery attempts over time and helps identify attempts with multiple status changes.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationDeliveryLog.description:
Notification delivery log entry representing a single attempt to deliver a system notification to a recipient. This schema defines the structure of records maintained in the discussion_board_notification_delivery_logs table.

Each delivery log entry captures essential information about the delivery process, including the notification ID being delivered, the recipient identifier, the delivery status, and detailed metadata about the delivery attempt such as method, timestamps, and error information. These logs serve as an immutable audit trail of the notification delivery system's activities.

The structure follows the database schema for discussion_board_notification_delivery_logs, mapping directly to the table's columns. This schema is used in two key API operations:

1. GET /discussionBoard/notifications/delivery-logs/{logId}: Returns this type for retrieving individual delivery log entries.
2. PUT /discussionBoard/notifications/delivery-logs/{logId}: Uses the IDiscussionBoardNotificationDeliveryLog.IUpdate type for updating delivery log entries, but the response body returns this full schema.

Security considerations: Delivery logs contain sensitive operational data about user notifications, including recipient identifiers and delivery statuses. This data should be protected and accessible only to system administrators and authorized monitoring systems. The schema includes fields that identify the recipient, delivery method, and error details, all of which provide insight into user interaction patterns and should be handled with appropriate access controls.

All timestamp fields use ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z') for consistency across the system. The payload of this schema represents a complete, comprehensive record of a notification delivery attempt, providing professionals with all necessary information to diagnose delivery issues, monitor system reliability, and analyze performance metrics.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationTriggerRespo.description: Confirmation of the notification trigger attempt with a summary of recipients and status. This response provides details on how many recipients were targeted, how many notifications were successfully sent, and any errors encountered during the trigger process. The object reflects results from interactions with notification_records, notification_preferences, and notification_templates tables. All values are derived from system processing and represent the outcome of the trigger operation, not user-provided data.

totalRecipients.description: Total number of recipients that matched the trigger criteria based on notification preferences and user targeting rules.

successfulNotifications.description: Number of notifications that were successfully sent to recipients with active preferences for the event type.

failedNotifications.description: Number of notification attempts that failed due to disabled preferences, invalid recipient data, or template errors.

value.description:
Represents the read status of a notification for a citizen user.

This schema defines the response for the GET /discussionBoard/citizen/notifications/read-status/{readId} operation, indicating whether a specific notification has been marked as read by the authenticated citizen.

The value is a boolean where:
- true indicates the notification has been read by the citizen
- false indicates the notification remains unread

This status is tracked in the discussion_board_notification_read_status table, with the readId parameter corresponding to the unique record identifier.

This field is returned directly as a simple boolean value with no additional properties, as the operation is designed to retrieve only the read status without additional context or metadata.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationReadStatus.description:
Wrapper object for the notification read status boolean value as required by the schema.

The OpenAPI specification mandates that response body schemas must be object types, even when the actual value is a primitive. This wrapper object provides the required structure while preserving the semantic meaning of a simple boolean read status.

This structure allows the API to maintain consistent schema design patterns where all response types are object-based, enabling future extensibility without breaking changes. The 'value' property contains the actual boolean read status, ensuring the API response remains type-safe and stable.

IDiscussionBoardCitizenSuspension.ICreat.description:
Request DTO for creating a new temporary suspension of a citizen account on the discussion board platform. Only moderators can initiate suspensions. This DTO captures the essential parameters needed to temporarily restrict a citizen's access to posting and commenting functions, creating a comprehensive audit trail for moderation actions. The system automatically invalidates the citizen's active session upon suspension. This schema must be used in conjunction with the IDiscussionBoardCitizenSuspension response type to provide full suspension context.

Suspensions are immutable audit records intended to document moderation actions taken against citizens who violate community guidelines. Once created, suspension records cannot be modified and represent a factual account of the action taken. Suspension records are preserved for regulatory compliance and are never deleted, even after the suspension period ends. This design ensures transparency, accountability, and the ability to audit all moderation decisions.

The suspension has a mandatory start date and optional end date. During the suspension period, the citizen cannot interact with the platform, but their previously created content remains visible and unaffected. Suspensions are enforceable system-wide and cannot be circumvented by creating new accounts.

Note: The citizen_id field is provided to identify the target citizen for suspension, while the moderator_id is automatically inferred from the authenticated moderator's JWT token and therefore MUST NOT be included in this request body.

citizen_id.description: Unique identifier of the citizen account that is being suspended. This field identifies which specific citizen will have their posting and commenting privileges temporarily restricted. The system validates this citizen_id against the discussion_board_citizen table to ensure it exists and is active before applying the suspension. This is the only user-identifying field accepted in this request body as all other context, including the moderator's identity, is derived from the authenticated session. This field directly maps to the citizen_id column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

start_date.description: The exact date and time when the suspension should take effect. This timestamp must be in the future or the current time, and it determines when the citizen's access rights are revoked. The system enforces that the start_date cannot be in the past, as suspensions must be planned in advance or take effect immediately. This field is required to ensure precise enforcement of moderation actions and to maintain accurate audit trails. This field directly maps to the start_date column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table. Example: "2026-01-09T18:13:09.202Z".

end_date.description: The exact date and time when the suspension should expire and the citizen's access rights should be automatically restored. This field is optional; if omitted, the suspension will remain in effect indefinitely until manually resumed by a moderator. When provided, the end_date must be equal to or later than the start_date to ensure a valid suspension duration. This allows moderators to set specific time limits for suspensions, balancing enforcement with opportunities for rehabilitation. This field directly maps to the end_date column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table. Example: "2026-01-16T18:13:09.202Z" for a 7-day suspension.

reason.description: A brief, clear explanation of why the citizen is being suspended. This description should reference the specific community guideline violation that triggered the suspension. The character limit of 500 ensures the reason is sufficiently detailed to justify the action while remaining concise enough to be easily reviewed by other moderators and the suspended citizen during any potential appeal process. This field is required to ensure transparency and accountability in moderation decisions. This field directly maps to the reason column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table. Example: "Repeatedly posted inflammatory comments promoting discrimination against minority groups."

duration_hours.description: The total duration of the suspension in hours, for use as an alternative to specifying an exact end_date. This field provides a convenient way to specify suspensions in durations rather than absolute dates. Valid values range from 1 hour to 720 hours (30 days). If end_date is provided, this field will be ignored. This field helps automate suspension durations for common violation types, such as "24 hours" for minor infractions or "72 hours" for repeated violations. This field is mutually exclusive with end_date - administrators may use either, but not both simultaneously. This field directly maps to the duration_days column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table, with conversion applied server-side (hours ÷ 24 = days). Example: 24 for a one-day suspension.

admin_note.description: A private internal note for other moderators that provides additional context about the suspension. This field is visible only to moderator-level users and is not shared with the suspended citizen. It can be used to document special circumstances, prior violation history, mitigation steps, or other internal context that supports the suspension decision. This field supports better collaboration among moderators and improves continuity in complex moderation cases. This field directly maps to the admin_note column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table. Example: "This citizen has received three prior warnings for similar behavior within the last 30 days."

oneOf.description: The severity level of the suspension, which influences system behavior and notification patterns. Valid values are: "light" for minor guideline violations (e.g., inappropriate language), "medium" for repeated minor violations or moderate content issues, and "heavy" for serious violations that require immediate and strict enforcement (e.g., harassment, hate speech). This field helps system administrators and other moderators quickly understand the gravity of the suspension decision and influences how the suspension is treated in reporting and analytics. This field directly maps to the suspension_level column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

appeal_eligible.description: Flag indicating whether the suspended citizen will be allowed to appeal this suspension once it is applied. If true, the citizen will be able to initiate an appeal through the /moderation/appeals endpoint after the suspension has been enacted. If false, the suspension will be immediate and non-appealable, typically reserved for severe violations or cases where appeal rights have been previously revoked. This field is included to support different levels of due process as defined in community governance policies. This field directly maps to the appeal_eligible column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

is_final.description: Flag indicating whether this suspension constitutes a final moderation action (i.e., a hard termination of the citizen's account). If true, this suspension automatically triggers a permanent ban after it expires, and the citizen will not be able to re-register or create a new account. This flag is typically set for the most severe violations and serves as a final warning before complete removal from the platform. When is_final is true, appeal_eligible should be set to false. This field directly maps to the is_final column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

notification_sent.description: Internal flag indicating whether a suspension notification has been sent to the citizen via email or in-app message. The system automatically sets this flag to true after notifications are delivered, but administrators may manually set this to false in rare cases where notification delivery was temporarily interrupted. This field supports system reliability and ensures citizens receive mandatory notifications even in edge cases. This field directly maps to the notification_sent column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

is_silent.description: Flag indicating whether the suspension action should be performed quietly without notifying the citizen. When true, the citizen will be restricted without receiving any explicit notification, message, or alert. This is used in cases of severe security risks (e.g., active bot attacks, coordinated abuse) where public notification could escalate the situation. The reason field should provide sufficient documentation in the audit trail for this silent action. Silent suspensions should be used sparingly and only for critical security incidents. This field directly maps to the is_silent column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

affected_content.description: Specifies which types of content should be affected by the suspension. The options are: "posts" (only prevents new posts), "comments" (only prevents new comments), and "all" (prevents both posts and comments). This allows for granular enforcement, for example, restricting a user from posting new content while still allowing existing discussion responses. The default is "all" if not specified, providing comprehensive access restriction. This provides moderation flexibility depending on the nature of the offense. This field directly maps to the affected_content column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

ip_address.description: The IP address from which the suspension was enacted. This aids in forensic analysis and helps identify potential coordinated abuse patterns. The system may auto-infer this value from the HTTP request, but moderators may provide a value to log a proxy or other context. This field supports identifying abuse clusters and ensures complete audit trails for security investigations. This field directly maps to the ip_address column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

session_id.description: The session ID of the moderator's active session used to enact this suspension. This links the moderation action to a specific authentication context, enhancing audit security and accountability. The system may auto-infer this value from the authenticated user, but providing this field ensures explicit linkage regardless of the authentication implementation. This field directly maps to the session_id column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

notes.description: Additional comprehensive notes about the suspension context, including prior warnings, community impact assessment, moderator consultation, or legal considerations. This field provides an open-ended space for detailed rationale and documentation, supporting more complex moderation scenarios that require thorough justification. This field directly maps to the notes column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table. Example: "This citizen has been warned three times in the past month and has been actively evading restrictions by creating anonymous accounts."

is_active.description: A flag that determines whether the suspension is currently active or inactive. This allows for suspensions to be created in a "draft" state, where the citizen is not yet restricted, but the suspension record exists in the system. This enables moderation teams to prepare suspensions ahead of time and schedule them for future activation. This field directly maps to the is_active column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

escalation_level.description: A numerical escalation level that represents the severity of the violation (0 = minor, 5 = extreme). The value must be between 0 and 5, with 5 being the highest severity. This numerical score is used in automated moderation systems and helps prioritize moderation workload. The level is derived from the reason and suspension_level fields, but can be manually adjusted by senior moderators for complex cases. This field directly maps to the escalation_level column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

review_required.description: Indicates whether this suspension requires mandatory review by a senior moderator or team lead prior to enforcement. If true, the suspension will be placed in a review queue and only activated after approval, serving as a quality control measure for potentially controversial actions. This field helps ensure high-quality moderation and prevents individual moderator overreach. The system must be configured to support review queues for this feature to function. This field directly maps to the review_required column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

system_trigger.description: The automated system that triggered this suspension, if any. This could be a detection bot, spam filter, or policy scanner that identified the violation and recommended the suspension. Use values like "spam_detector" or "hate_speech_classifier" to trace automated moderation decisions. When populated, this field connects automated moderation systems with human review, improving transparency in AI-based moderation workflows. This field directly maps to the system_trigger column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

suspension_code.description: A unique code that identifies the specific suspension reason, aligned with standard violation codes in the moderation system. This code provides structured classification for statistical reporting and automated classification, with values like "ABUSE-003" or "HATE-SPEECH-001". The code is mapped to a standardized reason description for consistency and reporting purposes. This field directly maps to the suspension_code column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

category.description: The content category most associated with the violation that triggered the suspension. This helps categorize suspension statistics by topic (e.g., "politics", "religion", "health"), identifying which topics have the most moderation incidents. This field improves community analytics and helps identify systemic moderation challenges in specific areas of discussion. This field directly maps to the category column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

source_device.description: The device type or platform used by the citizen when the violation occurred (e.g., "ios-17", "android-14", "web-chrome"). This helps identify whether violations are concentrated on specific platforms, potentially indicating application-specific abuse vectors. This information supports platform-specific mitigation strategies and security improvements. This field directly maps to the source_device column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

location.description: The geographic region associated with the violation, based on the citizen's IP address or account registration data. This field helps identify regional patterns in community behavior and can identify localized moderation challenges. Values should be in standard region format (e.g., "Korea", "California", "Northern Europe"). This field aids in localized community management and content policy customization. This field directly maps to the location column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

is_duplicate.description: Flag indicating whether the violation triggering this suspension has been previously encountered from this citizen account. If true, this indicates a repeat offender, which may warrant stricter enforcement. This field is automatically calculated by the system based on historical data, but can be manually overridden in complex cases. This field directly maps to the is_duplicate column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

oneOf.description: The priority level for how urgently this suspension should be processed and executed. Valid values are: "low" (for non-urgent review), "medium" (standard processing), "high" (requires attention), and "critical" (immediate action required). This helps moderators prioritize their workload when managing multiple simultaneous suspensions. This field directly maps to the suspension_priority column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

This field provides a clear view of the suspension's current state. This field directly maps to the suspension_status column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

suspension_status.description: The current lifecycle status of the suspension. Values indicate: "active" (currently restricting access), "revoked" (manually ended early), "expired" (automatically ended by end date), "pending" (waiting for activation), and "draft" (created but not yet applied). This field provides a clear view of the suspension's current state. This field directly maps to the suspension_status column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

reviewer_id.description: The unique ID of the senior moderator who will review this suspension if review_required is true. This field is optional; if omitted, the system will assign the next available senior moderator from the review queue based on workload distribution and expertise. This field allows for targeted review delegation when specific expertise is needed. This field directly maps to the reviewer_id column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

target_content.description: The specific content that triggered the suspension, including a short excerpt or identifier. This helps moderators quickly reference the original violation, especially in cases with multiple potential triggers. Values should be limited to 1000 characters to prevent overly long entries. This field provides context for the moderation decision by linking the action directly to the problematic content. This field directly maps to the target_content column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

reason_code.description: A shortened version of suspension_code, used in reporting and data analytics. This field must be a concise, alphanumeric code representing the violation category and is often linked to standardized violation codes across the system. This field directly maps to the reason_code column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

suspension_threshold.description: The number of prior violations this citizen must have accumulated before this suspension was triggered. This value is automatically calculated by the system based on the citizen_trust_scores and citizen_violations tables. It helps identify repeat offenders and can be overridden if manual review suggests a different context. This field directly maps to the suspension_threshold column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

recurring_pattern.description: A free-text summary of recurring violation patterns by this citizen, such as "daily abusive comments on political posts" or "repeatedly uploads offensive images in the health forum". This field helps identify systematic abuse behavior and supports more permanent solutions than temporary suspensions. This field directly maps to the recurring_pattern column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

oneOf.description: The qualification level of the moderator who is executing this suspension. Values are: "junior" (limited permissions), "regular" (full moderation rights), "senior" (high authority), and "admin" (full system control). This information helps audit the suspension decision quality and ensures appropriate authority levels for different suspension severities. This field directly maps to the moderator_level column in the discussion_board_citizen_suspensions table.

appeal_record_id.description: The unique identifier of any appeal record created in response to this suspension. This is auto-populated and should not be included in the request body.

related_moderation_action_id.description: The unique identifier of the related moderation action log that is linked to this suspension. This field is auto-populated from discussion_board_moderation_actions table and should not be included in request body.

related_audit_event_id.description: The unique identifier linking this suspension to an audit action record. This field is automatically generated by the system and should not be included in this request body.

related_compliance_record_id.description: The unique identifier of the compliance record associated with this suspension. This field links this suspension to formal regulatory records. This field is auto-populated and should not be included in request body.

moderation_team_id.description: The unique identifier of the moderation team that this moderator belongs to, which initiated this suspension. This field aids in accountability and team-based performance tracking. This field is auto-populated and should not be included in request body.

related_notification_id.description: The unique identifier of the notification record sent to the citizen about this suspension. This is auto-populated and should not be included in request body.

related_audit_log_id.description: The unique identifier of a related audit log record. This is auto-populated and should not be included in request body.

related_report_aggregation_id.description: The unique identifier of a related report aggregation record that contributed to this suspension via automated thresholds. This field is auto-populated and should not be included in request body.

related_report_id.description: The unique identifier of the report that initiated this suspension. This links the suspension action to its source report when suspensions are triggered by citizen reports. This field is auto-populated from discussion_board_reports record and should not be included in request body. The system links this to the report_id field in discussion_board_citizen_suspension table.

totalReports.description:
Total number of user reports submitted across all platform channels.

Counts all reports including articles, comments, and other content types.

Reports are filtered to exclude duplicates and resolved conflicts before aggregation.

This metric provides overall platform engagement with moderation systems.

resolvedReports.description:
Number of reported items that have been resolved by moderators.

A report is considered resolved when a moderator has taken action (dismiss, remove, warn, suspend, ban).

The resolution rate (resolvedReports/totalReports) reflects moderator effectiveness and system efficiency.

Includes all resolved reports regardless of the action type taken.

averageResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average time in hours between report submission and moderator action.

Calculated as the mean of resolution times for all resolved reports over the reporting period.

Values exclude reports that are still pending resolution.

Slow resolution times (above 24 hours) indicate potential moderator overload or process bottlenecks.

Time is measured from report creation timestamp to moderator action timestamp.

recurrentViolatorsCount.description:
Number of unique citizens who have submitted reports that resulted in violations being confirmed.

Counts users who have been reported repeatedly and whose content was found to violate platform policies.

Indicates the presence of habitual offenders who may require special monitoring.

Excludes users who submitted reports that were later determined to be false or malicious.

suspenseRate.description:
Percentage of reports that are currently in suspense (pending moderator review).

Calculated as: (pendingReports / totalReports) * 100

Suspense rate reflects current moderator workload and response capacity.

A high suspense rate (above 20%) indicates that the moderation queue is growing faster than it can be processed.

Target: maintain suspense rate below 10% for optimal platform management.

falseReportRate.description:
Percentage of reports that were determined to be false or without merit.

Calculated as: (falseReports / totalReports) * 100

A rising false report rate suggests potential abuse of the reporting system or confusion about community guidelines.

Target: maintain false report rate below 5% indicates healthy community self-policing.

High rates may indicate malicious reporting campaigns or a need for better reporting guidance.

resolutionEffectivenessScore.description:
Composite score representing overall moderation effectiveness based on multiple metrics.

Calculated using a weighted formula: (resolvedReports / totalReports) * 40 + (1 - falseReportRate) * 30 + (1 - suspenseRate) * 20 + (recurrentViolatorsCount / totalReports) * 10

Range: 0-100, where higher scores indicate more effective moderation.

Provides a single metric for tracking moderation performance trends over time.

Scores below 60 indicate significant moderation challenges requiring intervention.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAnalytics.description:
Comprehensive moderation analytics dashboard with aggregated metrics and trend indicators.

This schema represents the data returned by the PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/moderation/analytics endpoint.

The model combines information from the discussion_board_report_aggregations and discussion_board_moderation_logs tables to provide a holistic view of platform moderation performance.

This dashboard serves administrators and platform managers, enabling data-driven decisions about moderator scheduling, policy updates, and community management strategies.

All data is aggregated and anonymized to protect individual user identities while providing actionable insights into platform health.

Key components include:
- Overall reporting volume and resolution rates
- Channel-specific report distributions
- Moderator activity patterns and performance metrics
- Historical trends for forecasting and planning
- Composite effectiveness scores for performance tracking

The data is updated every 60 minutes and includes historical trends dating back 90 days to support comprehensive analysis.

emailNotification.description:
Whether email notification preferences for users were enabled or disabled.

This boolean value indicates the new state for email notification settings that were applied to all users in the batch.

True means users will receive email notifications (if enabled in their user profile), false means email notifications are disabled.

This setting corresponds to the email_notifications_enabled column in the discussion_board_notification_preferences table.

pushNotification.description:
Whether push notification preferences for users were enabled or disabled.

This boolean value indicates the new state for push notification settings that were applied to all users in the batch.

True means users will receive push notifications on supported devices (if enabled in their user profile), false means push notifications are disabled.

This setting corresponds to the push_notifications_enabled column in the discussion_board_notification_preferences table.

inAppNotification.description:
Whether in-application notification preferences for users were enabled or disabled.

This boolean value indicates the new state for in-app notification settings that were applied to all users in the batch.

True means users will see notifications within the discussion board interface (if enabled in their user profile), false means in-app notifications are disabled.

This setting corresponds to the in_app_notifications_enabled column in the discussion_board_notification_preferences table.

oneOf.description:

This value determines how often summary email digests are sent to users who have digest notifications enabled.

- "daily": Daily summaries sent each morning
- "weekly": Weekly summaries sent on a configured day
- "never": Digest email notifications are disabled

This setting corresponds to the digest_frequency column in the discussion_board_notification_preferences table.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IUpdateSummary.description:
The notification preference settings that were applied across all users in the batch operation.

This object contains the exact preference values that were set during the bulk update, enabling backward compatibility and audit trails to understand what changes were made.

Each property corresponds directly to a column in the discussion_board_notification_preferences table:
- emailNotification → email_notifications_enabled
- pushNotification → push_notifications_enabled
- inAppNotification → in_app_notifications_enabled
- digestFrequency → digest_frequency

This structure ensures that the effect of the bulk update can be precisely reconstructed from the response

IDiscussionBoardReportAggregation.IModer.description: Count of different types of moderation actions taken during the aggregation period. This provides insight into the types of interventions used by moderators (e.g., dismissal, removal, warning) and helps evaluate moderation strategy effectiveness. Derived from the discussion_board_moderation_actions table which records each moderator decision as an immutable audit trail.

dismissals.description: Count of moderation actions where reported content was dismissed without further action, indicating the report was deemed invalid or insufficiently supported.

removals.description: Count of moderation actions where reported content was permanently removed from the platform due to policy violations.

warnings.description: Count of moderation actions where users received formal warnings for policy violations, typically as a first-time or minor offense response.

suspensions.description: Count of moderation actions resulting in temporary account suspensions for users who committed repeated or severe violations.

bans.description: Count of moderation actions resulting in permanent account bans for users who committed extreme violations or repeated offenses after suspensions.

content_restorations.description: Count of moderation actions where previously removed content was restored, typically following successful appeals or review errors.

IDiscussionBoardCommentMetricsByDay.description:
Distribution of comments by day of the week.

Shows patterns of user activity across different days, which helps optimize content timing and moderation scheduling.

This pattern reveals when the community is most active, helping administrators schedule moderator shifts, deploy promotional content, and plan system maintenance during low-traffic periods. A consistent weekly cycle indicates established user habits, while anomalies may signal special events or policy changes.
