IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board comment, optimized for list views and aggregated data display. Contains essential information for rendering comment listings while excluding large text content and detailed metadata that would impact performance.

This schema is designed for use in paginated comment lists (IPageIDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary) where performance and data volume are critical. The summary excludes the full comment content to minimize payload size, while preserving metadata that enables user engagement and content moderation.

Only properties that are essential for display, sorting, filtering, and moderation decisions are included. This follows the summarized object pattern where the full detail (IDiscussionBoardComment) is available via separate endpoint when needed.

Used in operations:
- GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments
- GET /discussionBoard/citizen/comments
- GET /discussionBoard/search/comments

Note: The author information is presented as a reference object to maintain context without requiring additional API calls to retrieve citizen details.

id.description: Unique identifier for this comment. Corresponds to the id field in the discussion_board_comments database table.

content.description: Current content of the comment limited to 100 characters to prevent excessive data in list views. The full content is available through a different API endpoint (GET /comments/{id}). This is a truncated version for display in comment lists and feeds.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was created. Follows ISO 8601 format and corresponds to the created_at field in the discussion_board_comments table. Used for sorting comments chronologically in feeds.

upvote_count.description: Number of upvotes received by this comment. Derived from discussion_board_comment_votes table where vote_value = 1. Used to identify high-quality or popular comments.

downvote_count.description: Number of downvotes received by this comment. Derived from discussion_board_comment_votes table where vote_value = -1. Used to identify low-quality, spam, or inappropriate comments.

reply_count.description: Number of direct replies to this comment. Calculated from discussion_board_comment_replies table. First-level replies only, not recursive. Used to identify active discussion threads.

has_replies.description: Indicator flag showing whether this comment has any replies. True if reply_count > 0, false otherwise. Used in UI to show reply indicators without requiring a count fetch operation.

author.description: Summary information about the citizen who authored this comment. References the IDiscussionBoardCitizen.ISummary type to provide context about the commenter without including their full profile data. Contains essential display information like name and avatar_url. The full citizen profile is available through separate API endpoint (GET /citizen/{id}).

article_id.description: Unique identifier of the article this comment is associated with. Corresponds to the article_id field in the discussion_board_comments table and links to the discussion_board_articles table. Used for context and to ensure comments are filtered by article visibility status.

is_flagged.description: Indicates whether the comment has been reported by users. True if at least one report exists in discussion_board_comment_reports table. Used by moderators to prioritize reviews. Note: Flagged comments may still be visible to users unless they have been moderated.

oneOf.description: The current user's vote status on this comment, if authenticated. Only populated when the request is made by an authenticated citizen. Values: 'up' if user upvoted, 'down' if user downvoted, 'none' if no vote or anonymous user. Used to render user's voting state in UI.

The current user's vote status on this comment, if authenticated. Only populated when the request is made by an authenticated citizen. Values: 'up' if user upvoted, 'down' if user downvoted, 'none' if no vote or anonymous user. Used to render user's voting state in UI.

The current user's vote status on this comment, if authenticated. Only populated when the request is made by an authenticated citizen. Values: 'up' if user upvoted, 'down' if user downvoted, 'none' if no vote or anonymous user. Used to render user's voting state in UI.

is_my_vote.description: The current user's vote status on this comment, if authenticated. Only populated when the request is made by an authenticated citizen. Values: 'up' if user upvoted, 'down' if user downvoted, 'none' if no vote or anonymous user. Used to render user's voting state in UI.

report_summary.description: Summary of report statistics associated with this comment. Provides an aggregated view of reports without exposing individual report details, maintaining user privacy while allowing moderators to understand community feedback. This object contains total report count and most common reason types.

moderation_actions.description: Summary of the most recent moderation action taken on this comment. Provides transparency to users about why a comment might be hidden, giving context to moderation decisions. This points to the latest action recorded in discussion_board_comment_mod_actions table.

reactions.description: Summary of additional engagement metrics beyond basic upvotes/downvotes. These represent alternative user engagement mechanisms such as emoji reactions. Serves as an extended metric for content popularity and community sentiment.

IDiscussionBoardUser.INotificationPrefer.description:
Request body for bulk updating notification preferences for multiple users. This schema defines the structure for modifying notification settings for a list of users as part of an administrative bulk operation. The operation applies identical preference settings across multiple users, typically during onboarding, policy changes, or system-wide configuration updates.

Each field maps directly to the notification preference configuration in the discussion_board_users table's relationship with notification preferences. The user_id references a citizen account which must exist, and preference fields determine what types of notifications the user receives.

The preference fields follow the notification system configuration and align with the discussion_board_notification_preferences table schema, which is managed through the discussion_board_users entity's one-to-one relationship. This design ensures data integrity by preventing direct access to the subsidiary notification_preferences table.

When this schema is used in the PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/notifications/preferences/bulk operation, the server validates that each user_id corresponds to an existing citizen record and updates or creates notification preference records as needed, with all changes logged for audit purposes.

enabled.description:
Global toggle for all notifications. If set to false, suppresses all types of notifications regardless of other preference settings. If true, individual preference settings control notification delivery. This acts as a master switch for the user's entire notification experience.

When false, it effectively disables the user's ability to receive any notifications, similar to an opt-out state. This is useful for users who wish to temporarily disengage from all system communications, such as during extended leave, vacations, or when dealing with notification fatigue.

Default behavior: If not explicitly provided in the request, the system will NOT retain previous values but will instead treat the field as undefined, requiring explicit value assignment.

Note: Even when this is true, individual notification types may still be disabled via their respective flags, allowing granular control of notification delivery.

email_notifications.description:
Enables or disables email delivery of notifications. When true, system will send email messages for all notification types that are enabled and have email as a delivery channel. When false, email notifications are suppressed even if other delivery channels (like push notifications) are enabled.

This preference is independent of other delivery mechanisms. A user may receive push notifications but not email notifications, or vice versa.

Common use cases: This setting is often used by users who prefer mobile notifications over email, or by organizations that want to reduce email traffic.

Note: This does NOT affect system emails (password reset, account verification) which are mandatory system communications and always sent regardless of this preference.

push_notifications.description:
Enables or disables push notifications delivered to the user's mobile devices or browser. When true, notifications are sent as instant alerts to devices where the user has active client sessions. When false, those notifications are queued or suppressed entirely.

Push notifications are prioritized for urgent system alerts, moderator actions, and direct user interactions (e.g., replies to comments you've posted).

This preference is particularly useful for users who wish to reduce device interruptions while still receiving email updates or for those who prefer to check notifications manually through the web interface.

Note: Device registration and push token management are handled separately in the client application; this flag only controls whether the system will attempt to send notifications to already-registered devices.

in_app_notifications.description:
Enables or disables notifications displayed inside the application's user interface. When enabled, users will see visual indicators (banners, counters on the notification icon) within the web or mobile application, allowing them to review notifications at their convenience.

This does NOT send any external communications, but only affects UI elements within the platform. This is often the least intrusive notification channel and is commonly enabled even when email or push notifications are disabled.

Use case: Ideal for users who want to remain informed about platform activity without being interrupted by external alerts. This preference is typically always active unless the user has completely opted out of the platform's notification system.

daily_digest.description:
Enables or disables the daily summary email that compiles all notification activity from the previous day into a single digest message. When true, system sends one aggregated email containing summaries of all notification types at a scheduled time (typically early morning).

This preference is designed for users who prefer a low-intensity review of platform activity rather than frequent updates. It helps reduce email clutter while keeping users informe about overall platform activity.

When disabled, users receive no daily summary, but can still receive real-time notifications (if enabled) and see in-app notifications.

Note: Daily digests are only sent if at least one notification type is enabled; if all notifications are disabled, no digest is sent regardless of this setting.

weekly_summary.description:
Enables or disables the weekly summary email that compiles notification activity from the past week into a single comprehensive message. This provides an overview of longer-term engagement patterns. When true, a single email is delivered at the start of each week.

This preference is designed for users who prefer a high-level review of platform activity rather than frequent updates. It's particularly useful for users with high-volume interactions who find daily digests too frequent.

Note: Weekly summaries are only sent if the daily_digest option is disabled (to avoid duplication) and at least one notification type is active. The system automatically suppresses weekly summaries if the user has both daily_digest and weekly_summary enabled.

moderation_alerts.description:
Enables or disables notifications related to moderator actions against your content. When true, you will be notified when your posts, comments, or other contributions are: flagged, hidden, deleted, or moderated by platform moderators.

This includes notifications for both automated system actions and manual moderator interventions.

Use case: Critical for active contributors who want to be immediately aware of moderation events on their content, especially if they wish to appeal decisions.

Note: This setting does NOT affect notifications you receive when you perform moderator actions on other users' content. That is handled by a separate system.

comment_replies.description:
Enables or disables notifications when someone replies to your comments. When true, you'll receive a notification every time a new reply is posted in a thread where you've originally commented.

This allows users to follow conversations they've participated in without manually refreshing or monitoring threads. Useful for collaborative discussions or Q&A threads.

Note: Notifications are triggered only for direct replies to your specific comment, not for replies to other users' replies in the same thread (unless you're also participating in that thread).

article_comments.description:
Enables or disables notifications when someone comments on an article you've written or authored. When true, you'll be notified of each new comment on your content, allowing you to engage with readers.

This is especially important for users who create and moderate their own articles. It enables active community management by ensuring authors are promptly informed of reader feedback.

Note: This setting only applies to articles where you are listed as the author; it does not notify you of comments on articles authored by others.

following_activity.description:
Enables or disables notifications about activity from users you're following. When true, you will receive alerts when followed users post new articles, comment on content, or engage with the platform in significant ways.

This preference is designed to keep users apprised of updates from communities or individuals they've chosen to follow. It helps maintain personal networks within the platform.

Note: The system uses a 'follow' relationship system which is separate from the notification preference system. This setting only affects whether notifications are triggered for those relationships.

direct_messages.description:
Enables or disables notification of direct messages from other users. When true, you will be notified when someone sends you a private message through the platform's direct messaging system.

This is important for users who want to stay connected for private conversations and maintain communication channels outside of public discussions.

Note: This setting does NOT affect system-generated messages (like password resets or terms updates) which are always delivered regardless of this preference.

admin_updates.description:
Enables or disables notifications about official platform announcements, policy updates, or maintenance schedules from administrators. When true, you will receive alerts about major updates, scheduled downtime, system upgrades, or changes to community guidelines.

This preference ensures users stay informed about important platform-wide developments and allows them to prepare for changes that may affect their experience.

Note: This setting does NOT affect moderator-specific alerts (see moderation_alerts) or notifications about your own content. It is purely for official administrative communications from the platform management team.

security_alerts.description:
Enables or disables notifications about security-sensitive events related to your account. When true, you'll be notified of: new login locations, password changes, suspicious activity, or potential account compromise attempts.

This preference is critical for account security and should always be enabled for security-conscious users. It provides real-time monitoring of account integrity.

Note: These are mandatory security alerts that pertain specifically to account activity. Even when all other notification types are disabled, security_alerts cannot be turned off by users for compliance and safety reasons. The system enforces this at the backend level, so this flag is effectively ignored in terms of disabling, but is included in the API for consistency and audit purposes.

api_access.description:
Enables or disables notifications related to API access and integration activities. When true, you will be notified when API keys are created, modified, revoked, or when API usage thresholds are approached or exceeded.

This preference is designed for developers and administrators who use or manage programmatic access to the platform's API.

Note: This setting does NOT affect system API notifications (like rate limits being applied) which are always sent regardless. This only affects user-specific notifications about API lifecycle events.

- APPEAL: Generated when a user appeals a moderation decision

The record_type directly influences which related entities are linked to this compliance record and determines the visibility and processing workflow for the record.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorWorkloadDistrib.description: This is a placeholder. The actual schema will be submitted immediately after.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAggregatedReportM.description: Distribution of moderator action types among all resolved reports. Shows the balance between different moderation tools (dismiss, remove, warn, suspension, ban). Helps assess whether moderation is appropriately calibrated, minimizing overuse or underuse of penalty actions.

dismiss.description: Number of reports where moderators chose to dismiss the report without taking any action on the content. Indicates reports that were deemed invalid, unfounded, or not violating community guidelines.

remove.description: Number of reports where moderators removed the reported article from public view. Indicates serious policy violations that warranted content removal while preserving the article in system archives for audit purposes.

warn.description: Number of reports where moderators issued a warning to the article's author. Used for minor or first-time violations as a corrective measure to notify users of policy breaches without removing content.

suspension.description: Number of reports where moderators imposed a temporary suspension on the author's account. Indicates repeated or severe violations requiring temporary withdrawal of posting privileges to allow for reflection and rehabilitation.

ban.description: Number of reports where moderators imposed a permanent ban on the author's account. Indicates severe, repeated, or egregious violations that demonstrate an unwillingness to comply with community guidelines.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAggregatedReportR.description: Distribution of report reason categories (e.g., harassment, spam, misinformation, etc.). Identifies primary policy violation types on the platform. This distribution helps prioritize policy education, guide automated moderation systems, and target specific behavior patterns that require intervention.

harassment.description: Number of reports categorized as harassment, including personal attacks, hateful speech, threats, or targeted abuse against individuals or groups.

spam.description: Number of reports categorized as spam, including repetitive, irrelevant, or unsolicited content designed to disrupt discussion or promote unrelated products/services.

misinformation.description: Number of reports categorized as misinformation, including false or misleading content presented as factual information that could mislead readers or damage public understanding.

insults.description: Number of reports categorized as insults, including disrespectful, derogatory, or degrading comments directed at individuals or groups.

offensive_content.description: Number of reports categorized as offensive content, including graphic, vulgar, or sexually explicit material that violates community standards.

impersonation.description: Number of reports categorized as impersonation, where users falsely claim to be other individuals, organizations, or entities to deceive others or gain unfair advantage.

copyright_violation.description: Number of reports categorized as copyright violation, where content is submitted without proper authorization or licensing from the rights holder.

privacy_violation.description: Number of reports categorized as privacy violation, where personal private information is disclosed without consent, including addresses, phone numbers, or sensitive personal data.

other.description: Number of reports categorized as other, for violations that don't fit into the predefined categories but still require moderation attention.

no_reason_given.description: Number of reports submitted without providing any reason or justification, potentially indicating seed reports or abuse of the reporting system.

ICommentReactions.description:
Represents reaction metrics for a discussion board comment in the context of a summarized view. Captures user engagement beyond basic upvotes/downvotes using standardized emoji-type reactions.

This schema defines a dictionary-like structure where each key represents a specific reaction type (e.g., "like", "laugh", "support") and the value represents the count of users who have applied that reaction to the comment.

The reaction types are predefined by the system and should be consistent across all comments. This enables consistent data analysis and UI rendering. Reactions provide users with more nuanced ways to respond to content beyond a simple binary upvote/downvote.

Used in the IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary to provide richer engagement metrics without requiring additional API calls to fetch reaction details.

Follows the pattern of a Record<string, number> where keys are reaction type identifiers and values are integer counts.

like.description: Number of users who gave a 'like' reaction to this comment. This is the most common reaction and represents general approval or appreciation.

laugh.description: Number of users who gave a 'laugh' reaction to this comment. Used to indicate humorous or ironic content that users found amusing.

support.description: Number of users who gave a 'support' reaction to this comment. Indicates agreement or encouragement, often used for comments expressing perspective or advocacy.

surprised.description: Number of users who gave a 'surprised' reaction to this comment. Indicates unexpected, shocking, or noteworthy content that stood out to users.

care.description: Number of users who gave a 'care' reaction to this comment. Serves as an emotional response indicating empathy, concern, or personal connection with the comment's content.

IDiscussionBoardCommentMetricsStatus.description:
Distribution of comment statuses including active and moderated.

Shows the proportion of comments that are active vs. removed or hidden by moderation.

Uses comment status mapping from discussion_board_comments and discussion_board_comment_mod_actions tables.

This ratio is a crucial health indicator for the community: a high percentage of active comments suggests effective self-moderation and high-quality discourse, while a high percentage of moderated comments indicates systemic content issues requiring attention from moderators or policy updates.

Used to balance community freedom with content safety and to calibrate automated moderation systems.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAggregatedReportR.description:
Distribution of report ages categorized in time intervals.

Indicates whether issues are being reported promptly or if reporting is delayed. Short delays may indicate active moderation engagement, while prolonged delays may suggest users are waiting for signs of systemic action before reporting.

This schema captures the time-to-report distribution for article reports, showing the proportion of reports submitted within different time windows after article publication. This data helps identify whether content issues are flagged immediately (suggesting active community monitoring) or chronically (indicating delayed notifications or disengagement).

The age categories correspond to strategic time thresholds that reflect community response patterns:

- Hours 0-1: Immediate reporting reflecting real-time monitoring
- Hours 1-24: Typical daily reporting cycle
- Days 1-7: Short-term reporting within a week
- Days 7-30: Medium-term reporting over weeks
- Days 31-180: Long-term reporting over months
- Days 181+: Historical reporting demonstrating persistent issues

These intervals are calculated based on the timestamp difference between article creation and report submission. The sum of all categories should equal 100% of total reports.

The distribution pattern informs moderation strategy:
- High 0-1 hour reports: Strong community engagement
- High 181+ day reports: Patience with social systems or poor notification
- High 7-30 day reports: Possible notification system failure
- Distribution balance across intervals: Healthy reporting behavior

hours_0_1.description: Number of reports submitted within the first hour after article publication.

hours_1_24.description: Number of reports submitted between 1 hour and 24 hours after article publication.

days_1_7.description: Number of reports submitted between 1 day and 7 days after article publication.

days_7_30.description: Number of reports submitted between 7 days and 30 days after article publication.

days_31_180.description: Number of reports submitted between 31 days and 180 days after article publication.

days_181_plus.description: Number of reports submitted more than 181 days after article publication.

IDiscussionBoardReportAggregation.ITrust.description:
Summary of average trust score changes for users involved in reported content during the aggregation period. Trust scores are calculated based on user behavior and moderation outcomes. This metric shows whether reported users tend to have positive or negative reputation trends. This schema is derived from the discussion_board_citizen_trust_scores and discussion_board_citizen_violations tables, capturing changes in citizen trust scores triggered by moderation actions on reported content.

The trust score is a composite metric that reflects a user's standing in the community based on positive contributions and adherence to community guidelines. Negative changes indicate users whose content is frequently reported and result in moderation penalties, while positive changes reflect users whose behavior improves after warnings or educational interventions. This data is crucial for identifying systemic issues in user behavior and evaluating the effectiveness of moderation strategies.

appealRate.description:
Rate of appeals filed by users against moderator decisions.

Represents the proportion of moderator actions that are appealed by users. Calculated as the number of appeals submitted divided by total moderation actions taken.

A high appeal rate may indicate inconsistent or poorly communicated moderation decisions, while a low rate suggests high moderator consistency and community trust in moderation outcomes.

overturnRate.description:
Percentage of appealed moderation decisions that were subsequently overturned.

Represents the rate at which appeals result in moderator decisions being reversed. Calculated as overturned decisions divided by total appeals.

A higher overturn rate may indicate moderation decisions that lack clear justification or violate community standards, while a low rate indicates consistent application of rules.

reviewQualityScore.description:
Composite score evaluating the quality and consistency of moderator actions.

Calculated from aggregated feedback points including appeal outcomes, user satisfaction ratings, timing effectiveness, and adherence to documentation. Higher scores indicate more reliable and trustworthy moderation.

This metric combines multiple indicators into a single normalized score for easy monitoring of moderator performance over time.

userSatisfactionRating.description:
Average user satisfaction rating for moderator interventions.

Collected through post-moderation feedback surveys where users rate their experience with moderator decisions. Ratings are on a 1-5 scale.

This direct feedback from the community provides insight into perceived fairness, transparency, and responsiveness of moderator actions.

moderatorConsistencyIndex.description:
Statistical measure of how consistently moderators apply rules across different content types and users.

Calculated by analyzing variance in decision outcomes for similar content items across different moderators. Higher values indicate greater consistency in rule application.

This metric helps identify individual moderators who may be applying rules inconsistently and need additional training.

initialResponseTimeAvg.description:
Average time in hours from report submission to initial moderator review.

Measures latency between when a report is filed and when a moderator first acts on it (marks as reviewed).

This metric assesses responsiveness and helps identify bottlenecks in the moderation workflow.

finalResolutionTimeAvg.description:
Average time in hours from report submission to final resolution.

Measures total time from report submission to final moderator decision (approve, remove, warn).

This metric reflects overall efficiency of the moderation process and highlights potential delays in case management.

escalationRate.description:
Percentage of moderation decisions that are escalated to senior moderators for review.

Represents the proportion of cases deemed complex or contentious by initial moderators, requiring higher-level review.

A high escalation rate may indicate gaps in junior moderator training or complex policy interpretation issues.

complianceAuditScore.description:
Score reflecting adherence to legal and regulatory compliance standards in moderation practices.

Constructed from automated checks of moderation actions against documented policies, retention schedules, and legal requirements.

Higher scores indicate strong compliance posture and reduced legal risk for the platform.

enforcementEquityIndex.description:
Metric assessing whether moderation actions are applied equitably across different user groups.

Calculated by comparing action rates across demographic segments to ensure no group is disproportionately targeted or protected.

This ensures fair application of moderation rules and helps prevent discrimination in platform governance.

IDiscussionBoardModerationEffectivenessM.description:
Metrics tracking the quality and consistency of moderation actions.

Tracks appeal rates, overturn rates, and feedback from users regarding moderator decisions to evaluate fairness and consistency of moderation practices.

IDiscussionBoardCommentModAction.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a moderation action taken on a discussion board comment. Contains essential metadata about moderation decisions without exposing sensitive auditor details. Used in comment summaries to provide transparency about why a comment was modified, hidden, or removed.

This schema follows the summary pattern where detailed action logs are available via separate endpoint, but this summary provides immediate context to users and moderation teams. The structure is designed to be lightweight for inclusion in comment summaries while preserving necessary audit trail information.

Used in:
- IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.moderation_actions (where referenced)
- Moderation dashboards and comment audit trails

Note: This summary omits sensitive personal information about moderators to protect privacy, while still providing actionable context about the moderation decision.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation action record. This UUIDv4 value is the primary key in the discussion_board_comment_mod_actions database table and is used to reference this action across related systems.

- 'delete': Permanently removes comment from the system

- 'unlock': Allows replies again to this comment
- 'pin': Pins comment to top of thread

reason.description:
Brief reason or justification for the moderation action as provided by the moderator. Limited to 500 characters to ensure consistency and prevent abuse. This field is populated when moderators provide reasoning for their decisions, enabling transparency and accountability.

The reason field follows a moderation policy framework with standardized categories, such as:
- "Spam or advertising"
- "Harassment or bullying"
- "Hate speech or discrimination"
- "Violation of community guidelines"
- "False information"
- "Abusive or threatening"
- "Off-topic"

This is not free-form text but follows predefined categories from moderation policy documentation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was performed. Follows ISO 8601 format and corresponds to the created_at field in the discussion_board_comment_mod_actions table. Used for chronological ordering of moderation events and calculating time-to-moderate metrics.

moderator.description:
Summary information about the moderator who performed this action. References the IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary type to provide context about the moderator without exposing their full profile information. Contains essential display information like username or identification identifier, maintaining privacy while establishing accountability.

This reference ensures users can understand who made the decision without compromising the moderator's personal information, following the principle of minimal disclosure.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the moderation action in its lifecycle. Valid values:
- 'pending': Action is queued for review or automatic processing
- 'completed': Action has been successfully executed
- 'reversed': Action was undone by another moderator or automated system

This status indicates whether the action has been fully implemented (completed) or if it is still pending execution or has been reversed by subsequent actions.

IComplianceRecordStatus.description:
Current status of the compliance record in its lifecycle.

Determines the stage of processing:
- PENDING_REVIEW: New record awaiting moderator investigation
- RESOLVED: Moderation action completed and decision final
- APPEAL_PENDED: User has appealed the decision and it's under review
- APPEAL_REJECTED: Appeal was reviewed but the original decision was upheld
- APPEAL_GRANTED: Appeal was successful and the original decision was overturned

The status determines the record's visibility and accessibility, with only RESOLVED and APPEAL_REJECTED records being considered final.

Status transitions are governed by the platform's moderation policy workflow.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLogDetails.description:
Description about the type.

CRITICAL: This description MUST be extensively detailed and MUST
reference and align with the description comments from the
corresponding database schema tables and columns.

The description MUST be organized into MULTIPLE PARAGRAPHS (separated
by line breaks) based on different aspects of the type:

- The purpose and business meaning of the type
- Relationships to other entities in the system
- Validation rules, constraints, and edge cases
- Usage context and examples when helpful

This structured approach improves readability and helps readers better
understand the type's various characteristics and use cases. The
description should be so comprehensive that anyone reading it can fully
understand the type without needing to reference other documentation.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

IDiscussionBoardReportAggregation.IRepor.description: Breakdown of reported content types by category. This provides insight into which types of content are most frequently reported and require moderation attention. Helps identify trending issues and content category vulnerabilities. This object maps content category names to their respective report counts, derived from the discussion_board_report_aggregations table.

articles.description: Number of reports involving articles in the discussion board system. This reflects the frequency of content violations in published posts, including issues related to offensive language, misinformation, harassment, or copyright infringement.

comments.description: Number of reports involving comments on articles or other comments. This metric tracks user-to-user interactions that violate community guidelines, such as abusive language, spam, personal attacks, or targeted harassment.

files.description: Number of reports involving file attachments associated with articles or comments. This includes reports on documents, images, or other file types that violate community standards or contain malicious content.

images.description: Number of reports involving image attachments linked to articles or comments. This tracks visual content violations including nudity, violence, hate symbols, or copyright-infringing material.

reputation.description: Number of reports specifically targeting user reputation or trust score manipulation. This includes reports on inauthentic behavior, fake accounts, bot activity, or coordinated manipulation of trust metrics.

system.description: Number of system-generated reports or automated moderation triggers. This category covers algorithmic detection of policy violations, automated spam identification, and system-initiated moderation flags that don't originate from user reports.

oneOf.description:
The standard for measuring notification success. The value of this field should be "failure" if the notification fails to deliver, "success" if the notification succeeds, and it should not be null or undefined. This field is used to determine the status of each notification attempt.

The values must be either "failure" or "success" and must be lowercase.

Examples:
- "success"
- "failure"

This field is essential for aggregate statistics like delivery success rate.

Any other values or null/undefined will be rejected by the system.

article_id.description:
Unique identifier of the article that failed to update.

This UUID corresponds to a specific article in the discussion_board_articles table that could not be processed during the bulk status update operation. This allows clients to trace exactly which article encountered validation or processing errors.

The article_id is included in the error response to provide direct context for troubleshooting. It matches the article_id provided in the request body, enabling clients to correlate failure reports with their original input.

Usage Context: Critical for moderation workflows where hundreds or thousands of articles are processed in a single batch. Without this field, clients would be unable to identify which specific article failed.

Format: Must be a valid UUID string (as defined in RFC 4122). The system validates that this ID corresponds to an existing article in the database before attempting processing.

code.description:
Machine-readable error code indicating the specific validation failure.

This standardized code allows automated systems to programmatically handle errors without relying on human-readable messages that may change. Each code corresponds to a specific business validation rule that was violated.

Known values:
- "ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND": The article_id does not correspond to any existing article in the database
- "INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION": The requested target_status is not permitted from the article's current status
- "DUPLICATE_STATUS": The requested status is identical to the article's current status
- "NOT_MODERATOR": The actor lacks sufficient privileges to perform this status update
- "ARTICLE_ARCHIVED": The article is already archived and cannot be modified

Business Rule: A successful status update cannot leave the article in a status that already exists. This code helps identify redundant operations. This code may also identify attempts to delete or modify archived, deleted, or highly restricted content.

Security: This code is logged server-side and exposed to clients only for debugging and operational transparency. It does not reveal system architecture details or internal system state.

Implementation: This code is directly mapped from validation rules in the moderation service layer.

message.description:
Human-readable description of the error condition.

This field provides a clear explanation of why the status update failed for the specific article. It should be understandable to frontend developers and moderation interface users, not technical system administrators.

Format: Plain text with a maximum length of 255 characters. This message is displayed to users in moderation dashboards and reporting interfaces to assist with troubleshooting.

Purpose: Accompanies the machine-readable code to provide context that helps users understand and take corrective actions. While the code is used by automated systems, this message helps human reviewers and moderators respond appropriately.

Security: This message is sanitized for user display and does not expose internal system details that could be exploited.

IDiscussionBoardArticleStatusUpdate.IErr.description:
Error information for a single article that failed to update during a bulk status update operation.

This schema defines the structure of individual error objects that are returned in the errors array of IDiscussionBoardArticleStatusUpdate.IResponse. Each error object represents one article in the batch that could not be processed due to validation or processing failure.

The failure may occur for several reasons: the article ID may be invalid or nonexistent, the target status may not be a permitted transition from the current status, or the requesting actor may lack sufficient privileges. The response for each failed article includes sufficient information for the client to identify the cause and potentially retry the operation with corrected data.

This error structure follows the industry-standard convention for batch operation responses, distinguishing between overall success (successCount) and specific failures (errors). This pattern enables partial success semantics - if some articles update successfully while others fail, the client still receives a successful response with detailed failure information.

Structure: Consists of three fields:
- article_id: The specific article that failed (UUID)
- code: Machine-readable error type
- message: Human-readable explanation

Use Case: When moderation teams process hundreds of articles for status changes, this error format allows them to quickly identify and address the specific articles that encountered problems without obscuring the successful updates.

System Rules:
- Only returned for articles that failed to update during processing
- Always returned as part of the errors array in the response
- Never included in successful response entries
- Must be provided for every article that fails processing

Relation: This error type is consumed by the IDiscussionBoardArticleStatusUpdate.IResponse schema and is associated with the discussion_board_articles table through article_id.

IDiscussionBoardReportAggregation.IRepor.description:
Breakdown of reports by category for deeper analysis of prevalent violation types. Enables identification of specific policy violations that require targeted moderation efforts or policy refinement. This object represents a mapping of report categories to their respective counts, derived from the discussion_board_report_aggregations table which stores aggregated statistics of user reports across multiple content categories on the platform.

Used in moderator analytics dashboards to visualize which types of content (e.g., hate speech, spam, nudity) are most frequently reported, enabling prioritization of moderation efforts and policy updates. Each key represents a specific report category (e.g., "hate_speech", "spam", "nudity") and each value represents the total count of reports of that category within the aggregation period.

hate_speech.description:
Total count of reports categorized as hate speech or discriminatory content.

This count reflects the volume of reported content containing abusive language, prejudice, or targeted harassment based on protected characteristics such as race, religion, gender, or sexual orientation. A high value in this category indicates potential systemic issues with hate-based content and may trigger enhanced moderation protocols and community education initiatives.

spam.description:
Total count of reports categorized as spam or promotional content.

This count reflects the volume of reported content containing unsolicited advertising, repetitive posting, or automated content designed to manipulate platform engagement. High spam counts indicate potential bot activity or coordinated campaigns and inform the need for improved detection algorithms and user reporting tools.

Note: This count includes both direct spam and deceptive promotional content that violates platform guidelines on commercial posting.

nudity.description:
Total count of reports categorized as nudity or sexually explicit content.

This count reflects the volume of reported content containing partial or full nudity, sexual activity, or sexually suggestive imagery. High values in this category indicate the need for enhanced content filtering and age-restriction enforcement. This category is particularly sensitive and requires careful moderation to protect minors and maintain community standards.

bullying.description:
Total count of reports categorized as bullying or targeted harassment.

This count reflects the volume of reported content containing repeated, aggressive, or intimidating behavior directed at specific users or groups. High values in this category may indicate clusters of toxic behavior or targeted attacks on vulnerable users and inform the need for proactive intervention and user support resources.

fake_news.description:
Total count of reports categorized as misinformation or fake news.

This count reflects the volume of reported content containing demonstrably false or misleading information presented as factual news. High values in this category indicate potential attempts to manipulate public opinion and may trigger fact-checking partnerships and user literacy campaigns.

impersonation.description:
Total count of reports categorized as impersonation or identity fraud.

This count reflects the volume of reported content where users are pretending to be other individuals or entities, including public figures, organizations, or other community members. High values in this category indicate potential security risks and may trigger account verification enhancements and fraud detection protocols.

illegal_content.description:
Total count of reports categorized as illegal or illegal activity-related content.

This count reflects the volume of reported content that violates laws such as threats of violence, incitement to crime, human trafficking, illegal drugs, or child exploitation. This category triggers immediate legal compliance protocols and may be reported to appropriate authorities in accordance with platform policies and jurisdictional requirements.

other.description:
Total count of reports categorized as other or unspecified violations.

This represents reports that do not fit into the predefined categories and may require manual review. A high value in this category may indicate a need for new category definitions or improved user reporting interface to better capture the nature of violations.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAggregatedReportM.description:
Aggregated statistics on article reports and statuses across the discussion board platform.

Provides comprehensive analytics for system administrators and moderators by combining data from article reports, status logs, and article records. This schema represents the response format for the GET /discussionBoard/reports/articles/aggregated endpoint, delivering high-level metrics on content health, moderation effectiveness, and reporting trends without exposing individual user identities or article details.

The aggregated report includes total article count, reporting activity metrics, status distribution, and temporal trends, enabling data-driven moderation decisions while preserving privacy through anonymized statistics. The metrics help identify content quality issues, track moderation performance, measure community engagement, and detect potential abuse patterns.

This schema supports the platform's commitment to transparency and community governance by providing actionable insights into content moderation operations without compromising user privacy. The data allows moderation teams to prioritize interventions, identify emerging trends, and evaluate the effectiveness of community guidelines.

The statistics are calculated from JOIN operations between the discussion_board_article_reports, discussion_board_article_status_logs, and discussion_board_articles tables, ensuring data integrity and accuracy through database constraints including foreign key relationships and unique key validations.

IStatusLogMetadata.description: A metadata container for status log records that may hold additional contextual information as key-value pairs. This object structure allows schema-compatible extension fields while maintaining type safety and immutability through strict schema definition.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAggregatedReportR.description:
Distribution of reasons why reports were rejected by moderators. Helps identify problematic reporting patterns and potential abuse, such as users submitting false reports or misunderstanding community guidelines. High rejection rates indicate user education needs.

This schema provides aggregated statistics on the distribution of reasons for rejecting user reports on discussion board articles. It quantifies the frequency of different rejection categories, including common reasons like 'false_positive', 'incomplete_information', and 'policy_misunderstanding'. Understanding this distribution helps platform administrators identify systemic issues with community reporting, evaluate the clarity of community guidelines, and design targeted user education initiatives to reduce inappropriate reporting behavior.

The values represent the count of reports rejected for each specific reason, allowing moderation teams to prioritize educational efforts, refine reporting interfaces, and adjust moderation policies based on the most frequent rejection patterns. This data is instrumental in improving the quality of community reporting and reducing the moderation team's burden from handling unfounded reports.

The schema uses a flexible key-value structure where each key represents a specific reason category and the value is the integer count of reports rejected for that reason. This allows the system to dynamically accommodate new rejection reasons as they emerge.

IDiscussionBoardActivityLogMetadata.description:
A container for contextual metadata about an activity log entry.

The IDiscussionBoardActivityLogMetadata object provides additional technical and contextual information about system events captured in the audit trail. This metadata is automatically collected by the system and enriches audit records with details about client environment, network conditions, and operational context.

This object serves as a flexible container for properties that vary by activity type, platform version, or request context, enabling comprehensive forensic analysis and system monitoring without requiring schema alterations for new metadata fields.

All properties in this object are optional to maintain flexibility for different activity types and platform components. Properties are consistently named in snake_case for compatibility with database column names in the discussion_board_activity_logs table and ensure ISO 8601 compatibility for all time-based fields.

This structure reflects the principle of least privilege in logging, ensuring sensitive information is only included where necessary for audit or operational purposes. The metadata does not contain personally identifiable information beyond what is required for system integrity and compliance.

The metadata structure is designed to support:
- Security investigations (IP address, user agent, session_id)
- Compliance reporting (time_zone, location, language)
- System diagnostics (error_code, retry_count, server_request_id)
- User behavior analysis (session_duration, device_type, client_id)
- Distributed tracing (correlation_id, transaction_id)

Each property in this schema corresponds directly to a column in the discussion_board_activity_logs database table, ensuring full compatibility between the API and persistence layers. The description of each property matches the field description in the database schema exactly.

This schema is referenced by IDiscussionBoardActivityLog and IDiscussionBoardActivityLog.ICreate, establishing a contract between the audit event representation and its source data.

The metadata structure follows AutoBE's technical standards for schema design and aligns with the company's information security and compliance policies.

IDiscussionBoardReportAggregationScores.description: Comprehensive summary of moderation activity across the discussion board platform, including key aggregated metrics for monitoring system health and moderator workload.

IEventMetadata.description:
Additional event-specific metadata in key-value format. Contains structured details that vary by event type, such as authentication method used, failed login attempts count, or specific permission changes attempted. Structure of this object varies depending on the event type.

This metadata object is used to capture dynamic, event-specific information that cannot be represented by fixed schema fields in the security log entry. Each key in this object represents a contextual attribute of the security event, and the value provides additional detail relevant to that specific event type. This flexible structure allows the system to record rich contextual information without requiring schema changes for new event types.

Examples of metadata fields:
- authentication_method: 'password', 'oauth', 'ldap', 'totp'
- failed_attempts: 3 (for authentication failures)
- permission_changed: 'moderator_access' (for permission changes)
- ip_location: 'United States' (for geo-location context)
- device_type: 'mobile' or 'desktop'

All values are typed according to their actual data type (string, number, boolean) and follow the same validation rules as core schema properties. The metadata object is not required for all events but is included when contextually relevant to enhance forensic analysis capabilities.

IPageIDiscussionBoardArticleComment.ISum.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

IPageIDiscussionBoardArticleCommentReply.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.
